title: Shane Steichen: Jonathan Taylor is on our football team, wants to win this game
summary: At this point, running back Jonathan Taylor is on the Colts.
full_text: At this point, running back Jonathan Taylor is on the Colts. By this time next week, he may not be. But Indianapolis is still planning to play Taylor in Sunday's matchup against the Cowboys, head coach Shane Steichen told reporters in his Wednesday press conference. Why? "Yeah, I think there’s a lot of stuff out there right now," Steichen said, via James Boyd of TheAthletic.com. " He’s on our football team , and he’s excited for this opportunity to go play. He wants to go win this game.” Taylor has expressed a desire to stick with the Colts, while also acknowledging that he’s not necessarily in control of his future at the moment. In eight games this season, Taylor has rushed for 610 yards with eight touchdowns and caught 21 passes for 202 yards. We’ll see if a team makes a deal for Taylor before the deadline on Nov. 10.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Micah Parsons will do individual work in his return to practice Wednesday
summary: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur outlined the plan for defensive end Micah Parsons's return to practice on Wednesday.
full_text: ' Packers head coach Matt LaFleur outlined the plan for defensive end Micah Parsons's return to practice on Wednesday. LaFleur said that Parsons will do individual work as the team opens his 21-day window to return from the physically unable to perform list. Parsons is returning from last season's torn ACL and LaFleur indicated that the plan is designed to ramp him up because he's been cleared for all activities on the medical front. I think he’s been cleared to go full-go in regards to what he’s doing out there," LaFleur said. "How they limit him and his ability — where it’s just individual. But I expect him to go when he’s out there. He’s been cleared for that. We’ll just take it one day at a time and hopefully he’ll be ready to go sooner than later." Reports last weekend said that the Packers are targeting their Week 12 game against the Rams as the date for Parsons to return to game action. That game will be played on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, so it would be a standalone slot for the football world to see Parsons back in the lineup for the first time in nearly a year.
author: Josh Alper

title: The facts contradict Jerry Jones's beliefs regarding coaching pay and wins
summary: The five highest-paid coaches are all proven winners.
full_text: Appearing Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Cowboys owner and G.M. Jerry Jones made a clunky case for the absence of a correlation between coaching pay and wins. When he makes his second weekly visit of the team's flagship station, he should be asked this question: Would you want Andy Reid, Sean Payton, John Harbaugh, Sean McVay, or Kyle Shanahan to be the Cowboys' head coach? They're the five highest-paid coaches in the league . And any team that doesn't have an objectively great coach would absolutely want one of those five. Because they win. In 2026, their combined record is 25-11-1. They have six Super Bowl trophies, and 11 Super Bowl appearances. They're highly compensated because they win. Which makes them worthy of high compensation. It's obvious. And it's insulting to the intelligence of anyone with reasonable cognitive skills (which barely qualifies me to be insulted) for Jerry to insist that there's "zero correlation" between coaching pay and wins. So what's really going on here? At one level, he's being cheap when it comes to a budgetary line item that has no salary cap, or salary floor. At another level, he likely doesn't want to have a true alpha whose W-2 would allow him to take over the team, and to minimize the outsized influence of anyone named Jones. Whatever the case, Jones's strategy to treat a coaching search like an exercise in wildcatting ignores the fact that he can afford to pay for a high-functioning oil well. But he doesn't want to spend the money — and he doesn't want to give the coach the power that comes from being highly paid. Through it all, the Cowboys haven't been to the NFC Championship since 1995. And there's definitely a correlation between Jerry's approach to hiring coaches and the continuation of " this ‘drought’ that people say we’re in ."
author: Mike Florio

title: Jack Campbell: I have full movement in my lower body, and am making progress with movement in my upper body
summary: The Lions released a statement from Campbell on Wednesday providing an update on his condition after he suffered a significant neck injury on Sunday.
full_text: ' Lions linebacker Jack Campbell has issued a statement on Wednesday after suffering a serious neck injury on Sunday, saying that he has full movement in his lower body and is continuing to make progress with movement in his upper body. This is the first definitive update on Campbell's condition since he was transported to the hospital on Sunday. "I’m incredibly encouraged by the progress I’ve made in such a short period of time," Campbell's statement reads, in part. "I have full movement in my lower body, and I’m continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there’s still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I’m taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better." Campbell went on to thank those who have helped take care of him since Sunday. “I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field,” Campbell said. "I know those were difficult moments, and I’m incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I’ll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. “I also can’t say enough about the incredible care I’ve received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They’ve been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I’m truly grateful for everything they’ve done.” Campbell added, “To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I’m proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn’t ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. “One thing I’ve learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That’s exactly how I’m going to approach this challenge. “Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can’t thank everyone enough.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Garrett Wilson is in the concussion protocol
summary: The Jets may be without wide receiver Garrett Wilson in Kansas City this weekend.
full_text: The Jets may be without wide receiver Garrett Wilson in Kansas City this weekend. Head coach Aaron Glenn said in a Wednesday press conference that Wilson is in the concussion protocol. It's not clear when Wilson entered the protocol or began experiencing concussion symptoms as he did not leave last Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders before the final whistle. Glenn called Wilson, who had six catches for 83 yards during the loss, day-to-day and his progress through the protocol will be tracked over the next few days. He has 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns on the season. Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper, Isaiah Williams, Tim Patrick, and Malik McClain are the other wideouts on the 53-man roster for the Jets.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jack Fox wins NFC special teams player of the week
summary: The Lions handed the Vikings their first loss of the season on Sunday.
full_text: '' The Lions handed the Vikings their first loss of the season on Sunday. Detroit was able to win the field position battle largely because of punter Jack Fox. Now he's been named NFC special teams player of the week. Fox averaged 46.5 yards on his four punts, with three being downed inside the 20-yard line. The Vikings’ average starting field position was inside their own 15-yard line, which was the lowest mark of Week 8. This is Fox’s second career player of the week award, which he previously won back in 2024.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Raiders RB Dylan Laube named the AFC special teams player of the week
summary: There were no kickoff returns for touchdowns in the first seven weeks of the 2026 season, but that streak came to an end in the second quarter of the Week 8 game between the Raiders and Jets at MetLife Stadium.
full_text: There were no kickoff returns for touchdowns in the first seven weeks of the 2026 season, but that streak came to an end in the second quarter of the Week 8 game between the Raiders and Jets at MetLife Stadium. After the Jets scored a touchdown to take a 13-7 lead, Raiders running back Dylan Laube fielded the ensuing kickoff and took it all the way to the end zone. Laube's 95-yard return gave the Raiders a lead that they'd fumble before recovering in the second half to earn a 38-33 win. Laube added 49 yards on two other returns later in the game and he was named the AFC special teams player of the week on Wednesday. Laube is the league leader with an average of 34.1 yards per kickoff return heading into Week 9. He'll try to hold onto that lead while facing the 49ers this Sunday.
author: Josh Alper

title: Alex Anzalone earns first NFC defensive player of the week award
summary: The Buccaneers beat the Falcons without completing a pass on Sunday.
full_text: The Buccaneers beat the Falcons without completing a pass on Sunday. They also beat the Falcons without allowing a point. Linebacker Alex Anzalone was in the middle of that, and now he's been named NFC defensive player of the week. Anzalone had two interceptions plus six tackles, including one for loss, in the Bucs’ 16-0 victory. Both of his picks came in the first quarter. According to the league, he is just the second linebacker since 2000 to have two interceptions in the first quarter of a game. Lofa Tatupu also accomplished the feat in 2007. This is Anzalone’s first career defensive player of the week award. The Buccaneers will be on the road to face the Bears on Sunday night this week.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Jaguars S Rayuan Lane is the AFC defensive player of the week
summary: The Jaguars had to turn to backup safeties due to injuries in last Sunday's game against the Colts and one of them came up with a huge play at the end of the first half.
full_text: The Jaguars had to turn to backup safeties due to injuries in last Sunday's game against the Colts and one of them came up with a huge play at the end of the first half. Rayuan Lane snagged a Daniel Jones pass that tight end Tyler Warren couldn't control and returned it 92 yards for a touchdown that pushed Jacksonville's lead to 28-0 before halftime. The Jaguars went on to win 42-7. Lane ended the day with four tackles, three passes defensed and a quarterback hit. That effort led to him being named the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. Lane was a 2025 sixth-round pick and his play last Sunday could help him earn a continued role in the secondary with Eric Murray out for the season due to an elbow injury.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tyler Allgeier wins first NFC offensive player of the week award
summary: The Cardinals had injury concerns at running back during Sunday's comeback victory over the Cowboys.
full_text: The Cardinals had injury concerns at running back during Sunday's comeback victory over the Cowboys. But the player who stayed healthy was a big part of the win. Now Tyler Allgeier has been named NFC offensive player of the week. Allgeier had 191 yards from scrimmage including 147 yards rushing with two total touchdowns in the 33-30 victory. Both his yards from scrimmage and rushing yards were career-highs. For Week 8, Allgeier led the league in scrimmage yards and was one of just three NFC players to record multiple scrimmage touchdowns. This is Allgeier’s first offensive player of the week award. It’s the first time a Cardinals running back has earned the honor since Adrian Peterson in Week 6 of the 2017 season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Tee Higgins named the AFC offensive player of the week
summary: A pair of Bengals wide receivers had big games in Week 8, but only one of them could be named the AFC offensive player of the week.
full_text: A pair of Bengals wide receivers had big games in Week 8, but only one of them could be named the AFC offensive player of the week. The NFL announced that Tee Higgins was their choice for that award on Wednesday. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns, which gave him the edge over Ja'Marr Chase. Chase finished the 43-36 overtime win with 11 catches for 141 yards and a touchdown. Higgins's first score gave the Bengals a 21-13 lead in the third quarter and his second tied the game with 1:17 left to play in regulation. It is the first time in his career that Higgins has taken weekly honors in the conference.
author: Josh Alper

title: KC Concepcion: Browns are confident, getting Shedeur Sanders ready for Sunday
summary: The Browns haven't officially named Shedeur Sanders this week's starter, but with Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol, all signs are pointing in that direction.
full_text: The Browns haven't officially named Shedeur Sanders this week's starter, but with Deshaun Watson in the concussion protocol , all signs are pointing in that direction. Those signs include Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion saying today that the offense is rallying around Sanders to get him ready to play against the Saints. "It was unfortunate what happened to Deshaun, but we're going to pick up Shedeur's confidence, and get him ready for Sunday," Concepcion said. Sanders lost a quarterback competition with Watson during the preseason, and Watson has played better than expected during the regular season. So Sanders has barely played this year, getting on the field just long enough to throw three passes. But on Sunday, he may start. Last year Sanders started seven games as a rookie and struggled, but this year he'll get to show what kind of progress he's made. The Browns, who have playoff aspirations, have to hope he's ready.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Bryce Young, C.J. Stroud continue fourth seasons without new contracts
summary: In theory, new deals could be done at any time.
full_text: Several players taken in the first round of the 2023 NFL draft have gotten their second contracts. The first two players picked that year still have not. Halfway through their fourth seasons, Panthers quarterback Bryce Young and Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud continue to play under their rookie deals. As to Stroud, a subpar third season complicated negotiations. A decision was made to proceed with his fourth season, without a second deal. A Tuesday article from ESPN took a close look at the respective preseason positions of player and team. The key facts: (1) the Texans offered a contract with a new-money value in excess of $50 million; and (2) Stroud did not ask to be the highest-paid quarterback in the league. (Patrick Mahomes currently leads the way at $63.093 million.) Although the Texans have slumped to 2-5 in 2026, Stroud's play has improved significantly. A new deal — closer to the top of the market — becomes likely after the current season. It remains theoretically possible that the two sides could work something out sooner than that. For the player, there's always an urgency to shift the injury risk to the team. Especially when the player will be assuming 60 minutes of injury risk, 17 times over. As to Young, we've recently caught wind of chatter that the Panthers are "far down the road" toward signing him to a second deal in excess of $50 million per year. Both are under contract through 2027, with their fifth-year options already exercised. For both, the guaranteed salary in 2027 will be $25.904 million. The franchise tag becomes an option for 2028, absent new deals. Most teams prefer to make a final decision before then. Up or out. New contract, or find a new quarterback. Again, both Young and Stroud are eligible for new contracts at any time. Both teams seem to want to keep them around. The only questions at this are when the deals will be one, what the new-money value will be, and (most importantly) how the payments will be structured — especially as to guarantees.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Jordyn Tyson will return to practice on Wednesday
summary: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Saints as they return from their bye week.
full_text: There is some positive news on the injury front for the Saints as they return from their bye week. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson is set to return to practice on Wednesday, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.football. Tyson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury since training camp. He was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return when rosters were reduced to 53 players. The Saints will have 21 days to activate Tyson to the 53-man roster. The No. 8 overall pick of this year’s draft, Tyson should provide a boost to a team that is No. 14 in points scored and No. 23 in total yards. The Saints will return to action at home against the Browns on Sunday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Falcons list James Pearce as a full practice participant
summary: The Falcons held a walkthrough upon arriving in Madrid on Wednesday and they release their estimated practice report for the day after that session came to an end.
full_text: The Falcons held a walkthrough upon arriving in Madrid on Wednesday and they release their estimated practice report for the day after that session came to an end. Linebacker James Pearce took part in the walkthrough and was listed as a full participant as he moves toward making his 2026 debut. Pearce missed the first eight games while serving a Personal Conduct Policy suspension related to a domestic violence incident earlier this year. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was the only player listed as out of practice. The Falcons announced earlier this week that Branch will not play against the Bengals on Sunday. Defensive end Samson Ebukam was also ruled out before being placed on injured reserve on Tuesday. Linebacker Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm), and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) were listed as limited participants. Defensive back Billy Bowman (hamstring), wide receiver Beaux Collins (hip), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle) were listed as full participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nebraska voters say no to mobile sports betting
summary: If you haven't heard, Tuesday was election day.
full_text: If you haven't heard, Tuesday was election day. Multiple candidates with NFL connections lost. In Nebraska, the sports books also lost. Via Erin Bamer of the Nebraska Examiner , voters there rejected online sports betting . The ballot initiative came after multiple efforts by gambling interests to legalize it through the legislative process, which has been successful in many other states. The outcome in Nebraska raises an obvious question. How many states in which their elected representatives embraced sports betting would have rejected it, if the people had the right to vote on it? For those charged with balancing the public budget, tax revenues from legalized sports betting become a siren's song. And it results in plenty of citizens wrecking their own finances by chasing the false promise of easy money. Earlier this year, Warren Buffett called sports betting a " tax on stupidity ." All gambling is, really. The system is designed to take your money, either quickly or slowly. Any wins will be outweighed over time by the losses. If that wasn't the case, the sports books wouldn't be in business. And the states wouldn't embrace the easy money that comes from aligning with the house and indirectly increasing the taxes of those who choose to participate. Because the house always wins. Except in states where the people are given the chance to vote on whether the vampire will be invited onto their phones.
author: Mike Florio

title: Browns sign TE Carsen Ryan to 53-man roster
summary: The Browns have made a Wednesday roster move.
full_text: The Browns have made a Wednesday roster move. Tight end Carsen Ryan has been signed to the 53-man roster from the club’s practice squad. Ryan has appeared in seven games for Cleveland this season, playing 85 special teams snaps and two offensive snaps. He’s recorded one tackle. Additionally, the Browns have signed running back Hassan Haskins to the team’s practice squad. He’s appeared in 44 career games for the Titans and Chargers.
author: Myles Simmons

title: 2026 season could highlight the unfairness of the eight-division structure
summary: It's time to consider ditching the two-conference, eight-division approach.
full_text: From time to time, the NFL's current structure has created unfair results, with the best of four bad teams assigned to a predetermined division earning a playoff berth and the home game that goes along with it. This year, the NFC has two very strong divisions, one so-so division, and one very weak division. Here's the basic reality. With the four NFC division winners getting tickets to the playoff party, the wild-card berths will go to three teams. And, currently, there are three teams in the NFC North and two in the NFC West that are potentially better than whoever will win the NFC East and the NFC South. Between the Vikings, Bears, Lions, Packers, 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams, two will be crowned division winners. That leaves five for the wild-card berths. Ultimately, two of them will be frozen out of the playoffs — even if both of those teams end up with better records than the best teams of the NFC East and NFC South. During last Friday's episode of PFT Live , I threw out an alternative approach that would be far more fair to all teams. Instead of two conferences with a quartet of four-team divisions, why not pivot to four eight-team divisions? NFL East, NFL North, NFL South, NFL West. The easiest configuration would consist of slapping the current East, North, South, and West divisions into one conference each. While some tweaks could be needed to better align things geographically, it would be far more fair to guarantee a playoff spot (and a home game) to the best of eight teams, not the best of four teams. Decisions would have to be made about scheduling. The home-and-home series (a vestige of the days when there were far fewer teams) would need to be retired. Each team would play the seven other teams in its conference, with 10 (or 11, inevitably) other games. The playoffs would consist of the four conference champions (with the best two getting byes) and 10 wild-card teams. And there would be an added benefit — it would be possble to have the best two teams meet in the Super Bowl, without regard to the traditional AFL-NFL/AFC-NFC separation. It would be one league. One playoff tree. Any combination of teams would, in theory, be possible for the Super Bowl. When the dust settles on the semifinal round, the best two teams would remain. That said, it won't be easy to get the owners to give up the current format, which entails in any given year a one-in-four shot at hosting a playoff game. But if the goal is to constantly strive for ways to create more compelling matchups, an eight-team, four-conference approach makes a lot more sense than the current structure. Football is a meritocracy. A configuration of four, eight-team conferences would be far more conducive to that ideal. Will it happen? Probably not. Should it be taken seriously by the league? Absolutely. Maybe this year, when the NFC East and NFC South provide none-of-the-above champions and two very viable teams are sent home after Week 18, will spark a real conversation about meaningful change.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Tyler Huntley to miss the rest of 2026 season
summary: Huntley injured his toe in last Sunday's loss to the Bills.
full_text: Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley's season is reportedly over. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that tests on Huntley's toe showed a turf toe injury that will require him to miss the rest of the team's games. Huntley had already been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Jaguars, which has undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in line to make his first NFL start. With Lamar Jackson dealing with a thumb injury that could also keep him out for the season, Fagnano could have an extended run in the starting job unless the Ravens opt to move in a different direction. Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed are the other in-house options, but both of them just signed with the team this week so it's less than an ideal situation for the Ravens' bid to stay in the AFC playoff race.
author: Josh Alper

title: Browns announce Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol
summary: Watson developed symptoms on Monday night, after first-quarter helmet-to-helmet hit.
full_text: Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders may be getting more than a handful of snaps in Week 9, when his team visits the Saints. The Browns have announced that starting quarterback Deshaun Watson is in the concussion protocol. "During the first quarter of Sunday's game against the Steelers, Deshaun took a helmet-to-helmet hit," the team said in a statement released on Wednesday morning. "The ATC spotter called down to the sideline, and the Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant (UNC) administered a gameday concussion evaluation. Deshaun was cleared by the UNC and returned on the Browns' next offensive series. As part of the protocol, the team's medical staff evaluated him again postgame and Monday morning. Both times he showed no symptoms, passed his evaluations, and was cleared. On Tuesday morning, he reported to the medical staff that he began experiencing concussion symptoms Monday night and was immediately placed in the concussion protocol ." Watson will remain in the concussion protocol until he clears the various steps. Until then, Sanders will presumably be the starter — unless the coaching staff decides to pivot to Dillon Gabriel. The development comes not long after Sanders hired an agent for the first time, presumably in an effort to secure a trade to a new team. For now, he'll get a chance to make the case to become the eventual starter for the Browns. Or to attract interest elsewhere in him once 2027 rolls around. For the 5-3 Browns, it's a significant development. They need to keep pace with the 6-2 Steelers and 5-2 Bengals. Picking up a fourth loss without Watson (who eventually threw for 324 yards in the 27-6 loss at Pittsburgh) will make that harder to accomplish.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills reverse course on "high-maintenance" C.J. Gardner-Johnson
summary: The Bills said they'd be keeping safety C.J.
full_text: The Bills said they'd be keeping safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. And now they're not. Tuesday's surprise move to release the veteran defensive back directly contradicts the comments made publicly by coach Joe Brady, on the same day Gardner-Johnson received a one-game suspension for spitting on an opponent during the Week 6 game against the Raiders. “Look, C.J.'s a member of the Buffalo Bills ,” Brady said on October 19. “We brought him here for a reason, and we know that he knows that he has to play better. He knows he has to be better for this team, and, you know, just like everybody else, right, we’ve got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes.” And now Gardner-Johnson is gone. As one source explained it to PFT, the Bills decided that Gardner-Johnson was simply too "high-maintenance" — and that the talent and production didn't justify the headaches. Plenty of other teams could have told the Bills what would happen. Gardner-Johnson has hopscotched around the league, from the Saints to the Eagles to the Lions to the Eagles (again) to the Texans to the Ravens to the Bears to the Bills. He has been good enough to get more chances, but not good enough to keep him around in light of the issues that he brings with him. The Bills hoped to harness his attitude in order to give the defense a lift. In the end, however, the baggage outweighed the boost. And now Gardner-Johnson becomes a free agent again. Plenty of coaches believe they can be the one to speak to a player's better angels. As to Gardner-Johnson, the demons have won, far too often.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lions put LB Jimmy Rolder on IR, waive DB Bishop Fitzgerald
summary: The Lions announced that linebacker Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury during Sunday's win over the Vikings and they moved him to the injured reserve list.
full_text: '' The Lions announced that linebacker Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury during Sunday's win over the Vikings and they moved him to the injured reserve list. Rolder was injured on the same play that linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a neck injury that has required him to remain hospitalized since Sunday. The fourth-round pick had 11 tackles and a sack in his five appearances during the regular season. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said that the team will sign linebacker K.J. Britt off of the Patriots' practice squad. They have another open roster spot at their disposal as well. They announced that defensive back Bishop Fitzgerald has been waived on Tuesday. Fitzgerald was signed off of the Steelers' practice squad in September, but he never appeared in a game for the Lions.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Macdonald wants Seahawks to "focus on recapturing us"
summary: After Monday night's loss to the Bears, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that his team was beaten in all three phases of the game and he revisited that line of thinking on Tuesday.
full_text: After Monday night's loss to the Bears, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that his team was beaten in all three phases of the game and he revisited that line of thinking on Tuesday. During an appearance on Seattle Sports 710, Macdonald said that there's an "itch to say" what needs to change about the team as they work to move forward from both the loss and the 4-4 start to their Super Bowl title defense. Macdonald then pivoted to suggesting "a deep breath" and a recentering of the things that propelled the Seahawks to success in the past rather than reaching for things to tweak across the board. "If we're going to go out, we want to go out in our way and our style, and that wasn't us, or the best version of us at least," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "So that's why I think it's so tough. We have to focus on recapturing us and making sure that we're us when we turn the tape on. There were too many times throughout that game where that wasn't us in terms of just our style of ball. That's where we need to get better." A home game against the Cardinals will be this week's opportunity to double down on the kind of recentering that Macdonald is talking about and getting that in place in time for the Seahawks to finish strong appears to be the path Macdonald is charting in Seattle.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Jacobs needs to display more (or any) contrition
summary: In May 2026, Packers running back Josh Jacobs crossed a line that should never be crossed.
full_text: ' In May 2026, Packers running back Josh Jacobs crossed a line that should never be crossed. And neither he nor his representatives are acting accordingly in what should be an effort to seek redemption. He pleaded no contest to battery of a woman. He's fighting in court to keep the video secret . He's responding to additional allegations through a strident statement from his lawyers attacking the accusers. The most tone-deaf gesture of all came last Thursday night, when he celebrated a touchdown by pretending to wear, and to be released from, handcuffs. His implausible explanation , which accused Prime Video of not showing enough of the celebration and attacked the media for interpreting the images with their lyin' eyes, was contradicted by the full video of the event . That's not the way to play this. His no-contest plea is equivalent to saying, "I did it." He should be contrite. He should be apologetic. He should be seeking redemption. The Packers continue to stand behind him , primarily because he's the best running back on the roster and they want to win games. Their reported interest in Colts running back Jonathan Taylor strongly suggests that, if the Packers could get Taylor, the support for Jacobs would immediately evaporate. Here's the basic reality. If the Packers were to cut Jacobs, would anyone sign him? The Chiefs took plenty of heat last week for adding kicker Justin Tucker to the practice squad; they may not be inclined to give another second chance to a player whose arrival would compound the negative reaction to Tucker's arrival. The reality, in every sport at every level, is obvious. If the player has enough skill and ability, someone will find a way to justify behavior that shouldn't be tolerated by an industry that relies so heavily on support from the public, both directly through ticket sales and TV ratings and indirectly through taxpayer funding for stadium projects. Still, Jacobs has done himself no favors by adopting a posture of defiance. He did something no man should ever do. He's lucky he's good enough at football to not lose his job over it. If he was at the bottom of the depth chart in Green Bay, he would have been gone a long time ago.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones claims (incorrectly) that there's "no correlation" between coaching pay and winning
summary: Jerry prefers to hire a cheap, unproven coach — and to hope he strikes gold.
full_text: Jerry Jones has said that the size of the check he would write to guarantee another Super Bowl win would be " embarrassing ." Yes, it would be embarrassingly small. Jones, when it comes to the resources he is willing to invest in the team, is cheap. He won't fire coaches who have buyouts. And he won't pay top dollar for new coaches. The owner and G.M. of the Cowboys defended his approach during his latest visit to 105.3 The Fan in Dallas by making the nonsensical claim that there's no connection between coaching pay and winning. "In the NFL, this is after years of looking at all the teams and all the coaches, there is no — there is zero correlation between how much you pay a coach, or how many coaches you have, as to winning," Jones said. "There is no correlation. And that's a random sample of years and all 32 teams involved. So put that in your hopper and smoke it." He's just wrong. Hiring a proven coach, and paying him accordingly, can change everything. We've seen it, time and again. Andy Reid instantly turned the Chiefs into consistent contenders, and three-time Super Bowl winners. Sean Payton has made the Broncos into an annual contender, positioning him to become the first coach to win a Super Bowl for two different teams. Most recently, John Harbaugh has immediately changed everything for the Giants. Harbaugh's success will result in his former rival, Mike Tomlin, fending off teams willing to pay him upwards of $30 million per year to swap out his earpiece and microphone on the NBC sideline set for the Sony headset along the white stripe. Jones prefers to speculate, when it comes to coaches. In lieu of paying for a coach who has proven that he can win, Jones wants to roll the dice on an unproven commodity in the hopes of maximizing the return on his investment. "You can be pretty creative in hiring your coaches," Jones said. "You can be creative sometime when you don't even know you're hiring the coaches. And so I've had some good experience of hiring people who have never been in the NFL. I've had some experience of hiring young coaches, older coaches, and so, of course, you constantly remind me, as you should, of what my record is. And I understand that. But I also know that the next time you throw the pick, if you were the old California gold miner, you may hit the Comstock Lode. And then it is gloryhole." "Creative" is another way of saying "cheap." Buy low, and reap the benefit when the less expensive option yields results. And stick with him until his contract expires, to avoid having to pay two coaches at the same time. It would be different if there truly was no correlation between quality (and cost) of coach and winning. But there ABSOLUTELY is a connection. Still, Jerry prefers to dig through the bargain bin in search of an abandoned Botticelli. His own twist on "if you have to ask you can't afford it" is "if you have to ask I don't want it." It's no surprise. In the early days of the salary cap, members of the media often pointed out that there's no cap on coaching pay. In time, the NFL realized, "Oh shit, there's no cap on coaching pay." That has led to what some believe is an effort to collectively keep coaching pay from growing at the rate that it should. And some in league circles are convinced that Jerry Jones is the ringleader of what is, as a practical matter, an effort to collude. Even if he's not going to pay top-of-market money for a coach, the higher the market goes, the more expensive it gets across the board. The rising tide, in other words, raises all dinghies. And Jerry would much rather spend his money on his aircraft carrier that has been retrofitted into a luxury hotel. That's his prerogative. But Cowboys fans — who fork over their money and who devote their time and attention to watching games on TV and consuming Cowboys content — should understand what's going on. Jerry Jones is pinching pennies when it comes to paying coaches. As a result, he's often getting what he isn't paying for. His mindset is highly relevant to the looming wreckage of the 2026 season. If coach Brian Schottenheimer has guaranteed money left on his contract for 2027, he will not be fired. And if Jones can avoid owing Schottenheimer a buyout, Jones will resist joining the pursuit of Tomlin, who admitted on the most recent edition of Football Night in America that he grew up a fan of the Cowboys. Actually, that could make Jerry think that deep-seated rooting interest will give him a chance at hiring Tomlin on the cheap. Because cheap does as cheap is. And, when it comes to his team (and specifically to his coaches), Jerry Jones is cheap.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jerry Jones wants to see more targets for George Pickens
summary: The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems.
full_text: The 3-5 Cowboys have plenty of problems. During the first of his two weekly radio spots on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, owner and G.M. Jerry Jones mentioned one specific thing that he'd like to see change. Regarding receiver George Pickens, Jones said this, via Jon Machota of The Athletic: "He needs the ball coming his way more ." Through eight games, Pickens has 62 targets. In Week 8 against the Cardinals, Pickens had the ball thrown in his direction only four times. Against the Eagles in Week 7, Pickens had six targets. He has 39 catches for 533 yards and two touchdowns in 2026. That projects to 83 catches for 1,132 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. In 2025, Pickens finished with 93 receptions, 1,429 yards, and nine scores. Hovering over the situation is the decision the Cowboys will have to make after the season. He's making $27.298 million under the franchise tag; they could tag him again next year, at $32.758 million. Which is still nearly $10 million behind the top of the receiver market. There's another option, now that the Cowboys are fading in the race for the NFC East title. They could make Pickens available in trade. Would a contender offer a second-round pick for him? The Chiefs are currently desperate for help at receiver; they're interested (we're told) in Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Colts receiver Josh Downs. If the Chiefs are in on Pickens, other teams in the AFC (like the Bills) should be thinking about it, too. If the Cowboys were to decide to make a move, they could stockpile a pick or two — and save $15.17 million in cash and cap space. For now, who knows? The Cowboys seem to be deluding themselves into thinking they're still contenders. Unless that's just part of the annual effort to keep their fans coughing up cash for tickets and merch. Which continues to work very well, relative to the on-field production. For 31 years, and counting.
author: Mike Florio

title: Peyton Manning, Greg Olsen emerge as the potential Troy Aikman replacement
summary: As the clock continues to tick toward a potential, if not inevitable, breakup between ESPN and Troy Aikman, a replacement will be needed on Monday Night Football if/when Aikman leaves.
full_text: ' As the clock continues to tick toward a potential, if not inevitable, breakup between ESPN and Troy Aikman, a replacement will be needed on Monday Night Football if/when Aikman leaves. Greg Olsen's name previously had emerged as a clear favorite , and for good reason. He's done the job at the highest level, and he has won multiple Emmys for it. But there's already a big name who is in the Disney tent, and who already works on most Monday nights: Peyton Manning. Via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing , Andrew Marchand of The Athletic recently characterized Olsen as the favorite in a Q&A column — but also planted a flag as to the Peyton possibility. Beyond putting someone in the booth who would perhaps instantly become the best analyst of them all, the move would give both ESPN and Manning an exit ramp from the ManningCast , which no longer moves the needle for ESPN2. The question becomes whether Manning wants to do it, and whether ESPN would compensate him at market level. With his long-time rival Tom Brady getting $37.5 million per year from Fox, Manning would want to be close to that. Or maybe to surpass it. That simple fact makes it far more likely that, when the dust settles, it'll be Olsen and not Manning as the Aikman replacement.

title: Bob Heinz, member of undefeated 1972 Dolphins' "No-Name Defense," dies at 79
summary: Bob Heinz, a member of the undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins' "No-Name Defense" and winner of two Super Bowl rings, has died at the age of 79.
full_text: Bob Heinz, a member of the undefeated 1972 Miami Dolphins' "No-Name Defense" and winner of two Super Bowl rings, has died at the age of 79. Heinz was born and raised in Milwaukee but went out West to play his college football at the University of the Pacific. After an excellent college career, he was a second-round pick of the Dolphins in 1969. The Dolphins defense that Heinz joined was known as the No-Name Defense, a term given to them by Cowboys coach Tom Landry, who called them "a bunch of no-names." Some players might have taken offense, but the members of the Dolphins' defense embraced it as a term that showed they were greater as a unit than any of them would have been individually. Heinz was a starting defensive tackle on both the 1972 Dolphins team that remains the only undefeated, untied team in NFL history, and the 1973 Dolphins, who repeated as Super Bowl champions. He missed the entire 1975 season with an injury, but returned in 1976 and 1977. He finished his NFL career with one season in Washington in 1978.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens trade candidates: Three quarterbacks Baltimore should consider amid injury crisis
summary: With Lamar Jackson sidelined and Tyler Huntley out for the year, Baltimore could look to Jacoby Brissett or Anthony Richardson before the trade deadline to keep its 4-4 season alive
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens sit in a dangerous position, as they lost their top two quarterbacks to injury, and their third option is also questionable. On his first passing attempt in the eventual 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills , Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that required surgery, landed him on injured reserve and could end his season. Then, Tyler Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury as well.
That forced undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into the lineup, who completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception vs. Buffalo. However, he's nursing an ankle injury and is considered questionable for the Ravens' Week 9 matchup vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday. That led Baltimore to add Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed to its roster.
While Fagnano will likely join Anthony Brown as the only undrafted rookie quarterbacks to start a game for the Ravens, should the team consider chasing a legitimate starter prior to next Tuesday's trade deadline? While Baltimore does reside in last place in the division with a 4-4 record, the season isn't over yet. Let's examine three quarterback options for the Ravens to consider.
The Arizona Cardinals demoted Jacoby Brissett from starter to third-stringer this week, as Mike LaFleur is moving forward with Gardner Minshew and rookie Carson Beck as his new No. 2. Brissett was benched for Minshew in the third quarter of the Cardinals' Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys , who sparked the offense with three touchdown passes in the fourth quarter to get the game to overtime. The Cardinals won that game in the extra period, leading LaFleur to make the decision he did.
Brissett has not been terrible this season. He's completed 63.3% of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight games. His 75.6 yards per game to Trey McBride entering Week 8 were the most by a QB-TE combo since 1970 (min. 15 games). Brissett isn't going to be raking in Pro Bowl votes, but he's a borderline starter in this league that would be an upgrade over an undrafted rookie or career third-stringer.
This would be the most intriguing swing of the bat for general manager Eric DeCosta, as Anthony Richardson is the option that offers the most upside. The former No. 4 overall pick out of Florida hasn't made a start since 2024, but he's one of the most athletic quarterback prospects we've ever seen. Obviously, it hasn't gone according to plan for him with the Indianapolis Colts . The 24-year-old quarterback is 8-7 as a starter, having completed 50.9% of his passes with 11 touchdowns and 13 interceptions in 18 total games played. Availability and consistency have been major issues for Richardson, but a change of scenery could do wonders for him.
Before you write Richardson off as a complete bust, consider the impact J.J. McCarthy is having early on for the New York Giants . Why couldn't Richardson thrive after his long-awaited trade? Plus, Richardson is a dual-threat athlete who could pair well with Derrick Henry . He averaged 40 rushing yards per game in his first two seasons, and scored 10 touchdowns on the ground as well. Give me the read option every play.
Tyson Bagent of the Chicago Bears has been floated as a trade candidate for the Ravens given his familiarity with new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Bagent has truly been one of the most fascinating stories we've seen in the NFL over the past couple of seasons. Undrafted in 2023 out of Shepherd University -- a Division II school in Shepherdstown, West Virginia, Bagent did enough with Chicago in his first preseason to earn a spot on the final 53-man roster. As a rookie, he was called upon to make four starts, and even defeated No. 1 overall pick Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers in prime time.
Bagent signed a two-year, $10 million extension in 2025, but has struggled this season. He threw for 268 yards and one interception in the Week 4, 23-12 win against the New York Jets , then threw for just 87 yards and two interceptions in the 31-7 blowout loss suffered at the hands of the Green Bay Packers the following week. Bagent's struggles look even worse considering that 38-year-old Case Keenum threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns in a primetime upset of the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 3. If Caleb Williams had to miss another start at some point, you have to wonder who Ben Johnson would start at quarterback this time around.
One question to consider is what would the Bears want for Bagent? If Ryan Poles wants a fourth-round pick for him,it should be "thanks but no thanks."
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Jadeveon Clowney mock trades: Cowboys reunion headlines four deals Texans can make before NFL trade deadline
summary: Clowney's name has surfaced in trade discussions this week
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline less than a week away, the hot stove is officially boiling. More and more names are being bandied about with each passing day. Some of them are big and some are smaller, but it seems like things could get pretty wild ahead of Nov. 10.
One name that has been floated in recent days is Houston Texans edge rusher Jadeveon Clowney . ESPN reported earlier this week that the former No. 1 overall pick's name has surfaced in trade discussions.
The Texans are sitting at 2-3, three full games back of the Jacksonville Jaguars in the AFC South and 2.5 games back of the final wild card spot. Clowney himself has played sparingly, appearing on only 37% of Houston's defensive snaps so far this season. He's also been fairly unproductive, recording just 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss and four quarterback hits.
His pressure rate of 13.0%, though, indicates he's been a bit more effective than his counting stats, as he ranks 58th out of 262 players who have rushed the passer at least 50 times so far this season, according to Tru Media. The sample is very small, as Clowney has just 69 pass-rush snaps.
Still, given Clowney's age (33 years old) and relative lack of production, it's hard to see him generating much in the way of a trade return for the Texans. It's most likely that he would net a late-round pick at most, and perhaps only a swap of picks. The Texans sent one of their 2027 seventh-round picks to Cleveland in 2025 and another to Detroit this past offseason in the David Montgomery deal, but have one incoming from the Chargers, so that is the pick we have them sending out in each deal.
As for a few teams that could make sense for Clowney, here's a list.
The Niners have already given their defensive line a boost by trading for DeForest Buckner , and they should welcome Nick Bosa back into the fold soon, if not this week coming off their bye. But they're still just 21st in the NFL in pressure rate, according to Tru Media, and they have been dealing with injuries along the defensive front all season. Adding another capable rotational player off the edge could give them an extra boost ahead of a potential playoff run.
The Chiefs have bigger needs, with the most obvious one being wide receiver, but that doesn't mean they can't use at least some help in the pass rush department. George Karlaftis has 34 pressures this season, but R Mason Thomas , Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Ashton Gillotte have combined for only 42, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding another body to the mix could have some merit. The Chiefs have a 2027 sixth-round pick incoming from the 49ers, likely very late in the round, which they can send out here.
To be clear, the Cowboys should almost certainly not be buyers ahead of the deadline. They are 3-5 and going nowhere fast. But we know that Jerry Jones doesn't operate that way. He fears irrelevance more than anything else, and the Cowboys are in danger of becoming irrelevant this season. Clowney was in Dallas last year and racked up 8.5 sacks but the team elected not to re-sign him because of scheme fit concerns, but with the pass rush mostly not getting home, perhaps the Cowboys would bring him back. Dallas sends out a 2028 pick here because the 2027 sixth-rounder is headed to Pittsburgh in the Joey Porter Jr. trade.
The Giants are in first place in the NFC East and apparently going hunting for all kinds of players at the deadline. With Brian Burns out for the year, the Giants check in 31st in pressure rate, per Tru Media, and they could use some help for Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux coming off the edge. If they allocate more resources to other positions, it could make sense to go for a cheaper option on the defensive front. The Giants have an incoming sixth-round pick in the 2027 draft from the Jacksonville Jaguars, and that's likely to land pretty late in the round.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Browns' Deshaun Watson in concussion protocol: Shedeur Sanders potentially in line to start Week 9 at Saints
summary: Watson cleared evaluation Sunday but started having symptoms Monday night
full_text:
Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson entered the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday morning, the Browns announced . Watson, who passed concussion evaluation after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit during Sunday's loss to the Steelers , told team doctors he started feeling concussion-like symptoms Monday night.
Deshaun Watson has been placed in concussion protocol pic.twitter.com/ViiyRHMct8
Should Watson be unable to play in Week 9 against the Saints , the Browns would likely turn to second-year pro Shedeur Sanders .
Watson briefly left Sunday's contest in Pittsburgh after a spotter called down to the sideline for Watson to be checked out after Jaquan Brisker's helmet-to-helmet hit (which was flagged). Sanders entered the game briefly before Watson returned. Watson finished the 27-6 loss with 324 passing yards but also eight sacks and zero touchdowns.
Brisker flagged for hit on Watson #Steelers #NFL pic.twitter.com/FCOv8QtjJA
The Browns say they also evaluated Watson for a concussion after the game and again Monday morning, per league rules. However, when Watson reported his symptoms to the team on Tuesday morning, Cleveland immediately put him in the protocol.
Sanders, 24, could start Sunday in a crucial game for the Browns, who are 5-3 this season. He has appeared in two games this year, but only for five snaps. He has completed all three of his passes for 2 yards.
Sanders did get considerable playing time as part of Cleveland's quarterback carousel last year, appearing in eight games (seven starts). He threw seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions while completing 56.6% of his passes. He had some impressive performances, including a three-touchdown day against the Titans , but struggled overall. Out of 36 quarterbacks with at least 200 pass attempts, he was last in completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception rate and passer rating.
Sanders lost the quarterback battle to Watson this offseason, but should he be called upon to start, he'd be in a much better offensive ecosystem than he was in last year. The Browns have upgraded their offensive line and wide receivers, with rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion impressing. The Saints could potentially provide a soft landing spot, too: New Orleans' defense ranks 28th in both yards per play and yards per game.

title: Brandon Aiyuk files to be reinstated, will report to 49ers facility this week, per report
summary: San Francisco now has the option to trade or release the disgruntled wide receiver, with an outright cut viewed as the most likely outcome after a turbulent year away from the team
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is taking the steps necessary to return to the field. This week, ESPN reported he had hired agent Drew Rosenhaus to represent him, and now, he has reportedly turned in paperwork filing to be reinstated . Adam Schefter says Aiyuk will report to the 49ers' facilities on Friday.
"Brandon is healthy and ready to get back on the field," Rosenhaus said.
If Aiyuk is reinstated, the 49ers could trade or release him. General manager John Lynch said 10 months ago it was safe to say the wide receiver had played his last snap for the 49ers. The franchise would like to pick up some compensation in parting ways with their two-year-old headache, but it remains to be seen if any team would offer anything for him. ESPN reported that if Aiyuk is reinstated, the most likely outcome is the franchise releasing him.
This strange saga began when Aiyuk tore his ACL in October 2024. He was placed on the PUP list prior to the 2025 season as he continued to rehab, but 13 months after his injury, it was reported that the 49ers had voided the $27 million of 2026 salary guarantees in his contract. Aiyuk apparently had not been checking in with the team, sticking to his rehab schedule or doing what his contract required of him. Aiyuk was placed on the reserve/left squad list in December.
Aiyuk spent this past offseason taking shots at the 49ers on social media, and acting as if he were going to reunite with his college quarterback in Jayden Daniels and sign with the Washington Commanders . However, the 49ers still owned his rights, so Aiyuk had to file for reinstatement and then be acquired via trade if his Washington dream were to come true. Aiyuk refused to complete these steps in the offseason, but now, he's playing ball.
Aiyuk established himself as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL in 2023, as he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on the way to Super Bowl LVIII. His 3.1 yards per route run that year ranked No. 3 behind Tyreek Hill and Nico Collins , and his 81.3% of receptions going for a first down or a touchdown ranked first in the NFL.
The offseason following the Super Bowl appearance, Aiyuk orchestrated a "hold-in" during training camp, which eventually led to the four-year, $120 million extension he was after. That 2024 season, Aiyuk reached 50 yards receiving in just one of the seven games he played in before tearing his ACL.

title: Midseason All-Rookie Team: QB Jalon Daniels leads team filled with multiple Browns, Jets
summary: A dynamic Browns wide receiver duo and Titans standout Carnell Tate highlight the offensive playmakers making an immediate impact through the first eight weeks
full_text:
The departure from a 16-game regular season eliminated a clean midway point to the NFL regular season, but there is a large enough sample size to assess the contributions of the rookie class through Week 8.
Reflecting upon the 2026 NFL Draft , there were 19 offensive and 13 defensive prospects taken in the first round. Although the No. 1 overall selection has yet to make his first start, several others are making a meaningful impact on their respective teams.
Here is the Midseason All-Rookie team:
Daniels is the selection by default. He is the only rookie quarterback to appear in more than one game and the only quarterback with more than 36 dropbacks.
The undrafted free agent out of Kansas had some good moments. He looked crisp in three quarters against the Steelers , but accuracy waned in the game's most critical moments. His comfort is throwing to the boundary rather than attacking the middle of the field, but he would lock onto his first read, and defenders began breaking on it once they picked up on the tendency. When the sea parted before him, Daniels showed the foot speed to get chunks of yardage on the ground.
To be a viable quarterback long-term, Daniels must do a better job handling pressure. He was sacked nine times on 123 dropbacks because the protection was either not set to handle the blitz or he could not feel the pressure on his back.
He completed 60 of 98 pass attempts for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions.
Preseason selection: Fernando Mendoza , Raiders
The running back position was more complicated than quarterback because each of the candidates has either missed time due to injury or is serving in a reserve role. Love leads all rookie running backs with 76 carries despite missing two games and is now actively dealing with an ankle injury that landed him on the injured reserve. His presence on the end-of-year All-Rookie team is very much in doubt.
Love shows good vision and does well breaking his feet down in space to leverage defenders. He is patient before making his move and has 11 receptions as well. Arizona's offensive line has left a lot to be desired. The Notre Dame product has been averaging 1.1 yards before contact this season, which is below average, according to TruMedia.
Las Vegas' Mike Washington Jr . has had some big runs on stretch plays to the boundary. San Francisco's Kaelon Black drew heavy consideration. Denver's Jonah Coleman has been a personal favorite, but the body of work is limited due to injury.
Preseason selection: Jeremiyah Love , Cardinals
Concepcion has the second-most receptions among rookie receivers but has nearly half of his receptions and 57.7% of his receiving yards over the past three games. It has taken some time to develop timing and chemistry with Deshaun Watson , who was errant on several passes in Concepcion's direction at the start of the season.
Among all rookie receivers, Concepcion ranks second in yards after the catch per reception (5.5), according to TruMedia. He is dynamic and elusive with the ball in his hands.
The Texas A&M product has 33 receptions for 352 yards.
KC Concepcion just has a different gear with the ball in his hands pic.twitter.com/bumtXpwWll
Preseason selection: K.C. Concepcion, Browns
Tate was the third choice, and the margins may be slimmer than one may expect of the leading rookie receiver. The No. 4 overall selection has four drops and three fumbles this season.
Tate has good size and the foot quickness to win out of the stem, but he generally has not been threatening downfield against man coverage. He was unavailable for Sunday's loss to the Bengals due to a shoulder injury; the first game of his career missed.
The Ohio State product leads all rookies in receptions (34) and receiving yards (413).
Preseason selection: Carnell Tate , Titans
Boston has slowed down a bit over the past month after his blistering start that led to some glamorous statistical and play-style comparisons. Most of his early season success was isolated to ball-winning downfield plays. In each of the first five games, he had a reception of at least 20 yards. In that metric, among rookies, he trails only his teammate, Concepcion, who has seven.
Boston is a classic X-receiver, but the Browns would be better served diversifying his usage as he becomes more comfortable transitioning to the NFL. The next step in Boston's growth is developing better chemistry with Watson and finishing plays. Boston has just one drop to his name, but there were a handful of others that could be classified as such. He is consistently open and a zone coverage merchant, but not always on the same page as his quarterback.
There are a variety of other pass catchers who deserve recognition, such as Omar Cooper Jr . ( Jets ), Germie Bernard (Steelers), Caleb Douglas ( Dolphins ), Antonio Williams ( Commanders ) and Malachi Fields ( Giants ).
Preseason selection: Denzel Boston , Browns
Sadiq has been a plus performer in both the pass and run games. He leads all rookie tight ends in receptions (17) and receiving yards (186). As a prospect, the ex-Oregon Duck was known for his play-making ability post-catch, and he has carried that trait into the league. Among all receivers and tight ends, Sadiq ranks second in yards after the catch per reception (6.0).
In the run game, he is a bulldog. He is constantly working and straining to sustain blocks and spring his teammates for bigger gains. At times, he could rein in that energy a bit better, but he has been a well-rounded asset for the AFC franchise.
In the preseason, Patriots tight end Eli Raridon was among those under consideration. He has been excellent for a rejuvenated New England team.
Preseason selection: Kenyon Sadiq , Jets
There have been a few rookies to moonlight as left tackles this season, but the possibilities boiled down to Kahlil Benson of the Chiefs , Jayden Williams of the Cardinals and Fano. Benson is a great story and incredibly valuable in the absence of former first-round pick Josh Simmons . However, Fano has a higher ceiling because of his athleticism.
Fano has a really natural feel for the game. He communicates and picks up exchanges well. He possesses the requisite foot quickness and ankle flexion to handle most of what is thrown at him. His issues are largely correctable, but his play strength still must improve.
Fano has been credited with two sacks and 18 pressures allowed on 311 pass-blocking snaps, according to TruMedia.
Preseason selection: Spencer Fano , Browns
Jacksonville's Emmanuel Pregnon and Proctor were candidates for different reasons. Pregnon has a better feel for the offense and consistently executes it well but does not possess Proctor's ceiling.
The former Alabama left tackle has allowed nine pressures and one sack in 186 pass-blocking snaps, according to TruMedia.
Preseason selection: Kadyn Proctor , Dolphins
A training camp injury to veteran Tyler Biadasz forced Slaughter into the starting lineup. Los Angeles' offensive woes can not be attributed to a single person, but the rookie has certainly been a flawed part of the line. TruMedia credits him with eight pressures and one sack allowed on 261 pass-blocking snaps, but more powerful interior players have given him fits with the bull rush. Slaughter has good foot mobility and can execute some of the blocks in space that have been asked of him.
Preseason selection: Jake Slaughter , Chargers
There was consideration to pencil in Ioane as the center given he spent some time there this season, which would allow Cleveland's Austin Barber to be the selection at right guard. Ioane and Barber have been the two best interior linemen this season. Baltimore intends to play the former at right guard, so he will align there in this exercise.
Although he is now dealing with an injury, TruMedia credits Ioane with seven pressures and one sack allowed on 210 pass-blocking snaps. Ioane plays with a sturdy base and looks for work when disengaged.
Preseason selection: Francis Mauigoa ,…

title: NFL Week 9 picks, best bets: Bears continue to surge in primetime, Vikings lose second straight vs. Bills
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 9 schedule, including five locks against the spread
full_text:
We've been on the wrong side of a couple of bad beats throughout the first half of the regular season, and Week 8 was no exception. One of my five locks last week was the Patriots covering a 7.5-point spread over the Dolphins in Miami. For a large chunk of the second half, we were well on our way to cashing. Then, in the blink of an eye, we were suddenly sweating it out.
After a 14-point third-quarter lead ballooned New England's lead to 11 and just four minutes remained in regulation, the Dolphins put together an eight-play, 84-yard touchdown drive to cut it within five. The gut punch was Malik Willis uncorking a 35-yard touchdown to Kevin Coleman Jr . to put them within the number.
Kevin Coleman Jr. scores and we have a one-score game in Miami NEvsMIA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/4NjWuELca1
Even when all was thought to be lost, there was another opportunity for New England to extend the lead late after a botched onside kick by Miami. The Patriots reached the Dolphins' 38-yard line and faced a third-and-5. If they failed to convert, a meaningless field-goal attempt would've brought the lead to eight. Alas, Rhamondre Stevenson rushed for the necessary yardage to move the chains, Drake Maye knelt three times, and we came out losers. Pain.
While that bat beat put in through a torture chamber, it was a good slate for us overall. I was 3-2 ATS with my locks of the week, 8-6 ATS overall, and 10-4 on the moneyline. I'll look to keep that momentum rolling and try to avoid any more bad beats as our attention now pivots to Week 9. As always, we begin with my five locks of the week.
Note : Tennessee and Pittsburgh are on the bye in Week 9.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Bears look like bona fide Super Bowl contenders right now after rolling into Seattle and taking it to the defending champion Seahawks , with new defensive stud Jeffery Simmons showing out in his debut.
They head back home for another primetime matchup against a Bucs team that didn't complete a pass in a 16-0 win over the Falcons . Over the past two games, Tampa Bay's passing attack has completed 7 of 14 attempts for 64 yards and one touchdown. That might be good enough to lock in two wins against NFC South rivals, but they'll need to chuck it to keep pace with Caleb Williams and keep this newly dominant defense honest. I don't believe they will be able to, which sets up Chicago to win its fourth straight game.
The Bears are also 3-1 ATS at home this season.
Projected score : Bears 28, Buccaneers 20 The pick : Bears -6.5
Weather was a factor, but I did find it noteworthy that the Patriots struggled to fend off the Dolphins in last week's win in Miami. Sure, a divisional game will always be pesky, but it is sticking in the back of my head as I look towards this matchup with Green Bay.
I think Drake Maye, who leads the NFL in total yards and total touchdowns from Week 4 to Week 8, will have some trouble against this evolving Packers defense. Over the past five games, Green Bay is allowing just 14.6 points per game, which ranks third in the NFL. Meanwhile, Jordan Love is first in the NFL in passing yards entering Week 8 and first in completions of 20-plus air yards. He's also fourth in passing touchdowns, so New England's defense will have its hands full and is firmly on upset alert.
Projected score : Packers 23, Patriots 21 The pick : Packers +3
Jayden Daniels was pretty erratic with his throws on Sunday night, despite pulling out the 27-10 win over Philadelphia. For the game, he had an off-target rate of 17.2%, which was the third-highest in a single game in his career. That's alarming, particularly as Washington hosts a Rams team that is starting to gain some momentum.
This season, L.A. is allowing 301.1 total yards per game, which ranks fifth in the league. If Daniels continues to misfire, this Rams defense has shown it can shut down an opponent. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 0-5 following a win since the start of last season and own a -9.0 points-per-game differential over that stretch.
This could be a game where Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua feast, as Washington is currently giving up a 100.6 passer rating against this season, which ranks 25th in the league. I expect another prolific game from that duo as L.A. wins and covers.
Projected score : Rams 27, Commanders 21 The pick : Rams -5.5
At any moment, another star could be shipped out of Indy, which makes this line something we'll want to jump on with it below a touchdown. Yes, the Cowboys defense is horrid and just lost to Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals , but Indianapolis is lost right now. They were just blown out 42-7 by the Jaguars and are 2-13 over their past 15 games. This season, they are allowing 27.8 points per game, which is the third-highest in the NFL entering Week 9. That sets up this Cowboys offense to flirt with 30 points on the day.
If they get there, it's hard to imagine Daniel Jones keeping pace, even when accounting for Dallas' defense. Jones has an NFL-worst 68.7 passer rating this season and appears to be barely clinging to his starting job. Since Week 9 of last year, Jones is 3-10 as the starter with 13 total touchdowns and 20 turnovers. Meanwhile, I think Indy will continue to limit Jonathan Taylor , with trade rumors still swirling around him. Last week, he played a season-low 62.3% of the offensive snaps, which was less than the 67.2% offensive snaps he logged the week prior in Week 7. If Taylor is less of a factor, that only lowers the ceiling of the Indy offense and clears a path for Dallas to cover.
Projected score : Cowboys 30, Colts 17 The pick : Cowboys -6
The Vikings suffered their first loss of the season in Week 8, falling to the Lions in a game that further emphasized the clunky start Kyler Murray has had running the offense. It's largely been masked by the stellar play of the defense, but Minnesota's offense is averaging just 279.4 total yards per game, which is the fourth-lowest in the league. Their 20 points per game average ranks sixth-lowest.
That's unsustainable, especially against another high-octane offense like the Bills . Buffalo is averaging a league-best 33.3 points per game. While the Vikings defense will make it hard for them to maintain that average, they may not need to reach 30 to pull out the win on the road. Last week, Detroit scored 19 points in the winning effort, while going 1-for-3 in the red zone. Buffalo scores touchdowns on 70% of its red zone trips this season (fifth-highest). If they maintain that success and merely get north of 20 points, that could be too tall of a mountain for Murray and the Vikings offense to overcome.

title: Tyler Huntley out for season: Ravens lose top backup with Lamar Jackson already out, per report
summary: Baltimore will start undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano on Thursday
full_text:
As the reeling Baltimore Ravens try to figure out whether Lamar Jackson's thumb injury will cost him the rest of the season, they got certainty on his backup. Tyler Huntley is in fact out for the remainder of 2026 due to a turf toe injury he suffered after relieving Jackson in Sunday's loss to the Bills , per ESPN's Adam Schefter .
The Ravens have been in scramble mode ever since the pair of quarterback injuries. Emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano , an undrafted rookie out of UConn, finished out Sunday's 36-10 blowout loss and will start Thursday against the Jaguars . Baltimore added Austin Reed , who was with the team in the preseason, to its practice squad and signed Kedon Slovis off Green Bay's practice squad earlier this week in an attempt to build some sort of depth on a short week. Reed has never taken a regular-season snap, and Slovis has taken five.
Huntley, 29, has spent six of his seven years with the Ravens after going undrafted in 2020. He has been a crucial depth piece, starting 14 games during his time in Baltimore, including three this year as Jackson dealt with an ankle injury. Huntley guided Baltimore to a win over the Falcons but lost to the Browns and Bengals before Jackson's short-lived return. He suffered the turf toe injury when Bills DT Ed Oliver landed on the back of his foot.
Ravens backup QB Tyler Huntley dealing with a toe injury. On the replay, you can see his right foot plant before continuing into extension, placing increased stress through the toe region. Turf toe is a concern here, involving injury to the plantar structures of the 1st MTP… pic.twitter.com/EIoipD8xyw
With more clarity on at least one quarterback's injury, the Ravens could look to make a trade ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, with Tyson Bagent and Jacoby Brissett as potential options mentioned by NFL Network's Ian Rapoport earlier this week.
Baltimore is 4-4 on the season and has lost three straight games.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Week 9 QB Power Rankings: Familiar name returns to No. 1, Cam Ward crawls out of basement

full_text:
Quarterbacks are the most vital position in football. After all, they're the highest-paid players, and the past 13 NFL MVP award winners are, that's right, quarterbacks. While some quarterbacks are a byproduct of their offensive ecosystems, a select few elevate above their current circumstances to the ranks of the elite.
These rankings are fluid and designed to tell the story of each starting quarterback's respective rise and/or fall throughout the season. That's why some quarterbacks in this week's rankings rose as many as seven spots or fell as many as five. Not in a vacuum, Patrick Mahomes would remain No. 1 for the foreseeable future and so on. He hasn't been in the top spot for some weeks now, given his torn ACL and others playing better ahead of him. However, that isn't set in stone, and he could rise back to the top of the board as the 2026 season progresses. He made some steps forward this week.
So where do the league's biggest names line up entering the ninth week of the regular season? Enjoy the Week 9 edition of the 2026 NFL Quarterback Power Rankings:

title: Prisco's Week 9 NFL expert picks: Jaguars roll over Lamar Jackson-less Ravens, Cowboys rebound
summary: Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss
full_text:
The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday.
Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3.
As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take.
Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week.
Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16
The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain.
Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21
The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line.
Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20
The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game.
Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17
The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around.
This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff .
Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13
The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game.
Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14
The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late.
Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20
This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it.
Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24
