George Pickens is the dream add here, but Kansas City must do something . Must. Mahomes is too good. Kenneth Walker III is too good. You just can't pass up many opportunities when you have Mahomes. The Chiefs have extra draft capital. Look at other Super Bowl contenders making big trades this season. If you're not giving Mahomes the best chance possible (within reason) to win a Super Bowl every year, you're being wasteful. It's already bad that the pass-catcher is such a huge issue for a second straight year, but the Chiefs have a chance to change that.
A week ago, I floated Adonai Mitchell as a potential solution for the Chiefs' wide receiver woes. He was coming off a zero-catch game, and Omar Cooper Jr . was emerging for the Jets .
Now? I think Mitchell might be a legit part of the Jets' long-term build. Sunday, he had seven catches for 142 yards and a touchdown. But it's more than the stats. It's how he looked as he accrued them.
Adonai Mitchell set a new career high with 142 receiving yards, topping his previous best of 102. 7 REC, 142 REC YDS, 1 TD vs Raiders Acquired in the Sauce Gardner trade, Mitchell is showing serious potential in New York. pic.twitter.com/djWO4vT8Ik
That is legitimate star-level film. I know the Raiders ' cornerbacks are young and not great, but Mitchell looked like varsity against JV.
Mitchell was a throw-in in the Sauce Gardner trade. An afterthought. His career was synonymous with a 75-yard catch in which he toasted…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 9 picks and score predictions: Packers ruin Tom Brady's trip to New England, Jaguars destroy Ravens
summary: John Breech makes his Week 9 NFL picks, including Jacksonville cruising past a short-handed Baltimore team and Green Bay spoiling a star-studded weekend in New England
full_text:
With the NFL season heading into Week 9, we are officially halfway through the year, which makes right now the perfect time to hand out some midseason awards. Actually, I'm only handing out one award, and it's going to me, and I don't even want it: It's the award for worst picker from Week 8.
I went 8-6 last week, which ended up being the worst record out of our experts here at CBS Sports in Week 8. I clearly spent way too much time trying to find a Halloween costume and not enough time researching my picks. Next year for Halloween, I'm going to go as someone who's good at picks, so I guess I'll be dressing up as Jamey Eisenberg.
Eisnenberg, who is our long-time NFL fantasy analyst here, might want to give up on the fantasy stuff and just start doing NFL picks full time because he went 12-2 last week. Also, he's 69-49-3 against the spread this year. I might have to copy his picks this week.
So will I actually copy Jamey's picks? Probably not, but let's get to the picks and find out for sure.
Actually, before we get to the Week 9 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . Also, as you probably know by now -- because I point it out every week -- I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address . I'm going to eat one piece of my six-year-old's Halloween candy every time someone signs up. My dentist is going to love this.
Speaking of things we love, let's get to the picks.
If you had asked me at 10 a.m. ET on Nov. 1 who was going to win this game, I probably would have picked the Ravens , but a few things have happened since then:
Those two injuries mean the Ravens will likely go into this game with an undrafted rookie ( Joe Fagnano ) as their starting quarterback, but that's not even a guarantee because he's dealing with an ankle injury. The Ravens literally might have to run the wishbone offense on Thursday. You have to be desperate to run the wishbone and I think the Ravens are there. Bill Walsh actually implemented it for a game in 1987 when he had to use a replacement quarterback while the regular players were on strike.
October 5, 1987 Bill Walsh Employs the Wishbone In the second half of the first MNF game to feature "replacement players" during the 1987 players' strike, the 49ers legendary head coach utilizes the "wishbone" offense against the Giants and head coach Bill Parcells. Walsh —… pic.twitter.com/EoXESclJi1
The Ravens could also run the wing-T. Basically, any offense from 1934 would work at this point. They could even call the Buccaneers ' for a few tips. They just won a game without throwing a single pass. The Ravens might have to do that this week.
So the Ravens don't even know who their starting QB will be this week, and to make matters worse, they have to face what might be the best team in the AFC. If Week 8 was any indication, the Jaguars have finally figured out how to run the ball again and when they run the ball, they're virtually unbeatable. Since Liam Coen took over as head coach, the Jags are 10-1 when they rush for at least 110 yards and they did that in Week 8 by rushing for a season-high 183 yards in a 42-7 win over the Colts .
When the Jaguars can run the ball, that takes some pressure off of Trevor Lawrence and he seems to thrive in those situations. In Week 8, Lawrence completed just 10 passes, but he threw for 210 yards and three touchdowns while finishing with a 153.3 passer rating.
Do you want to know how absurd that is? Those stats made Lawrence the first player in 55 years to finish with at least 200 passing yards, three touchdown passes and a passer rating of 150-or-higher on 10 completions or fewer. The last player to pull that off was Roger Staubach and he did that while playing for the Cowboys in 1971. Did I mention that the Cowboys won the Super Bowl that year? Because the Cowboys won the Super Bowl that year.
I'm not saying the Jags are going to win the Super Bowl this year or am I saying that? I don't know anymore. Pete Prisco made the Jags his preseason pick to win the Super Bowl and I can't comprehend living in a world where Prisco nails a prediction like that.
Jaguars Super Bowl Champs?! 👀 @PriscoCBS predicts that Jacksonville will defeat Dallas in Super Bowl LXI Do you agree? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/ehm4qv8MI8
I'm going to cut Pete some slack and ignore the Cowboys part of that prediction.
I don't know if the Jags are going to win the Super Bowl, but I do think they roll to a win on Thursday night.
PICK: Jaguars 30-13 over Ravens
For just the second time, Spain is hosting an NFL game, and the biggest winner might be everyone flying into Madrid this week. I've only been to Spain once, and they were handing out free shots of Jagermeister at the airport. And as we all know, you haven't lived until you've done free shots of Jager in a Spanish airport before noon. At least that's what I tell myself.
This seems like a solid idea: Free samples of jagermeister at the airport. I'll know what I'll be doing until takeoff pic.twitter.com/EGYk4XKEwE
I'm not sure if the shot guy is still there and I feel like someone needs to investigate, so I'll be heading to Madrid this week to find out. I will definitely report back my findings.
This is the fifth NFL game being held in Europe this year, and so far, the team that leaves later in the week has had a major advantage in each game. The team that has arrived on Friday has gone 4-0 this year. If you're wondering who has the travel advantage this week, the answer is NO ONE. The Bengals and Falcons will both depart on Tuesday night and spend their entire practice week in Madrid. I hope they've brushed up on their Spanish.
The bad news for the Falcons is that there's rain in the forecast for Sunday, and based on what I saw in Week 8, they might want to just forfeit if it rains, because they are arguably the worst team in NFL history when it comes to playing in the rain. Actually, forget that whole forfeit thing; the stadium in Spain has a retractable roof, so weather won't be a problem. That's good news for the Falcons.
🚨🏟️𝗨𝗡𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗟 The new Santiago Bernabéu equipped with a retractable roof is ready ahead of todays game against Getafe. pic.twitter.com/orCvRtdaBY
The other good news for the Falcons is that they could not have asked for a better matchup after an embarrassing loss on Sunday. The Bengals defense has given up 621 yards to tight ends this year, which is the second-highest number in the NFL. Kyle Pitts is on my fantasy team and this might be the first time all year where I actually feel confident about starting him. I've let my team know that no one is safe and that I will start cutting people if we don't start improving. And I will start with Kyle Pitts if he doesn't go off against the Bengals.
Another reason this is a solid matchup for the Falcons is that they have Bijan Robinson . The Bengals are giving up 4.8 yards per carry this year, which is the fourth-worst number in the NFL, and now, they have to face Robinson, who is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. That seems like a recipe for disaster. Basically, the Falcons offense is built to exploit every weakness on the Bengals' defense.
Also, if you watched the Falcons play the Buccaneers in Week 8, you may have noticed that Atlanta's defense can't stop the run, but that might not matter in this game, because the Bengals can't run the ball.
I think what I'm trying to say here is that the Falcons might put up a lot of points. However, that probably won't matter because the Bengals have Joe Burrow . Over his past three games, Burrow is averaging 314.7 passing yards and 4.3 touchdown passes per game. During that span, he became the FIRST quarterback in NFL history to throw at least four TD passes with a completion percentage of 70% in three straight games.
Burrow is currently on fire. Oh, and did I mention that he practically requested to play in…

title: Week 8, 3 down and 3 down: No silver lining from the Monsoon Bowl
summary: The Atlanta Falcons played the role of Artax from The Neverending Story, and like Atreyu, Falcons fans’ cries and pleas went unanswered as they watched their team slowly drown in the swamp. There is no up this week; everyone sank in the pit. Here’s the Week 8, 3 down and 3 down. 3 down Michael […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers rushes in the first half against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons played the role of Artax from The Neverending Story , and like Atreyu, Falcons fans’ cries and pleas went unanswered as they watched their team slowly drown in the swamp. There is no up this week; everyone sank in the pit. Here’s the Week 8, 3 down and 3 down. 3 down Michael Penix Jr. This is what the worst version of Penix looks like. The slow starts have been there all season, but the turnovers have not. He’s a rhythm passer, but that’s a two-way street; once he gets off beat, he stays there. When he finds his groove, he is one of the more efficient passers out there. Yes, the game plan was poor and so was the weather, but that doesn’t mean you carelessly throw off your back foot, or throw into double/triple coverage. Everyone has bad games; I don’t expect Penix to look this bad again, but it’s up to him to make sure that doesn’t happen. Michael Panix Bowles packed the line and once again Penix struggled with these looks. Rat defender ate his lunch all day, he struggled when forced to move and, mechanics deteriorated as things got worse and he compounded his bad decisions. Worst game of his career. pic.twitter.com/Rsx9i3eVlg — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 2, 2026 Matthew Bergeron The guard received his extension based on his potential, and he isn’t living up to it. Unlike others on the line, he isn’t a lineman with a typical outside-zone build; he has the physical traits that should transfer to a gap or duo scheme, but the team hasn’t had much success running these concepts behind him. Of all the Falcons linemen, he is the one who doesn’t get to use the size excuse many have applied to the Buccaneers -Falcons mismatch, but he was routinely manhandled. If Bergeron can’t turn things around, he’ll be the first black eye on Cunningham’s resume, because no matter how this season goes, they are tied to him through the 2027 season . Run Defense The Falcons didn’t allow a single reception in this game, but they did allow 324 rushing yards. The rookie linebackers struggled all game, and the attacking scheme’s aggressive nature is being taken advantage of by gap schemes, and Jeff Ulbrich is out of answers. He’s increased the number of defensive line slants, a technique that essentially has his defenders line up in one gap and shoot into another, but it doesn’t really solve the problem. For starters, it’s a guessing game; the defense doesn’t know where the ball is going and is hoping to catch the offense off guard, but they aren’t. The other issue is that against a gap scheme, they block down most of the time, so even if you move into a new gap, the OL isn’t necessarily unprepared; they just need to play sound and pick up whoever shows up. Injuries to the front have definitely taken their toll on the defense, so the struggles are understandable. It is also worth noting that 229 of those 324 yards came after contact , and the weather definitely played a role in that statistic. Every Bucs explosive run – DL slants were ineffective, resulting in massive gaps and let the OL get to the 2nd level with ease – LBs struggled with their keys, lots of gap guessing. Cooked when the OL got hands on them – Horrific run fits from Watts – Poor tackling by everyone pic.twitter.com/jValXYFFkV — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 2, 2026 3 down (part 2) Run Offense Something’s gotta give. If you want to be treated like a winning team, you have to perform against good opponents, and the Falcons run game has been stuffed in a locker for four straight weeks. The reality is, they’re just not that good, and Bijan can’t cover up their poor blocking every week. Tommy Rees’ lack of confidence showed immediately in his decision to come out throwing in a monsoon. He isn’t putting forth a good enough effort to throw the run game away so early. After their best week with multiple tight end personnel groups, the young coordinator tried to do everything out of 11 personnel (3 WRs, 1 TE), which let Tampa Bay stay in nickel all game. He did implement more pulling concepts this week but did far less gap and inside zone. It feels like the team is just aimlessly throwing things at the wall and hoping it sticks, but nothing is. iOL was soft, Falcons couldn't get anything going either direction but struggled running left the most. Ran every concept in the book, nothing worked. OTs consistently lose at POA. Was a big fan of Josiah Trotter (45) last cycle and he lit the Falcons up, bulled the iOL pic.twitter.com/TI5f3UdoQL — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) November 3, 2026 Xavier Watts I highlighted Watts last week as someone who’s had an underwhelming second year, but I also pointed out that I was nitpicking a bit as he hasn’t truly been “bad.” That is not the case this week; Watts was awful. Just like Penix, that was his worst performance as a Falcon. His run fits were nightmarish, constantly misreading leverage and putting himself out of position. The open-field tackling was brutal and spurred many of the explosive runs. The young safety will get a lot more chances to play the pass next week, and let’s hope that helps him get some confidence back. Nick Folk Folk is cooked, washed, etc. The 41-year-old team captain will unfortunately not be the solution to the Falcons multi-year kicking struggles. Hard to use weather as an excuse when Chase McLaughlin posts a perfect day. The Falcons have no confidence in the kicker beyond 50, and we’re starting to see them not have any within 50. Folk signed a 2-year deal , but Atlanta can cut him without any financial drawbacks at the end of the season; back to the drawing board. It’ll take a while to get the mud out of those new red jerseys. The Falcons probably won’t play in a monsoon again this year, but that doesn’t mean there wasn’t plenty to learn from this outcome. Their process coming in was flawed, and they’ve now dropped to third place. Things won’t get easier as they are set to face the explosive Bengals offense in Spain.

summary: The Falcons failed their latest test, as the offense sputtered in a rainy, muddy mess of a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8. Now sitting at 3-5, Atlanta’s season rests upon the edge of a knife. Four straight games against playoff contenders await, and if the Falcons can’t manage to scrape out […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 18: The Cincinnati Bengals offense lines up against the Atlanta Falcons defense during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 18, 2023 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons failed their latest test, as the offense sputtered in a rainy, muddy mess of a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8. Now sitting at 3-5, Atlanta’s season rests upon the edge of a knife. Four straight games against playoff contenders await, and if the Falcons can’t manage to scrape out a couple wins, their own playoff hopes will disappear. The good news is that star pass rusher James Pearce Jr. returns from suspension this week and is expected to play. That’s a welcome boost to a pass rush that has been good at generating pressure, but fairly average at sacking the quarterback. They’ll need that pass rush, and everything else they can muster, to slow down a lethal Bengals offense in Madrid on Sunday morning. The Falcons are currently 3-point underdogs to the Bengals in Week 9, per FanDuel. While Atlanta is technically the home team, the international game makes this a “neutral” field situation. This will be the toughest passing game the Falcons have faced yet, so we’ll get a good look at the defense with Pearce back in the fold. This one is likely to come down to the play of Atlanta’s offense, however. Can Michael Penix Jr. bounce back from a career-worst performance to win a potential shootout? title: NFC South Week 8 Review: No one wants to win this thing
summary: The NFC South is 3-13 at home. No one in the division has a winning record; not one team is even sitting at .500. Business as usual. Here’s the Week 8 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) Week 8 Result: Buccaneers 16 – Falcons 0Week 9 Opponent:  Chicago Bears The Buccaneers have strung together […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers is hit by Ty'ron Hopper #59 of the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFC South is 3-13 at home. No one in the division has a winning record; not one team is even sitting at .500. Business as usual. Here’s the Week 8 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5) Week 8 Result: Buccaneers 16 – Falcons 0 Week 9 Opponent: Chicago Bears The Buccaneers have strung together back-to-back wins against division rivals, and after starting 1-5, are in the thick of the NFC South title race. Tampa Bay used the same formula that worked against the Panthers on the Falcons: run through the opposing defense’s face. That’s the perfect plan in a monsoon. The Buccaneers amassed over 300 yards on the ground and won the game without completing a single pass. Their defense picked off Michael Penix Jr. four times and shut out the Falcons offense. We’ll see what this team is really made of when they head to Chicago next week. MAN ON A MISSION 😤 📺: #ATLvsTB on FOX pic.twitter.com/ZdgiEHk2Z5 — Tampa Bay Buccaneers (@Buccaneers) November 1, 2026 Carolina Panthers (3-4) Week 8 Result: Panthers 19 – Packers 27 Week 9 Opponent: Denver Broncos This game was not as close as the score suggests. The Panthers are beat up right now, and it shows in every phase of the game. Bryce Young was constantly under pressure and had the jitters on the rare occasion he was kept clean. While the defense wasn’t the main issue in this game, they were lucky the Packers skill players kept dropping the ball, because they were getting torched. That may be one reason former DC Ejiro Evero was let go after the loss. However, firing Evero won’t fix their injury issues and only adds to the chaos. Carolina is set to host the Broncos, who are licking their chops after seeing Young under pressure all game. That's SIX sacks now for the Packers defense 🔥 CARvsGB on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/XPXJUSzU7j — NFL (@NFL) October 30, 2026 New Orleans Saints (2-5) Week 8 Result: Bye Week Week 9 Opponent: Cleveland Browns The Saints were on the bye this week, and they needed it. Injuries have plagued the defense, and Kellen Moore’s offense needed to be unplugged and plugged back in. Most teams sitting at 2-5 by Week 8 wouldn’t have a chance at climbing up the division rankings, but this is the NFC South. New Orleans ’ season isn’t over, and they’ll look to get back on track against the Browns next week. Atlanta Falcons (3-5) Week 8 Result: Falcons 0 – Buccaneers 16 Week 9 Opponent: Cincinnati Bengals Michael Penix Jr. had his worst performance as a pro, Tommy Rees called his worst game since joining the team, and Jeff Ulbrich’s defense gave up 324 yards on the ground; now that’s teamwork. Will the Falcons play in these conditions again this year? Probably not, but the team’s process in this storm was deeply flawed. They came out trying to throw the ball, which ended up going to the other team far too often. This offensive line isn’t pulling its weight and has Bijan Robinson looking pedestrian outside of a few carries per game. The team had a chance to take the top spot in the division, and now they’re sitting in 3rd place. Atlanta heads overseas to take on the Bengals in Spain The division is as chaotic as ever and lacks a truly “good” team, but someone has to win it. This race is setting up to be a photo finish once again.

title: Falcons cut defenders Drake Jackson, Jared Ivey
summary: After a tough day for the Falcons’ run defense, they’re shuffling the bottom of the roster. Atlanta announced yesterday that it had cut ties with defensive lineman Jared Ivey and outside linebacker Drake Jackson. One or both could return to the practice squad, and my bet would be Ivey, given that the team prioritized picking […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Jared Ivey #51 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on against the San Francisco 49ers during an NFL football game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a tough day for the Falcons’ run defense, they’re shuffling the bottom of the roster. Atlanta announced yesterday that it had cut ties with defensive lineman Jared Ivey and outside linebacker Drake Jackson . One or both could return to the practice squad, and my bet would be Ivey, given that the team prioritized picking him up off of waivers after roster cutdowns. Ivey had appeared in seven games for Atlanta this year, moving around a bit and chipping in six pressures, a sack, six stops, and five tackles, per Pro Football Focus. Against the Bears in particular he was a bit of a menace as a pass rusher, but over the past two games he had struggled mightily as a run defender working against Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black, Bucky Irving, and Kenneth Gainwell. There’s evident talent here as a pass rusher and I think he’s better than the past two weeks in run support, so I don’t think the Falcons are planning on letting him go if another team doesn’t snap him up. Jackson, meanwhile, played 20 snaps over two games in Atlanta and was inactive against the Buccaneers. He may well return, too, assuming the Falcons can and will make room for him. Why the moves? I think Atlanta Journal-Constitution beat writer Daniel Flick has it right: The Falcons released defensive ends Jared Ivey & Drake Jackson, per the team. As a reminder: James Pearce Jr. is eligible for reinstatement from his suspension, and Yasir Abdullah is eligible to return from IR. Could be the use for those two spots. — Daniel Flick (@ByDanielFlick) November 2, 2026 James Pearce Jr. is expected to be ready to go this week, just in time to harry Joe Burrow and the Bengals. Abdullah, meanwhile, was super effective as a pass rusher against the Saints in Week 4—the last time he suited up for Atlanta—and has been a solid run defender and special teamer throughout his career. Getting both of those players back would be a boost for this defense in a tough matchup. If Ivey and Jackson aren’t back, we’ll wish them well, but I’m hoping we’ll see both land on the practice squad.

title: Ravens poach QB Kedon Slovis off Packers’ practice squad
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are signing quarterback Kedon Slovis off the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad, per The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero. The second-year passer will add depth behind Joe Fagnano and Austin Reed following injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Slovis, 25, has taken just five regular-season snaps since entering the NFL as an undrafted […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Kedon Slovis (12) throws the ball against the Las Vegas Raiders n the second half at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens are signing quarterback Kedon Slovis off the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad, per The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero. The second-year passer will add depth behind Joe Fagnano and Austin Reed following injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Slovis, 25, has taken just five regular-season snaps since entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2024 after five years(!) as a starter in college. He spent three years at USC and started as a true freshman before leading the Pac-12 in most volume passing statistics in 2020 and passing yards per game in 2020 and 2021. His numbers dropped sharply at Pitt and BYU over the next two years with a 58.0% completion rate, 216.5 yards per game, and a 3.6% touchdown rate after 68.4%, 280.6, and 6.1% marks, respectively, as a Trojan. Slovis did not make the Colts’ active roster as a rookie and spent the year on the Texans’ practice squad. He was waived by Houston during final roster cuts in 2025 and signed with the Cardinals’ practice squad, where he worked with now-Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork. After Kyle Murray went down in October, Slovis was promoted to the active roster. He appeared in two games after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew also suffered injuries. Arizona moved on from Slovis this past offseason. He took up the Packers’ third-string quarterback job and posted prolific numbers in the preseason. His 434 passing yards ranked third in the league, as did his 83.6 grade from Pro Football Focus (min. 50 snaps). Unlike Fagnano in Baltimore, however, his performance did not earn him a 53-man roster spot. He stayed on Green Bay’s practice squad, keeping him available to be poached by the Ravens amid their injury crisis. Slovis only has a few days to learn Baltimore’s offense – a tall task for a veteran, much less a third-year player. Since the emergency No. 3 quarterback must be on the 53-man roster, it would make sense to designate him such on Thursday night and elevate Austin Reed, who played for the Ravens in the preseason, to back up Fagnano – assuming he starts. The undrafted rookie is dealing with an ankle injury that limited him at Monday’s walkthrough, though both player and club have expressed optimism about his availability. The Ravens also worked out former 49ers quarterback Adrian Martinez on Tuesday morning, per The Athletic’s Jeff Zrebiec , who adds that the team may not be done adding at the position. Martinez went undrafted out of Kansas State in 2023 and has spent time with the Lions, Jets, and 49ers in the last three years. He appeared in one gamesfor the 49ers in 2025 and played just one snap. He was also named the UFL MVP in 2024 after passing for 1,750 yards and 15 touchdowns with 530 rushing yards and three scores on 54 attempts across the Birmingham Stallions’ 10 regular-season games.

title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis, Week 8: Quarterback position in flux
summary: Offense Lamar Jackson’s much-awaited return lasted just one play before he suffered a thumb injury, which sidelined him for the rest of the game. Then, backup Tyler Huntley exited the game after 10 snaps with a toe injury, opening the door for No. 3 quarterback Joe Fagnano to play the final 40 offensive reps under […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Landon Jackson #94 of the Buffalo Bills sacks Joe Fagnano #12 of the Baltimore Ravens during the first half at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Offense QB: Joe Fagnano 40, Tyler Huntley 10, Lamar Jackson 1 RB: Justice Hill 25, Derrick Henry 23, Rasheen Ali 1 WR: Zay Flowers 42, Rashod Bateman 39, Ja’Kobi Lane 33, Devontez Walker 8, LaJohntay Wester 6 TE: Mark Andrews 29, Matthew Hibner 21, Josh Cuevas 13, Nick Vannett 11 OL: Ronnie Stanley 51, John Simpson 51, Cam Jurgens 51, Andrew Vorhees 45, Roger Rosengarten 51, Chuma Edoga 6, Carson Vinson 2 Lamar Jackson’s much-awaited return lasted just one play before he suffered a thumb injury, which sidelined him for the rest of the game. Then, backup Tyler Huntley exited the game after 10 snaps with a toe injury, opening the door for No. 3 quarterback Joe Fagnano to play the final 40 offensive reps under center. In the backfield, Justice Hill’s 25 snaps slightly exceeded Derrick Henry’s total (23). It was a surprising zero-catch day for Zay Flowers, who was targeted five times in 42 snaps. Rashod Bateman played three less snaps than Flowers and caught one pass, as did Ja’Kobi Lane (33 snaps). Since returning from injury, Lane has clearly assumed the No. 3 wide receiver role, relegating Devontez Walker to a reduced snap count (8 plays). The snap breakdown at tight end was more of the same as well, with Mark Andrews leading the group in playing time (29 snaps). Matthew Hibner had zero catches again in 21 snaps, while Josh Cuevas caught one pass for 15 yards in only 13 snaps. Blocking tight end Nick Vannett recorded 11 reps on offense. On the offensive line, Andrew Vorhees got the start at right guard over Emery Jones Jr. and played 45 snaps. The other five starters all played the entire game (51 snaps). Backups Chuma Edoga and Carson Vinson combined to play eight snaps between the two of them. Defense DL: Nnamdi Madubuike 56, Travis Jones 47, Broderick Washington 37, Calais Campbell 27, John Jenkins 26 EDGE: Trey Hendrickson 48, Mike Green 47, Zion Young 35, Ethan Burke 34 ILB: Roquan Smith 52, Trenton Simpson 52, Teddye Buchanan 44 CB: Nate Wiggins 53, Marlon Humphrey 46, Chidobe Awuzie 43, T.J. Tampa 22, Keyon Martin 20 S: Malaki Starks 77, Kyle Hamilton 78, K’Von Wallace 47, Keondre Jackson 12 The Ravens’ defense played 82 total snaps against the Bills as the offense had multiple turnovers and short drives, forcing them to get back on the field. As a result, several players saw elevated snap counts compared to previous weeks, such as defensive backs K’Von Wallace (47 snaps) and Chidobe Awuzie (43 snaps), and front seven players Ethan Burke (34 snaps) and Broderick Washington (37). Nnamdi Madubuike once again paced the front seven in playing time with Travis Jones playing the second-most snaps behind him. Madubuike had a half-sack and two quarterback hits, which led the team. In his season-high 37 snaps, Washington corralled his first career interception. Campbell and Jenkins combined to play 53 snaps. Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green were neck-and-neck in snaps at edge rusher, followed by Zion Young and Burke — who were also just one snap apart. Roquan Smith exited the game briefly with an injury but returned to play 52 total snaps, racking up 11 tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. Teddye Buchanan saw his most action of the season with 44 snaps at linebacker. At cornerback, T.J. Tampa returned from injury and played 22 snaps, jumping Keyon Martin slightly in playing time. Nate Wiggins matched his snap total from last week (53), while Awuzie almost tied Marlon Humphrey in plays. Malaki Starks and Kyle Hamilton were the only defensive players with greater than 56 snaps, nearly going the distance.

title: What position should the Buffalo Bills target at NFL trade deadline?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. Now 6-1 and currently in first place in the AFC, the Buffalo Bills appear to be a team serious about its intent under new head coach […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Joe Brady of the Buffalo Bills looks on from the sideline against the Baltimore Ravens at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. Now 6-1 and currently in first place in the AFC, the Buffalo Bills appear to be a team serious about its intent under new head coach Joe Brady. It’s the team’s first change at head coach in nearly a decade, which brings with it a complete overhaul in defensive scheme. To this point, the offense has been as advertised thanks to the continued relationship between quarterback Josh Allen and Brady, who remains the team’s play caller. It’s the defense that has a lot of people scratching their heads week to week. At least that was true until the Bills’ Week 8 thrashing of the Baltimore Ravens. Though grains of salt are well-advised when considering the way Buffalo’s defense played last Sunday, they did look far more competent as a cohesively operating unit. What everyone wants to know right now is if the defense has turned the corner. It’s impossible to say that’s true given the situation in Week 8, but the results at least paint a promising picture of what could be in store later in the season. New defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard promised a more aggressive system, and he delivered on it against the Ravens. Considering all of that, it’s likely the Bills could stand to add talent in a few places on the roster before the trade deadline expires. Is the offense set, or would it make sense to bring in a viable wide receiver option to counter injuries? Most would agree that defense is the way to go, and maybe more than one player. What position makes the most sense? Is it someone at linebacker, or are they set with Terrel Bernard, Dorian, Williams, and to a lesser extent Kaleb Elarms-Orr leading the way? You may believe the play is to find a new starting option at safety with veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson now released by the Bills. Safety Damar Hamlin received the start in Gardner-Johnson’s place and he played a great game. Is Hamlin the team’s long-term plan at the position? Perhaps you have other plans, and want them to consider adding a player at a different position. Bills Mafia were pretty vocal about missing out on defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. Tell us what you think about where the Bills should add ahead of the trade deadline. Plus, has your confidence in the direction of the team changed following the results of Week 8 and their decision to move on from CJGJ? Vote now! What position should the Bills target? title: Buffalo Bills release C.J. Gardner-Johnson, what’s next in safety room?
summary: Another short-lived stint on a new team for C.J Gardner-Johnson, as the Buffalo Bills have released the mercurial safety following his one-game suspension for spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the team in March to a one-year, $3.5 million deal. And now he’s no longer a member of Bills. Jordan […]
full_text: Another short-lived stint on a new team for C.J Gardner-Johnson, as the Buffalo Bills have released the mercurial safety following his one-game suspension for spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. Gardner-Johnson was signed by the team in March to a one-year, $3.5 million deal. And now he’s no longer a member of Bills. Jordan Schultz was first on the report of Gardner-Johnson’s release: Sources: The #Bills are releasing safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson. Gardner-Johnson, who has started 6 games for Buffalo, did not play on Sunday due to a 1-game suspension for a spitting incident in the Raiders game. pic.twitter.com/X1a5G48J08 — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) November 3, 2026 After his first three NFL seasons on the Saints, the team that drafted him, since the beginning of the 2022 campaign, Gardner-Johnson has been on the Eagles, Lions, Eagles, Texans, Bears, and Bills, and has yet to stay with any of those teams for consecutive seasons. Beyond his on-field antics, Gardner-Johnson, who’ll turn 29 in December, had seriously problems tackling while in Buffalo. In fact, entering Week 9, his 25.7% missed tackle rate was the highest in the NFL among qualifying safeties. In six games for the Bills, the former University of Florida star had 26 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception. This news isn’t overly surprising, and not just because of the suspension. Buffalo has gotten quality production from Damar Hamlin next to Cole Bishop this season — 23 tackles, one pass breakup, and a 4.2% missed tackle rate. Beyond him, they just saw veteran Geno Stone make a big impact in his short audition against the Ravens in Week 8, as he led the team with six tackles on just 19 snaps, and there are two large, explosive youngsters waiting in the wings, Jalon Kilgore and Jordan Hancock, the latter of whom presumably will be activated from IR relatively soon. Also, versatile defensive back Te’Cory Couch played a fine game against the Ravens , can man the slot, or be deployed at safety if need be. Also, the trade deadline is a week from today on November 10, and there’s been plenty of speculation about the Bills adding veteran safety to pair with Bishop. Much like for his past teams, Buffalo’s Gardner-Johnson experiment did not work out.

title: Behind the Shades: My story and unexpected journey into a Bills Mafia docuseries
summary: When I started traveling around the country following the Buffalo Bills, I never imagined it would lead to being featured in a documentary. Yet, here we are. On October 21, Just One Before I Die, a five-part docuseries about Bills Mafia, premiered on Tubi. The series follows some of the most recognizable personalities in Bills Mafia, […]
full_text: When I started traveling around the country following the Buffalo Bills, I never imagined it would lead to being featured in a documentary. Yet, here we are. On October 21, Just One Before I Die , a five-part docuseries about Bills Mafia, premiered on Tubi. The series follows some of the most recognizable personalities in Bills Mafia, exploring their traditions, their dedication, and the relationships that make this fan base so unique. And somehow, I ended up being one of them. Not because I jump through tables, wear an elaborate costume, or cover myself in ketchup and mustard. Apparently, attending an unreasonable number of consecutive Buffalo Bills games was enough to get someone’s attention. How Did I Get Myself Into This? People often ask me how this whole consecutive-game streak started. Was it something I planned? Was I trying to break a record? Not even close. It really started in 2017, when I decided to get my season tickets back. My friend Adrian eventually began encouraging me to travel to more away games. At the time, I struggled with the idea of attending games in opposing stadiums. Mentally, I just wasn’t prepared for it. I couldn’t handle the heckling, and I definitely wasn’t comfortable sitting alone. By 2018, I had attended almost every home game and finally added a couple of away games. In 2019, I started traveling even more. Then came 2020. COVID hit, stadiums were empty, and suddenly the thing I’d grown to love was gone. I was absolutely CRAVING a football game and couldn’t wait until fans were allowed back in the stands for the playoffs. That’s when I realized I might have a problem. By 2021, my son was heading off to college, and I figured, why not try attending an entire season? Just one season. How hard could it be? Kenny “Pinto Ron” Johnson actually warned me. “Don’t do it. It gets addicting.” Naturally, I respectfully ignored him. Turns out he was right. Don’t tell him I said that. Somewhere along the way, I’d become addicted. Not just to watching the Bills play live, but to everything that came with it. The traveling, the tailgating, the friendships created, the adventures, and the excitement of experiencing a different city every week. I still don’t enjoy the heckling, but I’ve definitely developed thicker skin. And these days, I often find myself sitting alone without giving it a second thought. Looking back, I missed three random games in the 2019 season, or my streak would actually be quite a bit longer. And now here we are, years later, with a consecutive-game streak now sitting at 108, a documentary appearance, a bank account that probably hates me, and absolutely no indication that I’ve learned my lesson. The Docuseries Started With Pinto Ron Unbeknownst to me, Pinto Ron had mentioned my consecutive-game streak to the documentary’s production crew. The filmmakers were already traveling around the country capturing stories about Bills Mafia when our paths crossed in Los Angeles. That game happened to be my 75th consecutive Bills game. Pinto Ron introduced me to the crew, and they asked if they could interview me. Sure. Why not? It’s not like I had any idea what I was getting myself into. The following week, I spotted them again in Detroit. I actually had to remind them who I was, but they asked for another interview. At one point, I hadn’t heard from them in a while, and I found out they were conducting in-home and in-studio interviews with other people. I was certain they’d experienced enough of me. I even joked with several of the people they were following, “I’m just not good at the interviews. I don’t think I’m interesting enough.” Over time, though, we continued running into each other at games and tailgates. Since they were following so many of my friends, our paths crossed constantly. And somewhere along the way, I think we became friends. Just when I’d finally accepted that I probably wouldn’t be doing another interview… They mic’d me up again. Then came consecutive game No. 99 and all the emotions surrounding the final game at “the Ralph.” Eventually, the production team asked whether I’d be interested in having my 100th consecutive game featured in the documentary. Of course, I said yes. But I almost immediately regretted it. Following me around all day? I’m pretty superstitious, and I’m definitely social. How was this going to affect my game-day routine? What about my morning? What about the tailgate? But I also knew this was an opportunity most fans would dream of. Which is funny, considering how nervous I get when someone puts a camera in front of my face. When I tell you I’m awkward… I mean it! It’s not self deprecating, it’s true. You’d think someone who has spent years hosting podcasts, interviewing people, and talking about football would be comfortable being interviewed herself. You would be wrong. Very wrong. Some of that probably stems from my weight loss journey. It’s now been just over 10 years of the ups and downs of losing and trying to keep off 120 pounds. But I often still see myself negatively still, or fear being judged. But at my worst weight, I hid, I didn’t want anyone to see how I let myself go. I even canceled my season tickets for a couple years during the drought because I was afraid of seeing people I knew and being judged. Hours of Footage, Four Minutes of Usable Content Over the course of production, I ended up being filmed quite a bit, probably more than I even realized, since the cameras were constantly rolling around so many people I knew. They followed me through multiple games, tailgates, and milestone moments, including consecutive games 99 through 101. We eventually returned for final studio interviews in March 2026. And while I absolutely loved the experience, I’m fairly certain I tested the patience of the production team more than once. Here’s something I learned about documentary interviews. They’re not necessarily conducted like traditional interviews. Instead of simply answering a question, you’re often asked to incorporate the question into your response so the finished footage can stand on its own. Sounds simple enough, right? Apparently not for me. I constantly forgot how I was supposed to answer. Then there was the question of where I was supposed to look. At the camera? At the person asking the question? Somewhere slightly off to the side? I swear I needed a GPS just to figure out where my eyeballs were supposed to go. And I talk with my hands. A LOT. What in the world was I supposed to do with them? I eventually joked with the crew that they probably had hours of footage of me and about four minutes they could actually use. And honestly, that might have been generous. But the production team was incredibly patient, even when I wasn’t making their jobs particularly easy. Well, patient most of the time. Because there were definitely a few moments when they had entirely too much fun at my expense. When “Torpedo Dan” Called Me Out One of my favorite memories from filming involved a question I should have been able to answer without thinking. The crew asked how long I planned to continue my consecutive-game streak. I started talking about wanting to visit every NFL stadium, continuing until the Bills finally won a Super Bowl, and all the other goals I’d set for myself. And while those things are absolutely true, I realized afterward that I’d started giving the answer I thought the filmmakers wanted to hear. Not necessarily the answer I give every single week. Fortunately, my brother from another mother, Norm “Torpedo Dan” Brumfield, was there to remind me. He looked at me and essentially said, “Tell them the truth. Tell them what you say every week.” “When the bank account says NOPE… DECLINED… THAT’S A NO!” And he was absolutely right. Because as much as I’d love to tell everyone I’m going to keep attending Bills games until they win a Super Bowl, or until I hit the numbers “Mama J” or “Pinto Ron” have reached, there’s a very real financial component to this little…

summary: Welcome to the newest edition of the Weekly Stat Review! Another week, another painful viewing experience for fans of the Carolina Panthers. As is par for the course for Thursday Night Football, it was sloppy and potentially the least entertaining game of the week. That said, it also marked the last game as the Defensive […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Tucker Kraft #85 of the Green Bay Packers avoids a tackle from Marco Wilson #35 of the Carolina Panthers during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to the newest edition of the Weekly Stat Review! Another week, another painful viewing experience for fans of the Carolina Panthers . As is par for the course for Thursday Night Football, it was sloppy and potentially the least entertaining game of the week. That said, it also marked the last game as the Defensive Coordinator for Ejiro Evero, so this week’s stat review will be interesting to look back upon a few weeks from now to see if the trends shift at all after Evero’s departure and through the beginning of Todd Wash’s tenure. title: Taking stock of the Panthers cornerback room following the firing of Ejiro Evero
summary: Hello CSR! We’re coming off a wild week following the most recent Panthers loss to the Packers, one that saw them decide to jettison defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. It was quite a jarring move to make in the middle of a season where despite a myriad of injuries […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 18: DeVonta Smith #6 of the Philadelphia Eagles catches a touchdown pass against Will Lee III #24 of the Carolina Panthers in the fourth quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on October 18, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Panthers defeated the Eagles 25-14. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! We’re coming off a wild week following the most recent Panthers loss to the Packers, one that saw them decide to jettison defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. It was quite a jarring move to make in the middle of a season where despite a myriad of injuries along the defense, the Panthers still have a shot at the playoffs. As far as the Evero firing goes, I still haven’t quite settled on how I feel about it. I think I am currently leaning towards that it makes sense, but probably should have happened following the 2025 season rather than spending the 2026 off-season building around the scheme Evero would use. There were many questionable personnel decisions like not playing 2025 standout UDFA Corey Thornton or 3rd year CB Chau Smith-Wade, along with subbing out some of the younger guys with upside like Princely Umanmielen when the pass rush has struggled. All in all, I think the decision ultimately makes logical sense and I am looking forward to seeing what kind of changes the Panthers make post-Evero to try and right the ship, or at the very least keep it floating with duct tape until they get back Jaycee Horn, Mike Jackson, and Jaelan Phillips. The biggest question mark moving forward is going to be what the team does with their depleted CB room. Recently brought back coach and former cornerback DeAngelo Hall will have his work cut out for him. Let’s take a look at the current room as it stands. Will Lee III The 2026 4th round pick became the de facto CB1 following the injuries to Horn and Jackson. He’s logged 7 pass deflections in 7 games played and continues to progress after being thrown right into the fire. The Panthers planned on him being heavily involved early, as he manned one of the boundary spots in nickel formations when the cornerback room was fully healthy. Unfortunately, he is day to day right now with a hamstring injury, which means they may miss him for at least a game, possibly more depending on how his recovery goes. Not great, but the experience he’s getting this season as a 4th round rookie should prove very valuable from a long term perspective. Chau Smith-Wade The former 5th round pick played quite a bit since his rookie season in 2024. He’s played in 36 career games with 11 starts, though curiously his defensive snap counts went down this season following a career high 63% of snaps played on defense in 2025. This season, he’s only accounted for 21% of the defensive snaps, playing almost as many snaps on special teams (86) as he has on defense (88). This is a very curious decision considering all of the injuries surrounding this position group. However, that could change this week, especially if Will Lee can’t go. The Panthers primarily used Chau as a nickel corner, so prior to Evero’s firing, they were playing with additional safeties rather than with as much traditional nickel sets. I think if you’re looking to change the fortunes of the secondary, this is the week to throw him out there and see what happens. And that’s if they even have a choice pending Will Lee’s status. Malcolm DeWalt IV DeWalt, the final member of the active roster on this list, was brought in on the practice squad on October 24th, and promoted to the active roster ahead of the Packers game last week. He was an undrafted free agent this season, made the 53 man roster for the Atlanta Falcons, but was ultimately waived in October after being a healthy scratch for six games. He made one special teams tackle last week and played no defensive snaps. He played for 3 different colleges prior to entering the NFL, so I don’t really know what to expect from him should they be forced to play him this week. Practice Squad options The Panthers (as of this writing, per their team site) have 5 corners on their practice squad. They released Robert Rochell on Tuesday. Most likely, they will be calling up 2 or 3 of them for Sundays game depending on what happens with Will Lee. The first one I have to highlight is Marco Wilson. He’s a former 4th round pick from 2021 who has bounced around the league before landing on the Panthers practice squad on October 6th. He was called on to start against the Packers, being credited with 2 pass deflections and 8 total tackles. Of course, the Panthers defense was still not great in that game as the Packers tore them apart in the passing game, but it was an impressive showing for Wilson and I’d expect him to get called up again and possibly start this week. Next, we have 2025 UDFA Corey Thornton. Thornton was an impressive preseason story and played in 12 games for the Panthers in 2025, and managed to break in to the corner rotation before a broken fibula ended his season. Curiously, he hasn’t been called up at all during the Panthers injury woes from the practice squad. That might change this week depending on what kind of changes the Panthers are making and what options they have for significant playing time. Rounding out the last of the names is DeVonta Smith, Zion Childress, and Caelen Carson. Smith spent the entire off-season on the roster before being waived during final roster cuts and being added to the practice squad, so he has about as much familiarity as you could ask for from an undrafted rookie. Childress had stints with the Cowboys and Texans since entering as a UDFA in 2025. Carson was drafted in the 5th round pick by the Cowboys in 2024, and has 8 starts in his career. He could very well see some time depending on what decisions the Panthers make during the near future of the post-Evero defense. In closing, the Panthers have some… interesting decisions to make going into their next few games. It doesn’t appear they will be looking for cornerback help outside of the usual roster churning of the NFL season, which makes sense for a team that hasn’t made a ton of trades during the season under Dave Canales. I could see a low risk/low price move potentially being made, but dealing a high pick or even mid round pick for a corner doesn’t seem to be something they will consider. Personally, I’d really like to see them give Chau Smith-Wade and Corey Thornton some opportunities, and I was impressed with Marco Wilson despite getting thrown out there with less than a month under his belt in this scheme. Caelen Carson could also see some time. But either way, they’ll have do a lot of things schematically to mask this weakness currently. They may look to play more man coverage and press to change things up, or they may sit back in the same soft cushion zones we have grown accustomed to. Maybe some calculated aggression in coverage will help? What are your thoughts, Panthers fans?

title: Panthers vs Packers game review: Time to pivot
summary: The midway point of the NFL season is fast approaching, and the Carolina Panthers are not trending in the right direction. After 2 losses in 5 days, the magic ran out quickly and the plucky media darlings with an explosive offense have turned back into the pumpkin we all know and begrudgingly love. With all […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers runs the ball against Tre'von Moehrig #7 of the Carolina Panthers during the second quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The midway point of the NFL season is fast approaching, and the Carolina Panthers are not trending in the right direction. After 2 losses in 5 days, the magic ran out quickly and the plucky media darlings with an explosive offense have turned back into the pumpkin we all know and begrudgingly love. With all the evidence of Ejiro Evero’s tenure as the Defensive Coordinator, another loss in embarrassing fashion was enough to force Dave Canales’ hand to go in a different direction. While Evero has plenty of supporters within league circles that sing his praises and tout his merit as a coach, the consistency of the the defense’s inconsistency wore too thin. If there was ever a time to makes these changes it’s now, as despite everything, the Panthers are still in the lead for the NFC South title. As we all know, the NFC South counts as a division the same way that Thursday Night Football counts as primetime: barely. Anything can happen, and I’m not sure if that’s actually a good thing. While many different areas of the Panthers flailing, it’s the defense that is in the most desperate need of some change. On Thursday, Packers quarterback Jordan Love dropped back 41 times. The Panthers did not register a single quaterback hit, let alone a sack. If they were playing drop 8 coverage the entire game, then fine. But no, they also blitzed 44% of the time, according to SumerSports. The Panthers had a 44% blitz rate and did not sack Jordan Love That is the 4th highest blitz rate without generating a sack in a game this season, per @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) October 30, 2026 According to NFL’s NextGenStats, Jordan Love had a 2.47 second time to throw. So maybe he was just getting the ball out quickly underneath? Well, Love had the 10th highest average completed air yards (6.4 yards) in the NFL and the 5th highest intended air yards (9.8 yards) during Week 8. To the Panthers credit, they were able to hold the Packer’s to a pretty dismal rushing day. I’d like to give kudos, but I have a hard time reconciling that the Panthers had to sell out to stop the rushing attack of the league’s worst rushing team in order to find that success. Granted, when you are among the league’s worst rushing defense, maybe that’s what is necessary. Maybe they do have to sell out to stop the run and everything else be damned regardless of opponent or circumstance? Who knows, but hopefully a new defensive coordinator can help figure it out. If the Panthers do want to win the NFC South crown and make more than a whimper in the playoffs, it’s not going to happen if they stay as the defense ranked 28th in points per game, 22nd in yards per game, 30th in rush defense, 30th in pressure rate, 28th in 3rd down stop rate and dead last in the NFL in red zone stop rate. If you’re going to be bend-but-don’t-break, the ‘don’t break’ part is a crucial component. Being 4th in takeaways is nice, at least. Hopefully that sticks around. I guess we’ll find something soon, when the Panthers take on the Denver Broncos. Until then, keep pounding.

title: 5 Bears Takes: A Blockbuster, a Blowout, and Trade Deadline Thoughts
summary: It may have been 10 days since the Chicago Bears last played a game. Still, the front office kept things interesting on Thursday when they executed a blockbuster deal to bring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago ahead of next week’s trade deadline. With the added momentum of a two-game winning streak and a […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks guard Quenton Nelson (53) and Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (99) meet after the game at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It may have been 10 days since the Chicago Bears last played a game. Still, the front office kept things interesting on Thursday when they executed a blockbuster deal to bring All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to Chicago ahead of next week’s trade deadline. With the added momentum of a two-game winning streak and a much-needed mini-bye week in the rearview mirror, a potential preview of the NFC Championship Game happened on Monday night in Seattle. Despite playing on the road, the Bears once again showed that they are one of the best teams in the league, moving to 6-2 on the season following a 34-17 dominating win in front of the 12s. Caleb Williams became the first quarterback in eight games this season to eclipse the 200-yard passing mark against the Seahawks defense. All in all, it was a great week for this team, and they’ve got just one more game until their Week 10 bye. Going 3-0 against the Falcons, Patriots, and Seahawks is extremely impressive. Before we turn the page on the crazy week that was, let’s relive the fun and look ahead to the trade deadline in under a week. All of that and more in Week 8’s installment of 10 Bears Takes. 1. On Thursday morning, general manager Ryan Poles swung for the fences, sending a pair of first-round picks to the Tennessee Titans for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons– more on why this signals the Bears “going for it” in 2026 and what that means moving forward. If you’re like me, you were minding your own business on a rather ordinary Thursday morning when all of a sudden, the Twitter notifications came flying in. News broke that the Bears were sending their 2027 first- and fourth-round picks, plus a 2028 first-round pick, to the Titans for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-rounder. Like usual, a trade of this magnitude sent shockwaves around the league, prompting all sorts of responses from analysts. Ultimately, Poles and his front office paid a high price for Simmons, and that’s hard to debate. On the flip side, they were in desperate need of an impact defensive lineman, and that’s exactly what the 29-year-old All-Pro provides. Another factor in this trade and the price paid is that Simmons recently signed a three-year extension, which means the Titans have already paid a chunk of his contract, helping the cap hits moving forward. Here’s how each year’s cap hit looks moving forward: 2026: $7.94 million 2027: $22.55 million (all guarantees and dead money run out after this season) 2028: $30.9 million 2029: $29.1 million 2030: $33.1 million The next year and a half come cheap, especially considering his production. Although the last three years of the deal become considerably more expensive, this is where the Bears are highly likely to exercise a restructure (or two) on top of adding void years to lower his cap hit. Simply put, Simmons is one of, if not the best, interior defensive linemen in the game. His 15.5 sacks since the start of last season are the most in the NFL, and he’s top of the league in sacks, tackles, pressure percentage, and disruption EPA for a defensive tackle. In addition to his great pass-rushing numbers, he’s very good against the run and has the versatility to be used all over the defensive line. Although the defensive line is far from “fixed,” adding an elite player like Simmons should have a similar trickle-down effect as it did when they traded for Khalil Mack in 2018. He’ll make everyone better around him, and should take most of the double teams off players like Montez Sweat and Austin Booker. This is a “multiplier” move that should be felt across the defense. More importantly, this big swing signals something clear: The Bears believe they are Super Bowl contenders and are operating as such. Cap space, both now and in the future, will always be a big talking point, but given how much flexibility they have with cuts and restructures next year, they are still in good shape for the next offseason. Obviously, missing their first-round picks for the next two years takes away some of the excitement on draft day and hurts their ability to add impact players through the draft; there was little chance they could find this type of impact player with either of their next two first-rounders. This move isn’t without risk, but given how the roster was built in previous offseasons, it was also a must. Finding elite defensive line talent isn’t easy, and this move guarantees production now and in the immediate future. 2. Giving up first-round picks should never be taken lightly, but in many ways, this is the Khalil Mack trade again, with much more certainty at quarterback and on the offensive side of the ball. Without going too far into the sore subject that was the 2018-2021 Chicago Bears, the decision to “go for it” with a big trade that cost multiple first-round picks is very similar. The good news is that this time around, they have a much more established quarterback situation, and Ben Johnson appears to be the real deal. Although that reduces some of the risk in a big trade like this, the history of deals involving multiple first-round picks typically doesn’t favor the team acquiring the superstar. In theory, the Bears would have been able to find their three technique of the future eventually, but you’d have to go back to the Akiem Hicks days for that to be a reality. Instead, the team has flailed around with different coaching staffs and the same disappointing results. Some might point to trading Gervon Dexter Sr. as a mistake, and while that might be true, it’s also worth mentioning that he wasn’t the fit for what Dennis Allen wants at defensive tackle. Sure, the two players have some similar numbers on paper, but there’s a chance that Simmons has been doing this at a high level for close to half a decade. There will always be inherent risk in a move like this, but if all goes well, both first-rounders they give up will be later in the round. Thus, the variance for those picks will be much higher than it would be if they were in the Top 10. Obviously, there’s a chance something goes horribly wrong, and they end up handing the Titans a Top 10-15 pick, but that’s the risk assessment when a deal like this is made. The reality is quite simple for this team. They’ve had multiple swings at fixing the issue and failed. Finding a star defensive lineman gets harder the later they go in the first round. Simmons is a guaranteed stud, and barring injury, should continue to produce at a high level for close to the life of his contract. This does increase the pressure on Poles and his front office to draft well on Day 2, but ultimately, the pressure was already there to a certain extent. Sometimes teams have to take risks to reach their goals, and for the Bears, this was a worthy swing. In terms of cap flexibility, the team will have plenty of restructure or extension options on players during the offseason, not to mention the multiple veteran players like Jaylon Johnson, Grady Jarrett, T.J. Edwards, and one, if not both, of Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo that could be cut before the start of next offseason. We already knew the defense would need an overhaul starting in March, but adding a player like Simmons helps with the heavy lifting needed in the coming months. For now, fans can enjoy what should be a drastically improved unit, and the front office and coaching staff can use the next 10-plus games to properly evaluate the veterans listed above. 3. Even following the Simmons trade, the Bears should still be active in their search for additional defensive help– how things could look over the next week leading up to the trade deadline. So far, all reports suggest that the Bears will continue to scour the market for additional help on the…

title: Chicago Bears Pass Protection Analysis on the Sack Allowed vs Seahawks
summary: In the first two games since Caleb Williams returned, the Chicago Bears’ pass protection allowed 4 sacks to the Atlanta Falcons and then 3 to the New England Patriots. It’s not bad, and in context, I thought the pass protection was solid in each game, but it was still a much higher sack rate than […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts at the line against the Seattle Seahawks during the first quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the first two games since Caleb Williams returned, the Chicago Bears’ pass protection allowed 4 sacks to the Atlanta Falcons and then 3 to the New England Patriots. It’s not bad, and in context, I thought the pass protection was solid in each game, but it was still a much higher sack rate than a season ago, when he averaged just 1.4 per game. The Seattle Seahawks defense featured 5 players with multiple sacks through their first seven games, and with the Week 8 matchup in loud Lumen Field in Seattle, I figured their defense would get the best of Chicago’s pass protection scheme a few times. But the Bears only allowed 1 sack to Seattle’s vaunted defense, and I’ll break it down right here. Sack 19: 4th Quarter: 2-10-CHI 23 (14:02) (Shotgun) C.Williams sacked at CHI 13 for -10 yards (M.Morris) After Caleb faked to D’Andre Swift, he looked downfield at Luther Burden III (outside the right hash), but he felt pressure off the left so fast because left tackle Theo Benedet was walked back into the pocket. Caleb drifted right and looked to Swift in the left flat, but didn’t have a clear throwing lane. Benedet did a nice job staying between his guy and his quarterback, but the problem was the depth he gave up, so even though his guy didn’t get the sack, he’s the reason this play was blown up. If Benedet offered up just a bit more resistance, Williams could have hit one of his three checkdowns (probably Colston Loveland over the middle), but there wasn’t time to get through his progressions. It looked like Swift was going to chip if Benedet’s guy took an outside rush. He got a small piece of the defender on the way to the flat, but with the Seattle rush end square to Benedet, there wasn’t enough for Swift to hit Benedet set up inside first, then kicked out for the edge defender. In theory, that inside step would normally entice a defender to go around the edge, exposing his outside shoulder for Swift to target on his chip release and leaving Benedet in a good position as the defender redirected his rush inside. But the Seattle defender had his mind made up to bull rush on the play. Benedet likely didn’t expect it and was driven back. Caleb was forced out of the pocket and ended up even with left guard Joe Thuney, who pulled right to block the edge after a Loveland release. Mike Morris (#94) just reached out and grabbed Williams before delivering the belly-to-back suplex. The Bears did a good job mixing up the tempo and identifying the Seattle defenders all night long, which is hard to do Here’s the individual Sackwatch tally after eight games: Caleb Williams – 4.5 Sacks happen – 3 Garrett Bradbury – 3 Theo Benedet – 2.5 Ozzy Trapilo – 2 Jonah Jackson – 1 Colston Loveland – 1 Tyson Bagent – 1 Darnell Wright – 1 Historical Sackwatch after eight weeks of action. 2010 – 32 Martz 2011 – 21 Martz 2012 – 28 Tice 2013 – 12 Trestman 2014 – 20 Trestman 2015 – 14 Gase 2016 – 14 Loggains 2017 – 19 Loggains 2018 – 17 Nagy 2019 – 22 Nagy 2020 – 20 Nagy 2021 – 30 Nagy 2022 – 31 Getsy 2023 – 28 Getsy 2024 – 23 Waldron 2025 – 12 Johnson 2026 – 19 Johnson

title: How confident are you in the Bears and in Caleb Williams moving forward?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. The Chicago Bears have won three straight games in the most impressive fashion imaginable. Caleb Williams is the 1st quarterback in Bears history to lead his […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) calls a play at the line of scrimmage against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bears fans and fans across the country. The Chicago Bears have won three straight games in the most impressive fashion imaginable. Caleb Williams is the 1st quarterback in Bears history to lead his team to 30+ points in three consecutive games with no turnovers. The Bears also never trailed in any of these three games, and that 3-game streak of scoring 30 points while never trailing is tied for the second-longest streak in franchise history . They went four in a row three times, all in the 1940s (1941, 1942, and 1948). Those teams were led by Hall of Fame quarterback Sid Luckman, who is the only quarterback to win a league MVP for the Bears. There was some buzz around Williams as an MVP candidate before the season, and that was amplified following the Bears’ 59-point explosion in Week 1, but the hamstring injury seemed to derail that because it kept him out of the next three games. In his weekly NFL MVP Tracker at NFL.com , Kevin Patra wrote about the historical unlikelihood of Williams winning it. In the post NFL-AFL merger era (since 1970) in non-strike-shortened seasons, only one player has missed three games and still won the NFL MVP award: Joe Montana in 1989. Cool Joe battled through various injuries that season, missing Weeks 6, 8, and 15, and portions of others. While a long shot, the Bears did just beat last year’s Super Bowl participants in back-to-back weeks on primetime. They also have three more stand-alone games on the schedule, including a third straight primetime affair this Sunday. Patra also explained why Montana’s performance in 1989 won it that year and how Caleb could have a similar path. Despite missing three games, Montana was the best QB on the best team in the NFL, winning the MVP vote in a landslide (62 of 70 votes). The 49ers QB overcame the lack of counting stats by leading the NFL in all the efficiency categories: 70.2 percent completion rate, a 6.7 TD% rate, 53.7% success rate, 9.1 yards per attempt average, 270.8 yards per game, and set the then-record with a 112.4 passer rating — when 100 passer ratings were uncommon. That’s Williams’ path to the MVP: Be the most efficient passer on the best team. Caleb may not hit gaudy passing yard or touchdown numbers, but if all his other numbers are among the best in the NFL, while the Bears keep winning games, how could he not be a finalist? title: This time is different for the Chicago Bears
summary: The Chicago Bears’ blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons drew a lot of comparisons to their 2018 blockbuster trade for Khalil Mack. Both defenders were acquired to give a team with Super Bowl aspirations a boost, but the big difference is that this time the franchise knows exactly who they are with Ben Johnson and Caleb […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a win against the Seattle Seahawks with teammate Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears’ blockbuster trade for Jeffery Simmons drew a lot of comparisons to their 2018 blockbuster trade for Khalil Mack. Both defenders were acquired to give a team with Super Bowl aspirations a boost, but the big difference is that this time the franchise knows exactly who they are with Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams, while the 2018 team was headed into year one of Matt Nagy and year two of Mitchell Trubisky. There wasn’t proof of concept showing that Nagy/Mitch was the right pairing to lead the franchise to a championship. It was just hope. They hoped Trubisky would take a year-two leap. They hoped Nagy was the right guy for the job. They hoped the new look offense would gel and complement Vic Fangio’s defense. Whereas the Ben/Caleb pairing had a full year to cook, and part of 2026 to show improvement, which they did. This team was already firmly in the postseason mix thanks to the offense, so adding a game-wrecker to a well-coached Dennis Allen defense was a calculated gamble that made perfect sense. The Bears have a head coach/quarterback combo who can lead them to greatness and be mentioned in the same breath as Walsh/Montana and Reid/Mahomes. The nerds will try to use their spreadsheets to prove something about sustainability, regression, or some other dumb thing that can’t be measured. Analysts will point to history as to why this or that can’t happen. The haters will still try to poke holes no matter what their eyes tell them. But this time it’s different, and they know it.
