title: Detroit Lions create 2 roster spots, place Jimmy Rolder on IR
summary: On Tuesday, the Detroit Lions announced two roster moves, both creating vacant spots on the team’s 53-man roster. As expected, rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was placed on injured reserve after suffering what coach Dan Campbell called a season-ending injury. It was officially announced as a hamstring injury, and Campbell said surgery could be an option […]
full_text: Detroit Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder (41) celebrates a play against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Tuesday, the Detroit Lions announced two roster moves, both creating vacant spots on the team’s 53-man roster. As expected, rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was placed on injured reserve after suffering what coach Dan Campbell called a season-ending injury. It was officially announced as a hamstring injury, and Campbell said surgery could be an option for the former Wolverine. “Jimmy Rolder is going to require surgery, or he could. The point is this is a significant injury. He’ll be out for the season,” Campbell said on Monday. It’s a tough break for Rolder. He missed much of training camp with a hamstring injury, and Sunday was his first significant action on defense all year. In just 17 snaps, Rolder recorded five tackles, a sack, and another tackle for loss. Combined with the indefinite loss of Jack Campbell, the Lions are a bit shorthanded at linebacker. The other move the Lions made was waiving rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald. Undrafted in 2026, Fitzgerald was signed off the Steelers’ practice squad when the Lions were particularly vulnerable at the safety position. But with Brian Branch returning recently—although in concussion protocol this week—and with Kerby Joseph returning soon, Fitzgerald may have just been the odd man out. It’s worth noting that last week, Campbell indicated that Thomas Harper was nearing a return from injury , as well. With those two moves, the Lions now have two vacancies on the 53-man roster. One of those spots is expected to be taken by linebacker K.J Britt. On Monday, a report dropped that the Lions were signing the veteran special teamer off the Patriots’ practice squad , and Campbell confirmed it on his radio appearance on Tuesday. At this point, it isn’t clear what the Lions plan to do with the other open roster spot.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: NFL Week 9 power rankings: Lions’ rise continues but still have doubters
summary: The Detroit Lions (5-2) have now won three in a row and beaten NFC North rivals—the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8—in back-to-back games. The Lions’ balanced roster and adaptable coaching staff allow them to stay competitive with any opponent, and as we have seen in each of […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell reacts in front of quarterback Jared Goff (16) during the first quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions (5-2) have now won three in a row and beaten NFC North rivals—the Green Bay Packers in Week 7 and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8—in back-to-back games. The Lions’ balanced roster and adaptable coaching staff allow them to stay competitive with any opponent, and as we have seen in each of the three previous wins, they can beat an opponent in a variety of ways. Against the Cardinals, the Lions unleashed their passing attack; against the Packers, they controlled possessions and the clock; and last Sunday, they matched the Vikings’ aggression with an attacking run game and dominated on the ground. With each win, the Lions’ defense has steadily improved, though many national analysts are still looking at season-long stats instead of what they’ve done recently. In this week’s power rankings, the Lions moved up in every ranking; however, they’re still one holdout away from being a consensus top-10 team. Let’s take a closer look at this week’s national power rankings. Sports Illustrated: 4 ( Previous rank: 7) From Connor Orr : Drew Petzing has been on my ascending head coaches list but has put himself on many others after a sterling performance against the Vikings. Petzing managed to get the job done against Brian Flores and add a flourish, a particular feat that seems almost impossible given how talented this Minnesota defense is. NFL.com: 5 (Previous rank: 11) From Nick Shook : This might not age well, given the serious injury questions facing the Lions, but I’m giving them the boost because of how they finished their victory over the previously undefeated Vikings. Facing a 15-12 deficit in the fourth quarter, Detroit sliced right through Minnesota’s terrifying defense with apparent ease, leaning on Jahmyr Gibbs before finishing the drive with a beautiful touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Jameson Williams. The Lions won by sticking to their offensive identity, getting another encouraging showing from the defense and outlasting the Vikings in a victory that feels bigger than most. The Athletic: 7 (Previous rank: 9) From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall : Reality check: The defense is still a problem Detroit’s defensive EPA through eight weeks (minus-60.22) is the 16th-worst of any team in the last 10 years, according to TruMedia. Jahmyr Gibbs saved them Sunday by rushing for a career-best 99 yards after forcing a missed tackle, according to NextGenStats. He finished with 23 carries for 153 yards and now has more touchdowns in his first four seasons (59) than anyone other than Terrell Davis and LaDainian Tomlinson. USA Today: 7 (Previous rank: 11) From Nate Davis : Does there need to be concern about RB Jahmyr Gibbs’ usage at some point? He’s on pace for 464 touches, which would be the second-highest total in NFL history. (James Wilder had 492 in 1984.) Yahoo Sports: 8 (Previous rank: 10) From Frank Schwab : Biggest need: Defense, particularly at cornerback The Lions’ fan base wasn’t happy when the Cowboys overpaid to get cornerback Joey Porter Jr. in a trade. They know that cornerback is an issue and it seems hard to believe the deadline will pass without Detroit doing something at the position. Yet, there are other issues on a defense that has struggled most of the season, though it has allowed just 32 points the last two games. While the human element of linebacker Jack Campbell’s neck injury is overwhelming, and his recovery is the biggest part of that story, there is a football side to it as well. Detroit will presumably be without one of the best off-ball linebackers in the NFL indefinitely. While the team’s thoughts are primarily on their young star’s health, the Lions also have to deal with the reality of perhaps adding a linebacker before the deadline. CBS Sports: 9 (Previous rank: 10) From Pete Prisco : They beat the Packers and the Vikings in consecutive weeks in low-scoring games. That’s a new formula for this team to win games, but a good sign. ESPN: 9 (Previous rank: 11) From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard : Best in-season trade acquisition ever: DE Za’Darius Smith in 2024 The Lions have plenty of impactful offseason trades, including ones that helped them land quarterbacks in Jared Goff (2021) and Bobby Layne (1950). But the best in-season deal in terms of immediate impact likely goes to Smith. He had four sacks in eight regular-season games for the Lions, who had a team-record 15 wins and earned the NFC’s No. 1 seed in 2024. Detroit received Smith and a 2026 seventh-round draft selection from the Browns for a 2025 fifth-rounder and a 2026 sixth-rounder. Sporting News: 11 (Previous rank: 12) From Vinnie Iyer : The Lions have come through with huge back-to-back home division wins against the Packers and Vikings. The big surprise is the improved defense. After allowing an average of almost 30 points in the first five games, the Lions have given up only 32 total the past two weeks. They should keep up that play with the Dolphins in Miami next.
author: Erik Schlitt

title: Film study: Cade Mays is still the Detroit Lions’ best center
summary: The Detroit Lions are 2-0 in the division and on a three-game win streak after ending the Minnesota Vikings’ undefeated start to the 2026 season. While the score only resulted in a 19-15 final, the Lions racked up 230 yards rushing against the NFL’s premier defensive unit. Starting center Cade Mays entered the game in […]
full_text: Detroit Lions center Cade Mays (64) warms up ahead of the game between Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions are 2-0 in the division and on a three-game win streak after ending the Minnesota Vikings’ undefeated start to the 2026 season. While the score only resulted in a 19-15 final, the Lions racked up 230 yards rushing against the NFL’s premier defensive unit. Starting center Cade Mays entered the game in his second start of the season after suffering a fractured wrist in training camp. In his absence, backup Juice Scruggs had performed very well. Against Minnesota, Mays’ day was cut short after the first offensive possession in the second quarter , resulting in only 22 snaps played. Again, Scruggs filled in and played at a high level. With Mays in the game, the Lions only rushed for 31 yards. With Scruggs, the team captured the remaining 199 yards on the ground in just under three quarters of play. But correlation is not causation. For this film study, I went back to watch the all-22 film of all 22 of Mays’ snaps against the Vikings. The quick conclusion is this: Mays did not lose a single rep of his one-on-one matchups in either the run or pass game. Despite the various looks, pre-snap shifts, and varied simulated blitzes, Mays’ day was about as flawless as you could ask for. Below, I’ve clipped three plays that highlight the high-level play from Mays and capture the upside of what this offense can look like with him moving forward. Athleticism and strength in the run game The first play is an outside zone run play to the left. In the scheme, Mays is responsible for the gap to his left, but pre-snap there is no defender in the A-gap or even over the guard. The nearest defender is lined up in the B-gap as a 3-technique just outside of left guard Christian Mahogany. At the snap, the 3-technique defensive tackle stunts inside across Mahogany’s face and into Mays’ zone. Mays reaches the stunting defender, captures outside leverage by not stopping his feet at the point of contact, and continues to drive and strain through the whistle. The result: displacing the line of scrimmage for the soon-to-be MVP Jahmyr Gibbs to pick up a positive gain. Anchor and strain in pass protection The next play shown below highlights the size, strength, and finish Mays provides in the interior of the pocket for quarterback Jared Goff to rely on. At the snap, Mays absorbs and anchors against a strong bull rush from the defensive tackle, but once Goff steps up and the defender starts to swim out of his initial rush, Mays switches gears like a Ford F-150, driving his guy into the dirt once he gains leverage. If Goff had taken an extra moment to settle into the throw, the play could have resulted in Gibbs walking in for a touchdown. Mental processing and physical adaptation The final play highlighted below shows how Mays was able to mentally process the simulated pressure of the linebacker lined up as the 0-technique right over him and adjust when the blitz did not materialize. Not only does Mays make the initial recognition, but he is also able to adapt to pick up the presnap B-gap blitzing linebacker who stunts into the A-gap. From there, Mays picks up the defender and establishes leverage by moving his feet and hips to prevent the pocket from collapsing. The result is enough time for Goff to deliver the biggest explosive pass of the game, a 46-yard deep shot to Jameson Williams in stride. The aim of this film study was not to put down or dismiss Scruggs’ performance, which was very strong in its own right. In fact, Dan Campbell was asked on 97.1 about Scruggs and whether his quality play has started a competition at the center position. “… to get thrust back in there against that defense with everything that they were doing, to have that production, I mean, that was impressive. He was locked in. He was so ready to go. He was. I told you this before, we love Juice. He just fits us. He’s all about business, he’s a great teammate, he’s high-energy, he tries to finish plays, runs off the football. So he did a heck of a job. As of right now, he’s our guy, because I don’t see Cade practicing Wednesday and he might not Thursday. So we’re going to get Juice ready to go here.” At the end of the day, the Lions have two starting-caliber NFL centers on their roster. This is a huge credit to Brad Holmes for his effort in transforming the offensive line this offseason. The takeaway is clear, though. The ceiling for the Lions’ offense is highest with Cade Mays as the point man.
author: Anthony Balaj

title: Green Bay Packers News: Will the Packers be active at the trade deadline?
summary: We got one big early November Tuesday ordeal out of the way. Now the countdown is on for another one. The annual “will they/won’t they” dance that precedes the NFL trade deadline every year is in full swing, with various speculators wondering who the Packers should target and what, if anything, they should give up […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - AUGUST 28: General manager Brian Gutekunst of the Green Bay Packers looks on against the Arizona Cardinals during a preseason game at Lambeau Field on August 28, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images We got one big early November Tuesday ordeal out of the way. Now the countdown is on for another one. The annual “will they/won’t they” dance that precedes the NFL trade deadline every year is in full swing, with various speculators wondering who the Packers should target and what, if anything, they should give up to get them. The Packers are still in the aftermath of their last big trade, of course, which affects what they could do at this year’s trade deadline. They seem unlikely to give up any serious assets in the 2027 NFL Draft considering they don’t have a first round pick. But a lower-level trade might still be possible, especially if Gutekunst can get someone to bite on an offer involving 2028 assets. Even so, as cap-strapped as the Packers are, it doesn’t seem super likely they’re going to be buyers at this year’s deadline. And there’s little the Packers could sell off, either. Keisean Nixon and Carrington Valentine are probably their two most notable assets on expiring (and thus very movable) contracts, and I don’t think the Packers are in a position to jettison either one, even if Valentine has fallen out of favor this year. The safest bet seems like banking on this year being a quiet trade deadline. You’ll probably hear something about the Packers making calls or being in conversations, as always, but the chances of them landing a difference maker at the deadline seem low. title: Adam Stenavich explains the Kevin Zeitler situation
summary: The Green Bay Packers signed guard Kevin Zeitler, a former Wisconsin Badger and Pro Bowler, to a one-year, $4 million contract after the team’s poor start to the 2026 season. The team has since been able to protect quarterback Jordan Love better, but the run game hasn’t advanced much, and Zeitler has yet to take […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers signed guard Kevin Zeitler, a former Wisconsin Badger and Pro Bowler, to a one-year, $4 million contract after the team’s poor start to the 2026 season. The team has since been able to protect quarterback Jordan Love better, but the run game hasn’t advanced much, and Zeitler has yet to take an offensive snap for the team. After the game on Sunday, when the Packers surprisingly moved Laken Tomlinson to right guard, a position Tomlinson hadn’t played in about a decade, Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur stated that the team didn’t feel as though Tomlinson should have been benched, but they wanted to give Aaron Banks an opportunity at left guard. That was why Zeitler wasn’t getting burn, according to the head man. On Tuesday, Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich spoke to the media about the Zeitler situation, where he got a little more in-depth with his reasoning. This is what he had to say: Well, when we signed him, he was coming off an injury with his knee. So, it was kind of a question mark. It took him a few weeks to get to the point where he’s at right now, where he was kind of working his way back into it. What happened was Laken came in and really did a tremendous job, just coming in and really helping out our team and helping out our offensive line and really, you know, helping us, you know, becoming productive in a lot of senses. So, it just was one of those things where I thought he was going to come in and play, but Laken stepped up and did a nice job and it is what it is right now. Would I hesitate to put him in a game? No. I would not. He’s ready to play. So that’s sort of the story on Zeitler, for those wondering. Basically, the Zeitler opening ended up going to Tomlinson, at least for now. So far, Zeitler has played just 15 snaps for the Packers this season, all coming on the field goal protection unit. From left to right, the expected “preferred” offensive line for Green Bay moving forward is Jordan Morgan, Aaron Banks, Sean Rhyan, Laken Tomlinson and Anthony Belton — as Zach Bako-Bewele, the team’s starting right tackle, is on the injured reserve with a full patellar tendon tear. Rhyan is currently dealing with an injury, which has led to John Williams taking over at center — as the second-team option, Jacob Monk, is also on the injured reserve. Beyond those players, the Packers also roster Zeitler, Travis Glover (missed last week with an injury), Jager Burton, Donovan Jennings and Mekhi Becton Sr. Glover, Burton and Jennings have all gotten offensive looks in the regular season this year, while Becton was just called up from the practice squad last week.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Matthew Golden is putting together a wild second season
summary: Matthew Golden is pretty much always open and usually he can do something about it. That’s about as positive a spin as I can put on the Packers’ second-year wide receiver’s ongoing problems with drops. On the one hand, you have to be open a lot to have as many opportunities to drop passes as […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Matthew Golden #0 of the Green Bay Packers makes a catch and scores a touchdown against the Carolina Panthers during an NFL football game at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matthew Golden is pretty much always open and usually he can do something about it. That’s about as positive a spin as I can put on the Packers’ second-year wide receiver’s ongoing problems with drops. On the one hand, you have to be open a lot to have as many opportunities to drop passes as Golden has. On the other hand…man, that’s a lot of dropped passes. Most, if not all, of the writers in the APC stable were still pretty high on Golden even after his disappointing rookie year, and I think we all figured he’d have something of a redemption tour this year. But this is about as strange a second year as you could imagine. Golden has been legitimately great at times, but his struggles with doing the most basic thing you can ask of a receiver would be funny if they weren’t so frustrating. You gotta catch the ball! That’s like 95% of the job, maybe more! And it’s resulting in some unintentional comedy in the box score. Golden currently has 16 more targets than Christian Watson, but only one more catch. He’s 33 targets ahead of Tucker Kraft, but only eight catches ahead. Again, he’s clearly getting open, it’s just he’s not doing as much with the opportunity as you’d like. The good news is we’ve seen plenty of wide receivers figure out their drops. Davante Adams is everybody’s favorite example, but Christian Watson might be a better one, or at least a more contemporary one. He, too, had some early career bouts of the drops, but he’s mostly put that behind him. Well, mostly. He, too, has had some issues with drops this season. At least it keeps things interesting. How boring would things be if your receivers simply always caught the ball? title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 9
summary: The Houston Texans enjoyed a reprieve from the horrors last Sunday, as their bye week had arrived. This Sunday off came at a time when it felt like the moon was crashing down on the entire franchise, with cascading failures and injuries pushing the team, many Texans fans, and pretty much everyone on this website […]
full_text: The Houston Texans enjoyed a reprieve from the horrors last Sunday, as their bye week had arrived. This Sunday off came at a time when it felt like the moon was crashing down on the entire franchise, with cascading failures and injuries pushing the team, many Texans fans, and pretty much everyone on this website to a breaking point. Some are already declaring the season “lost,” some are wondering if the Texans should entertain the idea of tanking, and rumors had to be shut down at the possibility of the Texans dealing DE Jadeveon Clowney. Yet, despite all of the doom and gloom, the Texans are still getting a 24.9% chance of making the playoffs from ESPN’s Football Power Index, largely because of their extremely favorable remaining strength of schedule: Week 9: @ Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Week 10: @ Cleveland Browns (5-3) Week 11: Vs. Indianapolis Colts (2-6) Week 12: Vs. Baltimore Ravens (4-4) Week 13: @ Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) Week 14: @ Washington Commanders (2-4-1) Week 15: Vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) Week 16: @ Philadelphia Eagles (2-6) Week 17: @ Green Bay Packers (5-3) Week 18: Vs. Tennessee Titans (1-7) It’s not a very intimidating final half of the regular season, and ESPN is actually favoring Houston in eight of these final ten games! Although, Houston was favored to win in multiple contests they lost in the first half of this season, and with how this team has been playing recently, do you really expect them to look much better against the Chargers or the Browns? The road back to contention is clearly there for Houston, but it will require both their defense to shake off their rocky start to the season and their offense to find some consistency – even as the injury bug targets some of their best players. Second-year WR Jaylin Noel is now on IR thanks to a season-ending turf toe injury, meaning QB CJ Stroud will be relying on his connection with trade acquisitions Kayshon Boutte and Marvin Harrison Jr. to develop at a record pace…which will be another challenge for Houston’s quarterback to overcome this year. He’s overcome stalled contract negotiations, a complete collapse of his team’s defensive backfield, multiple WR and RB injuries, and the reality that scoring 30+ points can still not be enough to win. It’s been a whirlwind of a year for the Texans franchise in general, but for Stroud in particular, this season was a big bet on himself, and despite the win/loss record, he is succeeding. Texans OT Trent Brown is always insightful and one of my favorite players to chat with. We talked about the bye week, what this 2 and 5 Texans team needs to do moving forward and why he has such high praise for QB C.J. Stroud. Here’s our conversation. #Texans #CJStroud … pic.twitter.com/F6qi806at4 — Kim Y. Davis (@kimydavis) November 2, 2026 In fact, just yesterday, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler and DJ Bien-Aime released a piece on Stroud’s stalled contract negotiations, shedding some light on what Stroud’s camp was asking for. It turns out that, at least according to Fowler and Bien-Aime’s reporting, Stroud’s team was not looking for record breaking money, and instead was looking for something, “…similar to the deal Trevor Lawrence signed with Jacksonville two years ago, placing Stroud in the second-tier [of highly-paid QBs] of around $55 million per year.” Stroud and his agent, David Mulugheta, made a counteroffer. They did not demand that Stroud be the league’s highest-paid quarterback, per a source. Stroud understands the business side of being an NFL player, from market pay for players at multiple positions, to team construction. He knows if he takes every penny possible, paying the players around him becomes harder. – Jeremy Fowler, DJ Bien-Aime, C.J. Stroud turned down a big contract. A bigger one awaits. Now, this admittedly paints a favorable picture of Stroud and his agent, David Mulugheta, as some kind of “good faith” negotiators in the process, and the truth is probably something more complicated than this. Mulugheta is also not a stranger to using his relationship with ESPN reporters to cast his clients in a favorable light, so everything said in this article should be taken with a grain of salt. However, I still highly recommend reading through the article in its entirety, as it gives us an idea of what to expect next offseason: A lot of cap-clearing moves, potentially a big trade or two to get some big contracts off the books, and maybe even a yearly salary north of $70 million for Stroud. But, all of this discussion can be spared for the offseason. We’re still in the thick of 2026, and the Texans aren’t dead yet, no matter who says so! Here’s where the Houston Texans are ranked following their bye week: NFL.COM : 19. Houston Texans (2-5) (Last Week: 18) While we can officially agree Houston’s defense isn’t the unit we’ve known it to be in recent years, the Texans have a favorable road out of the bye. Dates with the Chargers and Colts sandwich a meeting with the Browns , so while 2-5 is a tough place to be after eight weeks, there’s still a path back to relevance. Keep an eye on Marvin Harrison Jr. ’s role in the offense, too. – Nick Shook ESPN: 22. Houston Texans (2-5) Week 8 result: Bye Week 8 ranking: 21 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: WR Demaryius Thomas in 2018 Historically, the Texans haven’t made many in-season trades. Zero have resulted in Houston receiving a game-changing player. The hope is Marvin Harrison Jr ., who was acquired from the Cardinals in early October, could become exactly that. Thomas was at least the most effective player out of all the choices. In 2018, Houston started 0-3 and reeled off nine consecutive wins to finish 11-5. Houston acquired Thomas after five wins in a row, and in his first game, he had 61 receiving yards against his former team, the Broncos. He finished the season with 275 receiving yards for Houston with two touchdowns. – DJ Bien-Aime SPORTS ILLUSTRATED: 25. Houston Texans (2–5) Last week’s ranking: No. 21 Last week’s result: idle This week: at Chargers The Texans will face the Chargers this weekend in a battle of the two most confoundingly disappointing teams I can ever remember. This is the kind of hype that forces me to never trust again. – Conor Orr BLEACHER REPORT: 20. Houston Texans (2-5) Last Week: 22 Week 8 Result: Bye Week General manager Nick Caserio was blunt in his assessment of the Houston Texans’ defense after disappointing through the team’s first seven games. Houston’s offense has played relatively well, but the defense underperformed after finishing as last year’s top-ranked unit. “We’re the worst team in the league in tackling,” Caserio said . “Too many missed tackles. Giving up too many explosive plays. Take those two areas right there. If we tackle better and we give up less explosive plays, then (you’ll) probably see a better result defensively.” Expect those previous problem areas to be points of emphasis coming out of the Texans’ bye week, especially with the winless Los Angeles Chargers next on the docket. – Brent Sobleski CBS SPORTS: 23. Texans (2-5) (Last Week: 21) It’s hard for many to see how this team is down this low in the rankings. Here’s why: the defense has been a mess. They can’t afford another loss or they might be done. – Pete Prisco USA TODAY: 26. Houston Texans (24): As generally bad as this 2-5 outfit has been, their schedule still very much portends a world where Houston winds up 10-7. – Nate Davis YAHOO! SPORTS: 19. Houston Texans (2-5, LW: 21) Biggest need: Running back, again The Texans made a big and questionable move in the offseason, trading fourth- and seventh-round draft picks, along with offensive lineman Juice Scruggs, to the Lions for running back David Montgomery. Scruggs has been more valuable this season than Montgomery, who has averaged 2.7 yards per carry and missed two games with injury. Woody Marks hasn’t been much better. Houston has no running game and it’s a big reason it is 2-5. Do the Texans possibly trade for another running…

title: Texans Sign DT Naquan Jones
summary: The Texans are making more midseason moves at defensive tackle. On Monday morning, the team announced that they are signing former Houston Texan DT Naquan Jones from the San Francisco 49ers’ practice squad: In a coinciding move, the Texans are also waiving DT Jaden Crumedy. Crumedy, 26, was signed by Texans off of the Green […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - JANUARY 04: Naquan Jones #91 of the Houston Texans jogs off the field against the Indianapolis Colts during an NFL football game at NRG Stadium on January 4, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Texans are making more midseason moves at defensive tackle. On Monday morning, the team announced that they are signing former Houston Texan DT Naquan Jones from the San Francisco 49ers’ practice squad: We have signed Naquan Jones and made other roster moves. pic.twitter.com/eyRuvODPrO — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) November 2, 2026 In a coinciding move, the Texans are also waiving DT Jaden Crumedy. Crumedy, 26, was signed by Texans off of the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad on September 11th, following rookie DT Kayden McDonald’s placement on IR to begin the season. Crumedy would appear in six games for the Texans, tallying six tackles, a QB hit, half a sack, and a 53.8 PFF Grade (51.4 RDEF, 71.4 TACK, 59.4 PRSH) in 87 snaps on defense. As of today, Crumedy has cleared waivers and is being signed to Houston’s practice squad. Naquan Jones, who is returning to the Texans after failing to make the initial 53-man roster, returns after a brief stint with the San Francisco 49ers, where he appeared in three games and tallied two tackles, one pressure, and a 29.5 PFF Grade (33.0 RDEF, 28.4 TACK, 52.5 PRSH) in 44 snaps on defense. He will replace Crumedy on the DT depth chart. The current lineup consists of: Sheldon Rankins Tommy Togiai Kayden McDonald Logan Hall Naquan Jones Mario Edwards Jr. (Season-Ending IR) Crumedy may not have been a complete disaster for the Texans, but he does not offer the veteran experience that Jones has, especially considering he played over 100 snaps in Houston’s final month of action in 2025. Naquan Jones should provide some much needed run stopping depth to the interior of the Texans dline. Here's some evidence of that from the end of last season. pic.twitter.com/Q0FR3Uwd2P — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) November 2, 2026 Following Houston’s 27-21 overtime loss to the New York Giants, it was clear that improvements had to be made in stopping the run before every team starts copying the Giants’ playbook against the Texans. At 6’ 3” and 313 lbs., Jones should plug right into the LDT spot, next to Logan Hall, Sheldon Rankins, Tommy Togiai, or Kayden McDonald depending on the situation. Hopefully, he’ll pick up where he left off in Houston last year as a solid, if unspectacular interior defender that possesses enough strength and speed to be a handful for opposing offensive lineman. His experience in DeMeco Ryans/Matt Burke’s scheme should give him a chance to make an impact right away, which could be great news if he and McDonald are able to complement each other. In addition to the Naquan Jones signing, the Texans are also signing UDFA RB Joshua Pitsenberger to the practice squad and releasing RB Deuce Vaughn. They also claimed former Cowboys RB Emari Demercado off waivers last week . Lastly, the Texans also announced today that UDFA WR Daniel Sobkowicz is also joining the practice squad along with Jaden Crumedy, and they are releasing 2025 7th round pick DT Kyonte Hamilton and TE Zaire Mitchell-Paden. What do you think of these moves? Are the Texans a better team with Naquan Jones on the roster instead of Jaden Crumedy, or was this a mistake? Will Joshua Pitsenberger and/or Emari Demercado contribute on special teams or the offense this coming weekend, or will we all just be anxiously waiting for RB David Montgomery’s return from injury? Let us know your thoughts down in the comments below! Go Texans!

title: Texans front office face a must-win game against the Chargers
summary: The Houston Texans face the only winless team in the NFL this Sunday when they take on the Los Angeles Chargers. Both teams had bigger plans that to waste away at the bottom of the AFC leaderboard The Chargers season is toast. The Texans still have a glimmer of hope purely based on their history […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 25: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the New York Giants at Reliant Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Texans face the only winless team in the NFL this Sunday when they take on the Los Angeles Chargers. Both teams had bigger plans that to waste away at the bottom of the AFC leaderboard The Chargers season is toast. The Texans still have a glimmer of hope purely based on their history of digging themselves out of holes in the past. Plus, the AFC South is as winnable a division as there is this season. The Texans lost their last three games by a combined 12 points. The Chargers have only scored above 20 points once this season, including scores of six, nine, and 14 twice. For Houston, a win not only rights the ship and re-opens the opportunity to make a last-ditch effort to save the season, but its a mandatory performance for this coaching staff and front office. For all intents and purposes, a loss to the 0-7 LA Chargers will end the Nick Caserio era. A 2-6 record with no early second round pick and a long list of undeveloped day two picks will be too much for this ownership group to look past. Houston has mortgaged their future without any near-term payout. They are $33.8M in the hole next year… before they even extend C.J. Stroud. Plus, they stand to lose Davis Mills, Tank Dell, Tommy Togiai, and Trent Brown. Houston is over-leveraged and is crashing like the ‘08 market. One person not in the spotlight is Frank Edgerly the Senior Director of Football Research and Game Management. He’s been with the team since 2023 and is a disciple of Caserio stemming back from their time in New England. The Texans defensive scheme was observed, analyzed, and addressed by the entire league this offseason. His role in not addressing these issues by self-scouting has been apparent. Not to mention the game management issues late into the fourth quarter where the team has been our maneuvered time and time again. The Chargers woes have stemmed from their horrific offensive line, inability to run the ball, and QB Justin Herbert’s regression. He’s thrown five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. When the Texans faced him in the 2024 AFC Wild Card Round, he had thrown just three interceptions all season. He’s been sacked 23 times on pace to pass his career high last year of 54. Houston desperately needs to add to both his interception and sack totals to win this do or die game against the Chargers. On defense, the Chargers have struggled to generate pass rush all season. DEs Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack lead the team with three sacks each. Like Houston, they lack an inside pass rusher who can disrupt the pocket. Thats ideal for Houston, whose achilles heel has been conceding pressure on the inside. With a good pocket, C.J. Stroud should be able to find his top targets on offense. Houston’s hot seat will remain hot even if Houston wins against the Chargers. They face next the Deshaun Watson-led Cleveland Browns, who are the darling of the 2026 season with a 5-3 record. Deshaun Watson’s trade, orchestrated by Nick Caserio in just his third month as General Manager. That trade netted Houston three first round picks, two fourth round pick, and a third. As it turns out, the compensation on the blockbuster trade has changed: Browns now are giving up six draft picks for Deshaun Watson; also instead of giving up a 2024 5th-round pick, it’s now a 2024 6th-round pick, per today’s wire. pic.twitter.com/Y98WFPmYeE — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) March 21, 2022 Without the overwhelming draft capital he was able to use to maneuver throughout drafts, he has struggled to make sound decisions early in the draft. He’s reached on players to fill needs, creating further issues at critical positions such as offensive line and defensive tackle. The 2025 and 2026 draft classes have been rife with under-performing draft picks at high value selections. Caserio will be directly graded against the outcome of both this Chargers game Sunday and the upcoming matchup against Cleveland. Both games are on the road. All that being said, if Houston can turn it around these next two weeks, things do look up for them. They play the actively taking Colts, a Lamar Jackson-less Ravens team, a winnable game against the Steelers, and a tossup against the Commanders. If Houston exits this six-game stretch at 7-6, they will be squarely in the hunt for another wild card spot in a crowded AFC. 5-1 is mandatory for Houston. Otherwise they need to close up shop on this season and multiple members of the front office.

With that, a review of Houston’s Bye Week: Where does Houston stand vis-a-vis the league after the bye? While Houston took the […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - OCTOBER 25: Houston Texans costumed mascot Toro enters the field during the NFL game between the New York Giants and Houston Texans on October 25, 2026 at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Leslie Plaza Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Houston’s Bye Week : Where does Houston stand vis-a-vis the league after the bye? While Houston took the week off, the chaos didn’t stop. That will likely continue when Houston gets back to their schedule. When they kick-off next Sunday in LA, they will be no better than 2.5 games back of the Jaguars, possibly down 3.5 games. They still have three division games (all at home) left. As for a Wild Card, sitting 11th in the conference does not help their situation. They sit 2.5 games back of New England for the final spot, with Cleveland, Las Vegas and Baltimore still ahead of them. They have three remaining non-conference games, but all of those are on the road and in December/January. While they are a maddening 0-4 at home, they somehow have a winning road record at 2-1. Given that the remainder of the schedule is 6 road games/4 home games, that may not be the worst thing in the world. On the opposite end of the spectrum, Houston holds the 8th pick in the 2027 draft. Just based on numbers, Houston could remain in the draft top 10 if their struggles continue. If the franchise gets solid play from Stroud in spite of bad team play and decides to give him that second contract, it could make Houston game for some wheeling and dealing related to that draft pick. The criticality of November: At 2-5, Houston finds themselves well back of the conference leaders. Still, there are 10 full games left. To be in legitimate position for a playoff berth, Houston will likely need at least double-digit wins. To get to the usual 10-7 record, Houston has to go 8-2. In particular, this squad can’t go any worse than 3-1 in November. Arguably, that will need to be 4-0. On one hand, this past week offered Houston one of the best schedule hands it could have been dealt. The LA Chargers are a league worse 0-7 and are as hard broke as any team in the league. The Cleveland Browns have the best record of the November slate at 5-3, but Watson’s play is falling off and they could possibly overlook the Texans, who will have a losing record when they go to Cleveland in two weeks. The Colts come to Houston, but they have been in fire-sale mode and might just be without long-time Texans’ nemesis Jonathan Taylor when they play late in the month. The calendar ends with a visit from the usually nightmarish Baltimore Ravens, but after this weekend, when they lost their QB1 and QB2 for significant time, they might be in a weakened state. On the other hand, all of that relies on Houston playing to its potential and not surrendering the explosive plays like they have. How often have golden paths been paved with fool’s gold for this franchise? November takes on added significant due to those games being conference matchups, and upping that conference record is going to be critical for overcoming the slow start for the team if the playoffs are to happen. Will the result on LA change anything for the Texans’ roster? A win means the team can still hold out hope for a run. A loss? It doesn’t mathematically eliminate the Texans, but for all intents and purposes, the team will be out of the running. That matchup will end under 48 hours from the trade deadline. Houston added Harrison and they likely aren’t done talking with other teams. However, if Houston loses, do they start off-loading players to try to recoup for the offseason? Houston hasn’t said as much, but especially if the squad can’t overcome the worst team in the league, that would force some tough discussions on the flight back. As it stands, Houston doesn’t have a lot of easily tradeable players. Sure, a player like Danielle Hunter would be on a lot of wish-lists, but how many teams could accommodate this contract and salary cap number? Maybe Xavier Hutchinson is traded not for an improvement, but for some draft capital for next season. How much improvement can a bye really offer? In theory, a bye offers a chance to fix some issues. Yet teams only have a week. It is not like teams can engage in a full-up training camp and fix all the issues. Maybe they can throw in some new plays or adjust some facets of their strategy. Coaches can be fired and new personnel put it, but that doesn’t always spark the desired change. The desperation firings of Chris Palmer as OC in 2005 did nothing to help that hapless offense and the sacking of Bill O’Brien in 2020 did not salvage that season. Could Houston get flexed out of their prime-time slots? The schedule-makers back-loaded the Texans’ primetime appearances, with a Week 11 Thursday Night game against the Colts, a Week 13 Sunday Night matchup against Pittsburgh, a Week 16 Christmas Eve duel against the Eagles and an Week 17 Monday Night game against the Packers. The Colts game is ineligible for flexing. The Christmas Eve game is also locked in, for better or worse. However, the Sunday Night Matchup at Pittsburgh and the Monday Night Game against Green Bay can get flexed. The league would need to give 12 days’ notice and there would be a lot of horse-trading going between the networks. Much depends on Houston remaining in the playoff mix. Pittsburgh and Green Bay rest in playoff position and have rather strong fanbases that help ratings. However, if Houston is playing out the string by Thanksgiving, look for one or both of those games to get moved. The Texans did have one scheduled Sunday Night Game in 2013 flexed to an early afternoon kickoff (their home game against the New England Patriots). FUN WITH NUMBERS: 1-2: Houston’s record post-bye under Ryans. 2023 saw Houston exit a bye week only to lose an ugly matchup with a bad Panthers’ team on the road. 2024 saw the team return from a late bye to beat the Dolphins to clinch the division at home after a Colts’ loss later that day. Last season, Houston came off an earlier bye only to lose a tough Monday Night matchup at the eventual Super Bowl Champion’s home in Seattle. .703: Houston’s post-bye winning percentage in the regular season during the Ryans’ regime: Remember the whole 8-2 target? Well, it might not completely be out of the norm for a Ryans’ squad. In 2023, the team exited it bye with that bad loss to Carolina but still finished the year 7-4. The late bye skews some of this, as Houston had a Week 14 bye before a 3-game stretch in 11 days, finished the year 2-2. Last season’s 9-game win streak did most of the lifting for a 10-2 finish. Given that there were no games or major news of note good or bad for players, we’ll forgo awarding of game balls or declarations of idiocy. Those will resume next week. The second part of the season starts in LA against the 0-7 Chargers. Kickoff is slated for 3:05 CST with coverage on CBS/Paramount+ (unless the game were [deservedly] flexed to local public access at 5:30 a.m. Sunday morning). See y’all there.

title: Stampede Blue Reacts Survey (Week 9): Should the Colts trade Jonathan Taylor?
summary: With the November 10 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaching, the Indianapolis Colts are facing one of their most difficult decisions in recent memory: whether to trade superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. Following the departures of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, Indianapolis appears to be embracing a rebuilding approach, and Taylor could be the […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - NOVEMBER 01: Quarterback Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts hands off the ball to runningback Jonathan Taylor #28 of the Indianapolis Colts during the second half of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the November 10 NFL trade deadline rapidly approaching, the Indianapolis Colts are facing one of their most difficult decisions in recent memory: whether to trade superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. Following the departures of Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner last week, Indianapolis appears to be embracing a rebuilding approach, and Taylor could be the next major name on his way out. Multiple teams have reportedly expressed interest in acquiring the 27-year-old, including the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Seattle Seahawks and New York Giants, with the Colts reportedly seeking compensation equivalent to a first-round pick. While Taylor remains one of the NFL’s premier running backs, the question is whether his remaining prime years align with Indianapolis’ timeline for returning to contention. He is under contract through 2028 and has publicly expressed his desire to remain with the franchise, but with the Colts sitting at 2-6 and already without their 2027 first-round selection, acquiring additional premium draft capital could prove extremely valuable. On the other hand, trading Taylor would leave an already struggling offense without its most dependable playmaker, potentially making life even more difficult for whoever eventually takes over at quarterback. With the deadline just days away, should Indianapolis capitalize on Taylor’s trade value or retain him as a cornerstone of its future? Should Jonathan Taylor be traded? Are you confident in the Colts? Any optimism surrounding the Colts following Chris Ballard’s dismissal appears to be fading quickly, particularly after Sunday’s humiliating 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Indianapolis was thoroughly outplayed on both sides of the football, trailing 28-0 at halftime before eventually suffering its fourth consecutive defeat. The offense managed just seven points, while the defense surrendered 42 in a performance that raised further questions about the team’s immediate future under Shane Steichen. What was already shaping up to be a disappointing season has now turned into a potential organizational reset, with several established veterans either traded or reportedly drawing interest from contenders. Last week’s Reacts survey showed that only 31 percent of Colts fans believed the franchise was headed in the right direction, a significant decline from the previous week’s 47 percent. That drop came after the trades of Nelson and Buckner, and the latest defeat is unlikely to have improved the mood surrounding the team. However, with the organization finally beginning to make significant changes and potentially accumulating additional draft capital, some fans may view the current struggles as a necessary step toward building a more competitive roster. Whether that long-term optimism outweighs the frustration of watching another lost season remains to be seen. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero, the Indianapolis Colts have resigned Ade Adebawore to a 2-year, $35 million contract extension (with a $13 million signing bonus): The Colts and DT Adetomiwa Adebawore agreed to terms on a two-year, $35 million extension that includes a $13M signing bonus and $22.5M in new money through 2027. The deal was… pic.twitter.com/D4TVQLVbvO — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 3, 2026 As an otherwise pending free agent, the former 2023 4th round pick of the Colts in in the midst of a breakout campaign with Indianapolis, recording 19 tackles (8 solo), 4 tackles for loss, 4.0 sacks, 16 total QB pressures, and 2 passes defensed during 8 games (2 starts). His pass rushing production has been pretty impressive when one considers that Adebawore was previously in a rotational interior pass rushing role during the 2026 season, with more limited snaps, but has now become a full-time starter in the aftermath of the Colts trading veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner early last week. A number of interested NFL suitors had reportedly called the Colts on Adebawore’s availability, but still only age 25-years-old, Indianapolis considers him a core defensive player of their recently jumpstarted rebuilding efforts and rightfully extended him, even with an expected general manager transition at year-end.

title: Chiefs Mailbag: What to think of the Kingsley Suamataia mess?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! A frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos dropped the Chiefs to 5-2 and left fans wondering how seriously to panic. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds ahead of […]
full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! A frustrating loss to the Denver Broncos dropped the Chiefs to 5-2 and left fans wondering how seriously to panic. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds ahead of hopefully a get-right opportunity against the New York Jets . Tomahawk0611 asks: Why didn’t left guard Kingsley Suamataia play yesterday? Has he been permanently benched? We saw Suamataia benched in Week 4 only to return to the starting lineup after the bye. I suspect that we will see him again in Week 9 against the Jets, but this has been a weird situation. I think it is fair to be frustrated with Reid’s cryptic responses, but what should be obvious is that the staff has made it clear to the player they are not happy about something. It is unclear whether that is tied to performance or practice habits. Whatever the problem, however, I don’t think fans are putting enough blame on Suamataia for how he is falling short of expectations. This is especially true considering one of the biggest fan criticisms from the past few seasons has been a perceived lack of accountability. The frustration with the staff and front office should be that they did not have a better backup plan than Mike Caliendo before deciding to hold the line on Suamataia. GoldenDomer asks: Is the QB sneak refusal an Andy Reid thing or Patrick Mahomes thing? It’s equally disappointing that Mahomes hasn’t just done it on his own at this point. Since the night in Denver that the world saw Mahomes’ kneecap put back into place on the field, the quarterback sneak has clearly not been an option for the Chiefs. We saw the team briefly use tight end Noah Gray — and Blake Bell before him — on the play. Unfortunately, teams quickly caught on. For fans, the obvious answer to short-yardage woes has been to re-sign running back Kareem Hunt. My solution would be to put backup quarterback Justin Fields into some third-and-1 and fourth-and-1 plays. Perhaps that means taking Mahomes off the field for a snap. Perhaps that has both quarterbacks on the field at the same time. Defenses accounting for Fields would likely pay bigger dividends for running backs Kenneth Walker and Emmett Johnson in the crucial situations. Glorified KC asks: Why did the defense struggle so much in the fourth quarter? Did Sean Payton figure out a weakness to exploit? They went from allowing 0 first downs in the third quarter to allowing 15 points in the fourth. To be fair, the Chiefs are not the only team to have trouble putting the Broncos away late. Of Denver’s now six wins, they were trailing or tied entering the fourth quarter four times (with one of their other wins coming in overtime). I assumed that the Jacksonville Jaguars and Los Angeles Rams would put the Broncos away, only to see a similar story unfold that we saw Sunday. Reid put the defense in bad positions twice by punting on fourth-and-1, leading to a touchback, before having Harrison Butker miss a 54-yard field goal to start Denver’s final position at their own 44-yard line. I actually think Reid chose the wrong time to punt in either situation. On both of Denver’s touchdown drives, the Chiefs’ defense surrendered a massive play. One saw a 15-yard penalty added on, and the final drive saw a 50-yard play go to the five-yard line. The defense let Kansas City down. However, I would also put heavy blame on conservative offensive playcalling that yielded zero points in the final frame. Atypical Vagabond asks: Can the Chiefs stop beating themselves? There is no reason not to win with a 15 point lead… yet we certainly found a way to lose. There are two seasons that are coming to mind when I see how the last two weeks have gone. The first season I covered the Chiefs for Arrowhead Pride was 2021. That year, the Chiefs appeared to play undisciplined much of the season and had a predictable offense where almost anyone could tell what play was about to be called based on the formation. That season ended with an inexcusable loss in the AFC Championship game. The other season I am thinking of came in 2023, when Kansas City took an extended offensive slump almost to the playoffs, including an inept Christmas Day performance against the Raiders. We will remember that year ended with Kansas City’s third Super Bowl title in a five-season span. The past two games have been frustrating. However, I think we need to wait out the rest of the slate and judge the Chiefs on the whole of the season. That said, we need to see the team really focus on getting right over the next three weeks against a trio of seemingly lesser opponents. RunningFree asks: At what point will (local) media turn on Andy’s way of not providing meaningful answers no matter the question? If someone asked him if it rained during the game at Denver he might say something along the lines of: “We’ll go back, look at the tape, and see where we’re at. I’m not gonna get into all the details on that. You guys saw what happened out there. So, uh, we’ll just go from there.” Truthfully, I included this question because it really made me laugh. I do not know how much longer the 68-year-old Reid plans to continue coaching. But I don’t see him changing his tone with the media. Fans frequently vent frustration that beat writers are not asking tough enough questions when Reid is available, typically on Wednesdays, Fridays, and after games. I would counter that most of those writers know what topics Reid is likely to be more upfront about. It is hard to create content off of the coach’s nonanswers. Local media will continue to ask similar questions in press conferences. When we do get unflattering details around the team — such as what we have seen recently with tackle Josh Simmons — expect national media to continue breaking the news. Thank you for reading this week’s Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! We will be back after the Chiefs try to get back on track against the Jets. Keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to ask your questions.
author: Jared Sapp

title: The Good and the Bad from the Chiefs’ loss to Broncos
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second game of the season in Week 8, 28-24, to the Denver Broncos. Let’s look at one thing that went well and two things that didn’t from the game: The Good Emmett Johnson’s performance Rookie running back Emmett Johnson was the best player on the field for the Chiefs […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second game of the season in Week 8, 28-24, to the Denver Broncos . Let’s look at one thing that went well and two things that didn’t from the game: The Good Emmett Johnson’s performance Rookie running back Emmett Johnson was the best player on the field for the Chiefs against the Broncos. Johnson finished with five catches for 128 yards, including a 73-yard receiving touchdown. He only got one carry, but it went for 15 yards. Johnson’s long touchdown was a great design by head coach Andy Reid and staff. The Broncos love to blitz on third downs. They send their nickel on a blitz, hoping to keep Johnson in protection. Instead, the Chiefs have Johnson leak across the formation and run a wheel route. The Broncos screw this coverage up, as one of the defensive linemen, likely the defensive end, should drop and carry Johnson. Regardless, it’s still Johnson on a defensive end in a footrace, and Johnson is going to win that often. Andy Reid wanted to get Denver’s linebackers in space, and Johnson executed on those plays. The Broncos are in Quarters coverage here against the 2×2 formation for the Chiefs. The boundary cornerback is occupied by tight end Travis Kelce running a 12-yard in route and can’t turn back to the flat quickly enough. Wide receiver Rashee Rice runs an underneath route to occupy the backside linebacker, leaving the other linebacker responsible for covering Johnson in the flat because the coverage was flooded. He had no chance of stopping Johnson, easily getting around him for another explosive play. I really liked Johnson coming out of Nebraska due to his combination of agility and balance in the hole. This play is a good example of that. Johnson makes the defensive end miss in the hole after right tackle Jaylon Moore whiffs on a block, makes the linebacker miss inside, jukes the safety inside with a deceleration move, spins out of another arm tackle, and gains 15. These types of plays were all over his Nebraska film, and he can do that in the NFL as well. Johnson is now up to 237 receiving yards on the year. He’s been terrific on third downs this year, which is huge for spelling lead back Kenneth Walker. I would like to see Johnson get into the rotation for carries as well. The case against giving Johnson carries is that it takes Walker off the field, and Walker has a greater chance of getting explosives. However, giving Johnson more carries does save Walker and keep him fresher to get those plays. I would argue that the Chiefs should probably throw the ball less than they do now and feature Johnson and Walker more often in the run game. The Bad Andy Reid’s 3rd and 2 play call before the missed kick There’s been some consternation about Andy Reid’s playcalling in this game, but honestly, I think the Chiefs offense played about as well as you can hope. This team has two shaky tackles against a great Denver pass rush and one NFL wide receiver in Rice against Denver’s top-tier cornerbacks. Kansas City’s only options were attacking the Broncos’ bad linebackers in coverage, and they did that well. The run game didn’t go as well as you would hope, but they also had a backup left guard — a separate issue for the team. Denver was always going to stop the run better in this game than they did in Week 1, but the Chiefs’ passing game was legitimately good. That was a huge difference from Week 1, too, when the Chiefs’ passing game was terrible. That said, I didn’t like this third-and-2 call before Butker misses the kick. Chiefs are in 12 personnel and run a half rollout for Mahomes. Kelce is the #3 receiver and runs the corner clearout route, which doesn’t make sense to me. The play is designed for Jalen Royals and Xavier Worthy to win on whip routes. Royals and Worthy can’t win against man coverage at all and had zero chance of getting open. Wouldn’t it make more sense to have one of those two bad receivers run the pointless clearout route and let Kelce or even Rice have the underneath route? Why are we designing plays for Worthy or Royals? Mahomes should’ve thrown this ball away, but I don’t like limiting the field on third-and-2; mainly, designing the play for Royals or Worthy is bad. Worthy just does nothing on the field well anymore, and they need to replace him. Hopefully Royals’ snaps go down once Rice gets healthier. The Bad Chiefs defending the flats The Chiefs defense made me mad in this game. Once again, they had zero pass rush. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix did hit some nice downfield throws that weren’t always bad coverage. But the biggest issue was how badly the Chiefs defended the flats. Bo Nix is either a vertical or flat thrower. He does nothing else. This is the Chiefs’ fifth time facing Nix, and they didn’t seem to realize it. It started twice on the first drive: the first was a running back screen Alohi Gilman was late to close on, and the second was Cochrane completely lost on a bootleg. Gilman has to defend Jonah Coleman in the flat here and lets Coleman run past him, and he gets called for pass interference. The Broncos run a switch release to Waddle for a touchdown. Chris Rolland-Wallace and Nohl Williams botch the switch call, and Rolland-Wallace is way too late to recover on Waddle. The annoying part is the Chiefs messed this up again, this time off a bootleg. Jadon Canady thinks he’s running the clearout route, but Williams does too, making one of them way too slow in the flat. The Chiefs send a six-man pressure here with two to the running back side of the protection. The Broncos have six in protection and slide the right way. I believe Nick Bolton is green-dogging here, which means he blitzes if the back stays in protection; otherwise, he has him in coverage. Regardless, he gets lost on the play, and the blitz means everyone is behind the play when it goes for 51 yards.
author: Nate Christensen

title: Week 9 AP NFL Power Rankings: Broncos enter top 10 after divisional win
summary: Maybe you’re like me and the Kansas City Chiefs’ loss completely ruined your Sunday afternoon. I couldn’t bring myself to watch football anymore until halftime on Monday night. Yes, the “Sunday Night Football” matchup was horrible — Philadelphia Eagles versus Washington Commanders. But it could have been the 1972 Dolphins versus 2007 Patriots, and I […]
full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Maybe you’re like me and the Kansas City Chiefs ’ loss completely ruined your Sunday afternoon. I couldn’t bring myself to watch football anymore until halftime on Monday night. Yes, the “Sunday Night Football” matchup was horrible — Philadelphia Eagles versus Washington Commanders . But it could have been the 1972 Dolphins versus 2007 Patriots, and I wouldn’t have watched. The Chiefs left too bad a taste in my mouth. Hopefully the Chiefs have moved on, but I’m still working through my anger over that game. Regardless of the Chiefs’ clunker, this NFL season continues to be entertaining and unpredictable. No team is unbeaten in the league, and only one team remains winless. Preseason favorites such as the Los Angeles Rams or Seattle Seahawks are only .500. The Pittsburgh Steelers and Jacksonville Jaguars are surprising first-place teams in their respective divisions. The Arrowhead Pride staff returned this week with the latest edition of the Power Rankings. This week’s rankings saw two new entrants in the top 10, while two new teams fell into the bottom 5. Biggest riser: Las Vegas Raiders +5 Biggest fallers: Baltimore Ravens and Indianapolis Colts -5 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. Buffalo Bills (1st) They could basically go on cruise control due to the Ravens’ quarterback injuries. 2. Chicago Bears (5th) A legit Super Bowl contender. They get more impressive by the week. Trading for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons solidifies one of the few holes on the roster. 3. San Francisco 49ers (3rd) I fully expect this team to be angry and return to form after their bye week following a head-scratching loss to the Falcons. 4. Minnesota Vikings (2nd) Their defense plays lights out. Their offense barely plays. 5. Jacksonville Jaguars (7th) They could potentially have this division wrapped up by Thanksgiving. A great team absolutely no one talks about. 6. Seattle Seahawks (4th) The Bears dropping 34 points on this defense is not what I wanted to see a week after the Chiefs couldn’t even get into the red zone. 7. Denver Broncos (11th) They may be in the top 10 of our rankings, but I don’t have a positive thing to say about this franchise at the moment. 8. Cincinnati Bengals (8th) Joe Burrow may be the current MVP frontrunner. 9. Kansas City Chiefs (6th) The worst vibes of any 5-2 team I can think of. 10. Detroit Lions (12th) A huge, gritty win for the Lions and their gritty head coach. 11. New England Patriots (9th) They almost blew it, but divisional games are always tough. A win is a win. 12. Pittsburgh Steelers (10th) This week’s matchup against the Bengals will tell me if the Steelers are for real or not. 13. Green Bay Packers (14th) If Micah Parsons comes back healthy, the NFC North race is the most interesting in football. 14. Los Angeles Rams (16th) Would Aaron Donald have come out of retirement had he known this team would only be .500 after Halloween? 15. New York Giants (17th) The surprising leaders of the NFC Least. 16. Cleveland Browns (15th) Not winning a single game in Pittsburgh since 2003 is objectively crazy. 17. Las Vegas Raiders (22nd) In my opinion, the Raiders are making the smart long-term play by keeping Fernando Mendoza on the bench and riding it out with Kirk Cousins. 18. Baltimore Ravens (13th) Some difficult conversations regarding Lamar Jackson’s long-term future in Baltimore will be happening soon. 19. Carolina Panthers (19th) The Chiefs may have been able to muster a sack against this offensive line. 20. Houston Texans (21st) We’ll see if they can dig themselves out of the hole they’ve created following their bye week. 21. Atlanta Falcons (18th) I repeat—your offense fields Drake London, Bijan Robinson, and Kyle Pitts—yet you look this anemic? 22. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (20th) I legitimately thought I was being trolled when a friend texted me the Bucs won without completing a pass. How is that possible? 23. Dallas Cowboys (23rd) This team invents hilarious ways to lose football games every week. 24. Washington Commanders (27th) Good job, Jayden Daniels! You won a football game! 25. New Orleans Saints (25th) The first fall guy: the Saints fired their run game coordinator this week. 26. Arizona Cardinals (29th) Spoiler alert! 27. New York Jets (28th) This week should one hundred percent be a “get right” game for the Chiefs. But I’m worried that won’t be the case. 28. Philadelphia Eagles (24th) When I looked ahead at the NFL schedule, I unfortunately saw a lot of Eagles’ games in primetime. 29. Tennessee Titans (31st) They had the Bengals right where I wanted them. Until they let them off the hook. 30. Miami Dolphins (30th) Ollie Gordon has been a good waiver wire addition to a couple of my fantasy teams. But he hurt his real team on Sunday. 31. Indianapolis Colts (26th) I remember the old “Suck for Luck” campaign. But (currently) without a first-round pick in 2027, they’re tanking without any real direction. 32. Los Angeles Chargers (32nd) It’s getting real bleak in Southern California.

title: Poor situational football dooms Chiefs’ offense against Denver
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second straight game, 28-24, against the Denver Broncos on Sunday, falling to 5-2. The loss propelled Denver to first place in the AFC West standings and should leave the Chiefs scratching their heads. The Chiefs offense was fairly productive all game, with big plays from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and […]
full_text: (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs lost their second straight game, 28-24, against the Denver Broncos on Sunday, falling to 5-2. The loss propelled Denver to first place in the AFC West standings and should leave the Chiefs scratching their heads. The Chiefs offense was fairly productive all game, with big plays from quarterback Patrick Mahomes and rookie running back Emmet Johnson. Heading into the fourth quarter, the Chiefs led 24-13, but ended the game with a punt, a missed field goal, and a turnover on downs in the final minutes. The Chiefs’ offense outgained Denver by nearly 100 yards, but lingering third-down issues and poor situational football led to critical failures in the game’s largest moments. First possession of the fourth quarter The fourth quarter started well for the Chiefs, with running back Kenneth Walker converting a third down and keeping the clock running. After gaining four yards on a zone-read look on first down, Mahomes barely missed Kelce on second down on a pass that would have put the Chiefs past midfield and in the driver’s seat. On the ensuing third down, Mahomes would go to Johnson, who had a monster game up to that point. This look is somewhere between an option and a rollout pass to Johnson. As it turned into a downfield pass, right tackle Jaylon Moore was deemed too far downfield, and officials called an illegal man downfield penalty; meanwhile, Johnson got as close as he could to a first down. It is hard to know the series of events on the field, but Johnson was ruled down about a foot short of a first, and then Denver head coach Sean Payton declined the penalty, making it fourth-and-1. No review of the play was made, but once Payton declined the penalty, this locked in his decision and would have given the Chiefs a chance to go for it on fourth down. The Chiefs punt unit quickly ran to the field, where the ball was booted into the end zone for a touchback. Nine plays later, the Broncos scored and converted a two-point conversion to cut the deficit to three with less than nine minutes to play. The decision to kick The Chiefs would start their next drive on a positive note as they looked to drive the ball and burn time off the clock. With just under four minutes to play, the Chiefs had picked up another first down, with Walker and Johnson both contributing against a tired-looking Denver defensive front. With the run game finally firing, and Denver on the ropes, the next set of Chiefs plays was baffling. The Chiefs ran a screen to Rashee Rice outside, which, in theory, would strain the legs of the already-tired defense, but Rice made a poor choice to cut back inside instead of following his blocks to the outside and was tackled for only a two-yard gain. On the next play, the Chiefs ran a similar look to Walker. The screen to Walker appears to have been meant to take the defense by surprise, but they quickly swarm around Walker and prevent a larger gain. The play still gained six yards, and it would open up a manageable third-and-two. The next play and ensuing decision would shape the end of the game. The Chiefs’ run game had been ineffective for most of the game, but Walker and Johnson had started to wear down the defense’s tired legs. The Chiefs came out of the gun needing two yards for a first, and they ran a rollout look, but the play quickly broke down. Walker is responsible for the first man off the line, but the edge rusher knocks him back, stopping the rollout. This disrupts Mahomes timing and prevents him from seeing Kelce flashing across the screen. With no one else open, Mahomes takes a costly sack, putting the Chiefs in a situation where going for it on fourth and short is no longer an option. Loyal Andy Reid trotted out Harrison Butker to attempt a 54-yard kick, and it ended up wide right. The Broncos got the ball back in prime field position and scored in two plays to take a four-point lead. The Chiefs got one more shot, and it came down to the red zone. Final drive A monster Johnson kickoff return put the Chiefs in business, and it took them four plays to set up a first-and-goal at the Denver four-yard line. After an eight-yard shovel pass, the Chiefs let the clock run from 1:05 to 35 seconds. A Walker run would move the ball to the one-yard line. Out of timeouts, Denver could only wait, but then the Chiefs used a timeout of their own. On their first crack from the one, the Chiefs went with an old favorite— the corndog —but Denver was ready. With nine seconds to play, the Chiefs tried to run the ball again with Walker, but Denver was ready. Denver’s defensive line pinches down, and a free runner comes through at the line to stuff Walker for no gain. On the next play, it appeared that the Chiefs had won, but a penalty on Moore wiped it away and set up a fourth-and-6. On the game’s final play, Mahomes would take a sack on a poorly designed look. The play was poorly protected, and none of the Chiefs’ receivers found any daylight againt the Broncos’ man coverage. The bottom line There is more than one reason that led to this loss, but the poor situational football was a large culprit for the offenses implosion late in the game. The Chiefs short yardage conversions have become an issue, and there is a path to succsuess, but it would involve the team doing something they have not done in over seven years. The quarterback sneak is one of the most efficient plays in the history of the game, and the Chies blatant refusal to do so has cost the team due to a freak accident. Even if the team decides to execute the plays with Mahomes on the sideline, backup quarterback Justin Fields should be more than capable of getting the job done. Justin Fields converting 3rd and 4th shorts (1-2) the last 3 years. Might be worth a shot for the Chiefs to try this option to solve the short yardage woes pic.twitter.com/FBtsan5lAB — Billy M (@BillyM_91) November 2, 2026 The run game was bottled up, but the decsion to run a rollout look leading to a sack was inexcusable, especially when there was a hot hand like Johnson ready to go. Running the ball takes comitment, but if the rock is pounded enough times it will eventually break. Relying on one of the worst reciever rooms in the NFL to produce consistently in key moments is not an option. The decsion to allow Butker kick, to only put the team up six points may be one of the worst of Reid’s career. The inability to score from the one yard line against a gassed defense with no timeouts, and relying on old tricks like “corndog” that half the field for a wizard like Mahomes can no longer be accpeted, especially when the main target runs out of bounds. Starting one of the worst interor offensvie lienmen in the NFL inexplicably for the second time this season can also no longer be tolerated, especially when his body of work provides no evidence he has earned a stating spot, and his backup this week did not play with little context from the organization. The 2026 Chiefs have the offensive talent to remain one of the leagues best units, and they showd what they are capable of multiple times through the course of the game. The key situations, and bad decisions on critical downs are what seperates them from a two game division lead, and the race they will be in with the Broncos the rest of the season. The wrongs can me made right, but a plan needs to be put in place for these short yardage situations, what to do with Butker, and how the offensive line will look. November is here, and as the schedule gets tougher, the games get bigger. It will be worth watching to see how the Chiefs perform as the pressure builds.
