title: Mack Hollins to return to Patriots practice on Wednesday
summary: The New England Patriots’ depleted wide receiver group is about to receive a boost. Mack Hollins, who has missed the last four weeks on injured reserve, will make his return to practice on Wednesday. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Patriots will open his 21-day window to rejoin the active […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ depleted wide receiver group is about to receive a boost. Mack Hollins, who has missed the last four weeks on injured reserve, will make his return to practice on Wednesday. According to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Patriots will open his 21-day window to rejoin the active roster. Hollins, 33, was placed on injured reserve following New England’s Week 4 win over the Buffalo Bills due to a calf injury. Up until that point, he had played 63% of the team’s offensive snaps and been on the receiving end of 15 catches for 209 yards. His return to practice will be a big step for player and team alike. Hollins is not only a starter-caliber wide receiver and locker room leader for the Patriots, but also was part of a group of three wideouts who recently were forced to miss time. During last Sunday’s 24-19 victory over the Miami Dolphins, Hollins was joined on the sidelines by A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder; IR). In the three veterans’ absence, New England relied on a trio of Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and DeMario Douglas. The trio combined to catch nine passes for 156 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Week 8. The Patriots will host the Green Bay Packers at Gillette Stadium this week. They will release their first injury report leading up to the Nov. 8 contest on Wednesday afternoon.

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Packers ahead of Week 9
summary: New England Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf knows the Green Bay Packers well. And now, the same goes for offensive quality control coach T.C. McCartney, defensive quality control coach Jamael Lett, outside linebackers coach DeMarcus Covington and special teams coordinator Cam Achord. But there’s also those in the locker rooms. Between […]
full_text: Oct 18, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Green Bay Packers running back Pierre Strong Jr. (22) during the game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New England Patriots executive vice president of player personnel Eliot Wolf knows the Green Bay Packers well. And now, the same goes for offensive quality control coach T.C. McCartney, defensive quality control coach Jamael Lett, outside linebackers coach DeMarcus Covington and special teams coordinator Cam Achord. But there’s also those in the locker rooms. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, seven players currently in the fold have been members of both clubs during the NFL careers. Here’s a glance through the ex-Patriots and ex-Packers ahead of Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium. GREEN BAY Pierre Strong Jr., running back — Selected by Bill Belichick’s war room in the fourth round of the 2022 NFL draft at No. 127 overall, Strong checked into 15 games as a rookie. The FCS All-American out of South Dakota State handled 100 rushing yards, 42 receiving yards, 115 kickoff return yards and his first NFL touchdown across 23 all-purpose opportunities that season. He was traded to the Cleveland Browns at the cutdown deadline the following August in exchange for offensive tackle Tyrone Wheatley Jr. After two campaigns in the AFC North, Strong spent 2025 on the practice squad of the Packers and now resides on Green Bay’s 53-man roster. The 27-year-old running back stands 50 games into his career and with 116 carries for 536 yards, 34 catches for 243 yards, 24 kickoff returns for 570 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Jonnu Smith, tight end — Smith totaled 55 receptions for 539 yards and one touchdown across 30 games with the Patriots. The 31-year-old’s stay spanned 19 starts and reached its end halfway through a four-year contract. A trade with the Atlanta Falcons during the 2023 offseason brought a seventh-rounder back in return. And on the heels of being named to the Pro Bowl while a member of the Miami Dolphins in 2024, Smith was dealt to the Pittsburgh Steelers. A one-year deal then got him to Lambeau Field in August. Originally entering the NFL with the Tennessee Titans at pick No. 100 overall in the 2017 draft, the Florida International product has amassed 351 catches, 28 carries, 3,819 yards and 32 touchdowns from scrimmage across 148 career games. Mike Mularkey and Mike Vrabel served as the tight end’s head coaches in the AFC South before he agreed to terms at Gillette Stadium. David Blay Jr., defensive tackle — The Packers added Blay to the practice squad at the end of September. The 23-year-old defensive tackle originally entered the NFL in Foxborough as part of the organization’s undrafted class of 2026. He was waived by the Patriots two weeks into training camp and finished his rookie preseason with the Philadelphia Eagles before going through the wire unclaimed and catching on in Wisconsin. Blay made collegiate stops at West Chester, Louisiana Tech and Miami while appearing in 46 games. John Saunders Jr., safety — Saunders joined Green Bay’s practice squad on Tuesday after making autumn stops on scout teams in Ohio and New Jersey. The 25-year-old intercepted a pass in August preseason action with New England before being let go at the 53-man roster deadline. Last fall, as an undrafted rookie by way of Miami of Ohio and Ole Miss, Saunders had been added to the Patriots’ active roster off the practice squad of the Dolphins. He agreed to remain in the fold as a member of the practice squad for the rest of 2025 after clearing waivers. NEW ENGLAND Romeo Doubs, wide receiver — The Patriots placed Doubs on injured reserve six games into the fall after he suffered a shoulder injury on a 42-yard touchdown catch. Signed to a four-year deal as an unrestricted free agent in March, the veteran wide receiver stands with 14 receptions for 261 yards and three visits to the end zone this campaign in Foxborough. Not eligible for a return until late November, Doubs originally entered the NFL with Green Bay in the fourth round of the 2022 draft at No. 132 overall. The 26-year-old Nevada product started 50 of his 59 games as a Packer while reeling in 216 passes for 2,424 yards and 21 touchdowns. Greg Van Roten, guard — Van Roten landed on injured reserve in late September with a thigh injury. It was sustained at right guard during the 106th start and 147th game of his NFL journey. The 36-year-old had visited amid training camp and soon circled back on a one-year pact. First setting out as an undrafted rookie with the Green Bay Packers in 2012, the former All-Ivy League honoree out of Penn appeared in 10 games across two seasons there. Van Roten has been a member of eight different NFL organizations as well as the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts since then. He logged back-to-back ironman campaigns with the New York Giants before taking on a depth role at Gillette Stadium. Mike Brown, safety — Brown earned a promotion to New England’s 53-man roster in October after twice serving as a standard elevation from the practice squad. The 27-year-old safety first landed with the Patriots after not being tendered as a restricted free agent in March. Through six games, he has handed nine tackles while seeing 38 snaps on defense and 127 snaps on special teams. Entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2022, the Miami of Ohio alum spent his first preseason with the Minnesota Vikings and had a stint on Green Bay’s practice squad before returning to his previous NFC North club. After moving on to Cleveland later in his rookie campaign and appearing in three games, he was signed to head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Titans 53-man roster. The Tennessee tenure featured 59 tackles and a handful of starts across 35 contests.

title: Patriots vs. Dolphins snap counts from Week 8
summary: The New England Patriots offensive line has undergone multiple changes since the start of the season, and Sunday’s win over the Miami Dolphins saw the latest chapter in the ongoing story being written. After starting Walter Rouse at left guard, the Patriots made a switch at the half to insert Ben Brown into the lineup. […]
full_text: The New England Patriots offensive line has undergone multiple changes since the start of the season, and Sunday’s win over the Miami Dolphins saw the latest chapter in the ongoing story being written. After starting Walter Rouse at left guard, the Patriots made a switch at the half to insert Ben Brown into the lineup. Brown finished the game at the position, and now seems like the frontrunner to remain in that role for the foreseeable future and until starter Alijah Vera-Tucker is cleared to return from injured reserve. Rouse, meanwhile, appears to be headed back to the bench after starting two games in place of Vera-Tucker. For head coach Mike Vrabel, the change came down to in-game momentum; Rouse had struggled in the first half, prompting the change to a more reliable Brown after two quarters. “Ben’s worked really hard,” Vrabel said on Monday. “Coming in, he had worked through the knee injury – would have been Jacksonville, I think. He came back, had been working in practice, and we stuck with Walter and then wanted to take a look at Ben. We’ll see where that goes this week. Those guys play extremely hard. It’s never going to be perfect. I thought they both did some things well. I thought they both would have some plays that they would like to improve on.” Here is our full snap count report from the Patriots’ 24-19 win . Offense Total snaps: 60 | Time on the field: 31:09 | * denotes starter QB Drake Maye * (60; 100%), LT Will Campbell * (60; 100%), C Jared Wilson * (60; 100%), RG Matt Pryor * (60; 100%), RT Morgan Moses * (60; 100%), TE Eli Raridon * (55; 92%), WR Efton Chism III * (53; 88%), WR Kyle Williams * (50; 83%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson * (46; 77%), WR DeMario Douglas (39; 65%), LG Ben Brown (34; 57%), LG Walter Rouse * (26; 43%), TE Tanner Arkin * (16; 27%), RB Corey Kiner (11; 18%), TE Hunter Henry (8; 13%), TE Cameron Latu (7; 12%), RB Lan Larison (5; 8%), WR Ryan Miller (5; 8%), OT/TE Caleb Lomu (5; 8%) Besides the Ben Brown/Walter Rouse combo at left guard, the Patriots offensive line went wire-to-wire on Sunday. That included Matt Pryor, who, while far from perfect either, seems to remain the right guard of choice until one of the higher-ups on the depth chart returns. At wide receiver, the Patriots opted to leave DeMario Douglas in his role as a third slot receiver even with A.J. Brown on the inactives list. This meant that Efton Chism and Kyle Williams were the main options on the perimeter and in two-receiver sets. All three had their moments , with Douglas and Williams both catching long touchdowns to help New England pull away in the second half. At tight end, the Patriots got Hunter Henry involved early but he departed with a foot injury in the early second quarter. In his place, rookie Eli Raridon played a career-high 92% of snaps. Tanner Arkin, a regular on the inactives list in recent weeks, also set a new career mark with a 27% playing time share. Running back continued to be the Rhamondre Stevenson show, with Corey Kiner and recently-promoted Lan Larison only seeing spot duty. Defense Total snaps: 65 | Time on the field: 26:33 | * denotes starter LB Robert Spillane * (65; 100%), LB Christian Elliss * (65; 100%), CB Christian Gonzalez * (65; 100%), S Kevin Byard III * (65; 100%), S Craig Woodson * (65; 100%), CB Carlton Davis III * (63; 97%), ED Elijah Ponder * (54; 83%), DT Milton Williams * (44; 68%), ED Dre’Mont Jones * (42; 65%), CB Marcus Jones (40; 62%), DT Christian Barmore * (36; 55%), DT Cory Durden * (26; 40%), DT DaQuan Jones (21; 32%), DT Leonard Taylor III (20; 31%), ED Gabe Jacas (19; 29%), S Jaylen Reed (13; 20%), DT Joshua Farmer (10; 15%), CB Charles Woods (2; 3%) Coming off a three-game absence due to a neck injury, Carlton Davis returned to the lineup on Sunday and promptly played 63 of 65 defensive snaps — a positive sign even though he did show some rust in man-to-man coverage. The two snaps he wasn’t on the field for saw CB4 Charles Woods enter the field. On one of Woods’ snaps, he tripped and fell, allowing Miami’s Kevin Coleman Jr. to get open for a 35-yard touchdown. Going against one of the most productive scramble quarterbacks in football, the Patriots opted to increase their use of three-safety packages. This meant that late-August trade acquisition Jaylen Reed saw an uptick in opportunities again, playing 20-plus% of snaps for the first time since Week 5 and fourth time overall this season. Up front, Gabe Jacas’ knee injury in the early third quarter left New England thin on the edge. Elijah Ponder and Dre’Mont Jones, the latter of whom getting dinged up himself at one point, did not see a noticeable uptick in snaps. Instead, New England opted to use their big bodies on the interior to keep the rotation along the defensive line — both inside and outside — intact. That included Christian Barmore, who has been the recent subject of trade speculation . Against Miami, there was no noteworthy change in his usage. He did return to the starting lineup after a four-game absence, however, and at 55% had his highest playing time share since Week 1. He also clearly out-snapped Cory Durden, who did have the most disruptive game of his career but continued to be used on a rotational basis like the other DTs. Special teams Total snaps: 26 | Time on the field: 2:18 TE Cameron Latu (22; 85%), S Brenden Schooler (21; 81%), LB Darius Muasau (20; 77%), LB Namdi Obiazor (20; 77%), S/PP Mike Brown (20; 77%), LB Erick Hunter (17; 65%), S Jaylen Reed (17; 65%), RB/KR Lan Larison (13; 50%), CB Charles Woods (13; 50%), CB Kindle Vildor (13; 50%), K Andy Borregales (10; 38%), P/H Mitch Wishnowsky (8; 31%), LS Julian Ashby (8; 31%), TE Tanner Arkin (7; 27%), DT Leonard Taylor III (7; 27%), ED Elijah Ponder (7; 27%), OT Caleb Lomu (5; 19%), OT Dametrious Crownover (5; 19%), OL Jared Wilson (5; 19%), OL Matt Pryor (5; 19%), OL Walter Rouse (5; 19%), ED Gabe Jacas (5; 19%), CB/PR Marcus Jones (5; 19%), RB/KR Corey Kiner (4; 15%), DT Milton Williams (4; 15%), DT Cory Durden (4; 15%), DT DaQuan Jones (4; 15%), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (1; 4%), WR Efton Chism III (1; 4%), WR/KR Kyle Williams (1; 4%), WR DeMario Douglas (1; 4%), LB Robert Spillane (1; 4%), LB Christian Elliss (1; 4%), S Kevin Byard III (1; 4%) The Patriots made some changes to their kicking game operation versus the Dolphins, most prominently in the return game. With Kyle Williams playing a starter-level role on offense, the lead-off duo on kickoff returns consisted of Corey Kiner and Lan Larison. With Miami opting to go for the end zone shot each time, however, neither had a real oppotunity to return kicks on Sunday. Another change in the kicking game saw defensive tackle Leonard Taylor being used as a part of the kickoff coverage team. At 6-foot-3, 305 pounds he was an unlikely addition to the group, and ended up playing just two snaps. One of them saw him attack too far upfield and contribute to a 43-yard kickoff return in the first quarter. Did not play QB Tommy DeVito For a seventh time in eight games this season, Tommy DeVito remained on the bench throughout the game. Unlike the previous contest in Chicago, when he had company in the form of rookies Tanner Arkin and Dametrious Crownover, he was the only player not to take the field against the Dolphins. Inactive QB3 Behren Morton, RB TreVeyon Henderson, WR A.J. Brown, CB Karon Prunty, CB Channing Canada, S Elliott Davison The Patriots downgraded TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and A.J. Brown (knee) before the trip to Miami, while the other four inactives were all healthy scratches. That included safety Elliott Davison, who has since been released and is expected to rejoin the team via its practice squad. Of course, inactivity does not reflect roster status: cornerbacks Karon Prunty and Channing Canada were both healthy scratches, but New England still opted to cut veteran Kindle Vildor over them on Tuesday.

title: What activating Marcus Bryant, releasing Kindle Vildor means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots remain busy modifying the back end of their roster. After releasing safety Elliott Davison on Monday, they made two other depth moves on Tuesday. Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant was activated from injured reserve to the active roster, with cornerback Kindle Vildor released. The moves mean that the Patriots still have one […]
full_text: The New England Patriots remain busy modifying the back end of their roster. After releasing safety Elliott Davison on Monday, they made two other depth moves on Tuesday . Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant was activated from injured reserve to the active roster, with cornerback Kindle Vildor released. The moves mean that the Patriots still have one open spot on their 53-man team — one considered likely to be used on another player set to come off of IR soon, such as wide receiver Mack Hollins. What else do Tuesday’s moves mean, though? Let’s take a closer look at them through a big-picture lens. OT Marcus Bryant: Activated off IR During the regular season and obviously depending on each individual situation, every NFL team has the opportunity to bring up to eight players back from its injured reserve list. Entering Tuesday, the Patriots had used two such spots already — one on wide receiver A.J. Brown, who returned in Week 6, and the other on Bryant: he had already been declared as a return candidate back when he was first sent to IR in late August. This, of course, means that Tuesday’s activation did not change the eight-player return count; New England is still on 2-of-8 spots used. What the transaction means, however, is that he has rejoined the 53-man roster just in time before his 21-day activation window came to a close. As a consequence, the Patriots are now five players deep at offensive tackle: 53-man roster (5): Will Campbell (66 | LT), Morgan Moses (76 | RT), Caleb Lomu (74), Dametrious Crownover (68), Marcus Bryant (52) Practice squad (1): Lorenz Metz (61 | exempt) Will Campbell and Morgan Moses are entrenched as the starters, with Caleb Lomu having shown intriguing talent whenever entering the field for one of the two. The fourth spot, meanwhile, will be worth keeping an eye on moving forward. If we base the projection off of training camp and preseason, Bryant would be OT4 — in fact, he even had a case for OT3 after the summer — over rookie Dametrious Crownover. At the very least, Bryant’s return gives New England more flexibility and options up front. That includes using Caleb Lomu as an emergency interior lineman, even though the team clearly would prefer to keep him at tackle as much as possible. CB Kindle Vildor: Released Based on Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins, Vildor’s release comes as a minor surprise. While his 13 snaps on the day exclusively came on special teams, he was part of the game day roster as the fifth cornerback over rookies Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. In fact, the two youngsters were made healthy scratches. And yet, on Tuesday, it was the veteran — who has so far out-snapped both of them on the season — to be let go. The why has yet to be determined, although it seems that his status might be directly tied to that of cornerback Carlton Davis, who had missed three games due to a neck injury before returning on Sunday. With Davis back in the lineup, roster flexibility seemingly outweighed the need for a seventh player at the position regardless of experience or résumé. For the time being, New England’s cornerback group therefore now looks like this: 53-man roster (6): Christian Gonzalez (0), Carlton Davis III (7), Marcus Jones (25 | PR), Charles Woods (22), Channing Canada (29), Karon Prunty (21) Practice squad (1): Al’zillion Hamilton (26) The expectation is that Vildor could be brought back to the practice squad in the near future. If so, he would naturally become a candidate for game-day elevation again should the circumstances require such a move. Already having used one such elevation earlier in the season, the Patriots can bring him up two more times down the stretch this year. As noted above, his (or Elliott Davison’s, depending on how you look at it) roster spot is meanwhile likely to go to a player currently still on injured reserve. Wide receiver Mack Hollins and fullback Reggie Gilliam are eligible to return to practice this week, while offensive lineman Greg Van Roten is among other players who could make a comeback at any point.

title: Patriots activate offensive tackle Marcus Bryant from injured reserve amid series of moves
summary: After eight games away, Marcus Bryant’s stay on injured reserve is over. The New England Patriots activated the offensive tackle and released veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor from the 53-man roster amid a series of moves announced Tuesday. Bryant, 24, had been designated to return at the NFL’s cutdown deadline in August following a preseason ankle […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 16: New England Patriots offensive tackle Marcus Bryant (52) warms up before the NFL preseason game between the New England Patriots and Minnesota Vikings on August 16th, 2025, in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images After eight games away, Marcus Bryant’s stay on injured reserve is over. The New England Patriots activated the offensive tackle and released veteran cornerback Kindle Vildor from the 53-man roster amid a series of moves announced Tuesday. Bryant, 24, had been designated to return at the NFL’s cutdown deadline in August following a preseason ankle injury. His 21-day practice window opened in October and he has since gone from limited to full participation. Selected in the seventh round of the 2025 draft at No. 220 overall, Bryant outlasted the 53-man deadline as a rookie in Foxborough. The 6-foot-7, 220-pound swing tackle via Southern Methodist and Missouri went on to appear in 12 games for the Patriots last campaign, seeing 19 snaps on offense and 56 snaps on special teams. Vildor, 28, began 2026 on New England’s practice squad and was promoted to the 53-man roster after serving as a standard elevation. A game ball followed for the 5-foot-11, 189-pound cornerback, who has appeared in five games this fall en route to seven tackles, one stop for loss, one forced fumble and one pass deflection. Chosen by the Chicago Bears in the fifth round of the 2020 draft at No. 163 overall, Vildor has also been a member of the Tennessee Titans, Philadelphia Eagles, Detroit Lions and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Through 85 career games, including 27 starts, the Georgia Southern product as had a hand in 147 tackles, one sack, two forced fumbles and two interceptions. The juggling continued elsewhere on Tuesday. After losing linebacker K.J. Britt to the 53-man roster of the Lions the evening prior, the Patriots signed fellow linebacker Elias Neal to the practice squad and also released wide receiver Cameron Dorner and offensive lineman Jake Kubas. Neal, 25, went undrafted in 2024 after recording 375 tackles, 12 sacks, five interceptions and five fumble recoveries while at Marshall. The 6-foot, 224-pound linebacker made the initial 53-man roster of the Los Angeles Rams during his rookie season before serving as a standard elevation from the practice squad during the 2025 and 2026 campaigns. He was released in late October. Including playoffs, Neal has appeared in 12 NFL games. The former third-team All-Sun Belt selection’s career includes 162 snaps on special teams and three tackles. Dorner, 22, agreed to terms with the Patriots as an undrafted free agent in May and was retained on the practice squad at its formation after clearing waivers in August. In between, his preseason audition featured four catches for 37 yards. The 6-foot-1, 188-pound rookie wide receiver spent three years at Division II Shepherd before enrolling at North Texas in 2025. From there, he totaled 56 receptions for 911 yards and eight touchdowns for the Mean Green. Kubas, 26, joined New England’s practice squad as the calendar turned to September. The 6-foot-4, 308-pound guard entered the league as an undrafted rookie out of North Dakota State in 2024. A three-time FCS national champion, Kubas spent his previous two NFL seasons between the 53-man roster and practice squad of the New York Giants. He has appeared in five career games, starting three, while handling 198 snaps on offense and 16 snaps on special teams. The practice squad now carries two open spots. But one will soon be going to safety Elliott Davison, per ESPN’s Mike Reiss , after he cleared waivers . Davison, 24, had been promoted to the 53-man roster in October following two standard elevations . The 6-foot, 190-pound safety first landed on the practice squad in September before being released and re-signed. His time with the Patriots has brought two tackles and one pass deflection through three appearances spanning 10 snaps on defense and 57 snaps on special teams. Entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2025, the UTSA alum spent his rookie year on the practice squad of the New Orleans Saints. The Green Bay Packers visit Gillette Stadium on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 4:25 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots Power Rankings Week 9: Pats hold their ground
summary: I understand the Patriots looked shaky in the first half against the Dolphins on Sunday. I understand that the team has been dealing with an overabundance of injuries, and the status of top players remains in question on when – or if – they will return this season. But New England also stormed back and […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - NOVEMBER 01: A New England Patriots fan is seen with a message to New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) during a NFL game between the New England Patriots and the Miami Dolphins, on Sunday November 01, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL.(Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I understand the Patriots looked shaky in the first half against the Dolphins on Sunday. I understand that the team has been dealing with an overabundance of injuries, and the status of top players remains in question on when – or if – they will return this season. But New England also stormed back and won the game. What I don’t understand is why the experts dropped the Pats down in the rankings this week. The average of all these rankings turned out to be 10.5, which is reasonable. A fifth is too low, at least at the moment, and 14th is too high. Beating Green Bay on Sunday should give them a nice boost. But while the Dolphins may have been playing for pride, the Packers will be fighting to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. Both the Patriots and Packers are coming into Week 9 hot. QB Drake Maye has posted MVP-type numbers over the last four games, (11 touchdowns, 1 INT) and crossing the 110 passer rating mark in each game. QB Jordan Love (8 TDs, 3 INT) has also been productive in this stretch, averaging over 300 yards and 2 TDs per game with a strong completion percentage. The Packers are 2.5 point road underdogs but a solid matchup to New England, both offensively and defensively. If the Pats can play a clean game with regards to turnovers and penalties, they can win this one by a touchdown. GO PATS!! AFC East: Buffalo Bills (6-1) at Minnesota Vikings (6-1) New England Patriots (5-3) vs. Green Bay Packers (5-3) New York Jets (2-6) at Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) Miami Dolphins (1-6) vs. Detroit Lions (5-2) AFC Matchups: Denver Broncos (6-2) at Carolina Panthers (3-4) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2) – Bye Week Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) at Baltimore Ravens (4-4) Cincinnati Bengals (5-2) at Atlanta Falcons (3-5) Cleveland Browns (5-3) at New Orleans Saints (2-5) Las Vegas Raiders (4-4) at San Francisco 49ers (6-1) Houston Texans (2-5) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) Indianapolis Colts (2-6) vs. Dallas Cowboys (3-5) Tennessee Titans (1-7) – Bye Week 5th – Nate Davis (USA Today): They’ve only scored more than 30 points once this season as they navigate their offensive injuries. But Pats still play mean defense, giving up more than 30 points only once this season . [+3] 10th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): The Patriots had neither A.J. Brown nor TreVeyon Henderson to raise the big-play quotient in the offense, but Drake Maye still passed for 8.7 yards per attempt, and the team still rushed for 131 yards to beat the Dolphins. They won’t give the Bills much breathing room in the AFC East . [nc] 10th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): The Patriots had to shake off an ugly first half before they finally started to pull away from the awful Dolphins. They were playing without their top two receivers and one of their two best running backs, so it probably was never going to be easy. With the Packers and the Lions coming up before the bye week, they better get healthy soon. It would really help if they could get No. 1 WR A.J. Brown back since they’ll need a lot more out of Drake Maye and the passing game to beat either of their next two opponents. Stat To Know : With their win over the Dolphins, the Patriots are now 8-1 vs. divisional opponents since the start of last season . [+1] 10th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): They avoided the South Florida trap, again . [+1] 11th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Best in-season trade acquisition ever: Edge Kyle Van Noy in 2016. Dealing a 2017 sixth-round pick to the Lions for Van Noy and a 2017 seventh-round pick helped bring a key cog onto a team that won the Super Bowl that season, and then won it again two seasons later. Van Noy played 67 games (53 starts) for the franchise, setting a team high in total tackles in 2018 (92). And he is still going strong in 2026 as a member of the Vikings . — Mike Reiss [-1] 11th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): They didn’t look great in the victory over Miami, but a win is a win. The defense is getting better by the week . [nc] 11th – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): Biggest need: Interior offensive line.The Dolphins don’t have a good pass rush but they still pressured Drake Maye often in Week 8. Maye overcame that with a strong second half to lead the Patriots to a win, but it’s not like the line issues are going away. Guards Mike Onwenu and Alijah Vera-Tucker are on injured reserve. Getting a guard to help makes a lot of sense. The Patriots have also had some trade speculation on the selling side. Cornerback Carlton Davis III could be dealt, according to Albert Breer of SI.com. Davis returned from a neck injury for Week 8 and played 96.9% of the defensive snaps, but it’s possible the Patriots want to trade him for extra draft capital, which they could use to improve at guard . [nc] 11th – Nick Shook (NFL): The Patriots went to Miami — where they’ve historically found themselves in some hair-raising situations — played terribly in the first half and still found a way to win. Mike Vrabel addressed the team at halftime, inspiring a second-half showing that included 21 straight points to secure a mature victory that lesser, more-inexperienced teams wouldn’t have achieved . [-1] 12th – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): New England overcame a 13-3 halftime deficit to beat Miami 24-19, with Drake Maye delivering both TD passes after the break. Patriots now have five wins and have responded well to setbacks. The slow start against a one-win opponent keeps them from making a bigger move . [-2] 14th – Conor Orr (SI): I truly do not understand how Kyle Williams was robbed of a touchdown on Sunday. While I am beginning to accept and almost enjoy the incredible inconsistency from crew to crew on the most basic of subjects, how we do not have a general idea of what constitutes a touchdown catch is beyond me . [-3] AVG RANK: 10.5 [-0.2]

title: Rhamondre Stevenson is exactly who the Patriots offense needs right now
summary: The New England Patriots offense entered its game against the Miami Dolphins with a laundry list of injuries, and it didn’t get any shorter on Sunday. The team was already without three of its top four wide receivers, its No. 2 running back, its fullback, and its starters at both left and right guard. Then, […]
full_text: The New England Patriots offense entered its game against the Miami Dolphins with a laundry list of injuries, and it didn’t get any shorter on Sunday. The team was already without three of its top four wide receivers, its No. 2 running back, its fullback, and its starters at both left and right guard. Then, in the early second quarter, it also lost starting tight end Hunter Henry to a foot injury. And yet, it mattered not. While there were some first-half issues, the unit eventually regrouped and was able to help the Patriots secure a 24-19 victory . Unsurprisingly, quarterback Drake Maye had a big hand in the come-from-behind win, but so did one of the seemingly most under-appreciated running backs in the NFL: Rhamondre Stevenson. The sixth-year back finished with 82 rushing yards on 19 carries , three receptions for an extra 8 yards, and a successful onside kick recovery. The numbers may not stand out, but Stevenson’s impact on the Patriots is without question. He is exactly the player their offense needs right now. Just listen to Mike Vrabel. “He certainly does a lot for us,” New England’s head coach told WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show on Monday. “He’s a versatile running back. He’s very good in protection. Plays extremely well without the football. Whether that’s chasing to try to help the guy get extra yards or protecting the guy with the ball. Ball security is critical. But, his protection on third down and when they blitz, I think that’s a strength of his. “The things that he does on the football field tell me that he cares deeply about the team. I’ve enjoyed coaching him. I love how his growth has been as a leader in the running back room and in the offense. And then again, I’ll go back and say that there were times last year, when he didn’t take of the ball, that we did a terrible, horses—t job of protecting him. And again, there were times where he didn’t have good technique and there were times that we didn’t protect him. So, I think he’s continued to work hard at that, running hard and gaining yards after contact, but also taking care of the football.” Ball security has been a concern about Stevenson since his rookie campaign. In fact, he lost a fumble on his second career touch — one of 18 total fumbles and 10 turnovers he has had over his career so far. He even had one earlier this year in a win over Pittsburgh. However, while his fumble issues seemingly have been Stevenson’s defining characteristic in a nation-wide eye, he has shown that his performance makes up for it. Otherwise, he wouldn’t have been able to become one of the most prolific running backs in Patriots franchise history. With his 7-yard run in the third quarter, @Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson joins Sam Cunningham (5,453), Jim Nance (5,323) and Tony Collins (4,647) as the only Patriots players to reach 4,000 rushing yards. pic.twitter.com/W2QJhG4IHC — Patriots Communications (@PatriotsComms) November 1, 2026 Stevenson also has been something the Patriots haven’t gotten out of their offensive personnel a lot this season: reliable. Despite seeing a high number of reps week in and week out — he has more than double the snap count of the other running backs on the roster combined — he finds a way to make positive plays. He also does so without the support of some superb blocking; in fact, he likely would rank a lot higher than 22nd in the league in rushing yards (367), 28th in touchdowns (2) and 31st in yards per carry (3.8) if New England’s offensive line played at a more consistent level. The fact that it doesn’t, at least in run blocking, is a direct result of the injuries up front. Right guard Mike Onwenu went down in Week 2, followed by his replacement, Greg Van Roten, in Week 3; left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker was lost in Week 6, while top backup Ben Brown also missed time. That is not even touching on the injuries elsewhere on the offensive roster. Stevenson, meanwhile, has been a model of stability and availability, and a tone-setter for the entire unit even as the hits kept coming. “He loves the football team,” said Vrabel after Sunday’s game. “You can see it by the way that he prepares, the way he plays, the way he protects the guys that don’t have the ball, or how he plays when he doesn’t have the ball, his ability to protect the quarterback when they blitz. It does a lot of things for us. He goes and covers the onside kick. And a lot of guys may let that go, but he wanted to go be the answer and be the reason why we were going to win the football game.”

summary: The New Orleans Saints made a set of roster moves today, announcing that they have released kicker Daniel Carlson and claimed running back Audric Estime off waivers. full_text: METAIRIE, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 13: Audric Estimé #30 of the New Orleans Saints participates in drills during a joint practice at Ochsner Sports Performance Center on August 13, 2026 in Metairie, Louisiana. (Photo by Tyler Kaufman/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints made a set of roster moves today, announcing that they have released kicker Daniel Carlson and claimed running back Audric Estime off waivers. Estime is a much-needed addition to a running game that has been virtually nonexistent this season. Coming off their bye week, the Saints are looking to reinvigorate an offense that has struggled to find consistency, and that has to start with establishing the running game, which currently ranks among the worst in the NFL. The running back returns to New Orleans after averaging 4.3 yards per carry last season. Currently, CJ Donaldson leads the Saints with 4.8 yards per carry, while Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller are averaging just 3.0 and 2.8 yards per carry, respectively. With Donaldson dealing with an injury, bringing Estime back into the fold could provide a much-needed breath of fresh air for the Saints’ rushing attack. The decision to release Carlson is another indication that the Saints have yet to find stability at kicker since moving on from Will Lutz. Carlson has struggled throughout the season, costing New Orleans valuable points in several key situations. At this point, it would appear that Charlie Smyth is the leading candidate to take over kicking duties. With the Saints coming off their bye week and looking to turn things around, these moves could be just the beginning. What other roster moves do you think the Saints will make, or should make, as they look to improve this team?

(Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, November 3, 2026, New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson presented a $250,000 check to The Fourteens Foundation at the United Way Resiliency Center. The generous donation will provide much-needed assistance and support to the victims and families affected by the horrific New Year’s Day terrorist attack on Bourbon Street, while also helping the community continue to heal and recover. In the early morning hours of January 1, 2025, tragedy struck New Orleans when a terrorist drove a truck into a crowd of people celebrating the New Year in the French Quarter, killing 14 people and injuring dozens more. The devastating attack left families grieving, survivors facing long roads to recovery, and the city mourning an unimaginable loss. In the wake of the tragedy, the community has continued to come together to honor the victims, support their families, and provide assistance to those whose lives were forever changed. The Fourteens Foundation was established to create and maintain a permanent memorial honoring the 14 lives lost, their families, injured survivors, and the community, while also recognizing the heroic efforts of first responders. The foundation is committed to preserving history, fostering healing, and promoting education that advances unity, resilience, and peace for future generations. To learn more, please visit Fourteens Foundation: Memorial Foundation for Victims and Community Support

title: State of the NFC South: Week 8
summary: Only one winner from the NFC South this week, one on bye week, and one of the worst games of the season. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: So, let’s address that worst game of the season. With horrible weather in Tampa Bay, the Buccaneers shut out the Atlanta Falcons 16-0, and as you can guess, it was […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers takes the field prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Only one winner from the NFC South this week, one on bye week, and one of the worst games of the season. Tampa Bay Buccaneers : So, let’s address that worst game of the season. With horrible weather in Tampa Bay, the Buccaneers shut out the Atlanta Falcons 16-0, and as you can guess, it was ugly. With this being between two NFC South teams, I’ll get to the Buccaneers’ defensive performance there and speak on how much trouble they gave Michael Penix, but let’s focus on Tampa Bay’s offense. QB Baker Mayfield was, and I’m not joking, 0-3 on the day, and the Buccaneers had zero passing yards. If you had told me that statline, I would have thought it was a blizzard. The running game, obviously, was the star of the game. Bucky Irving had 170 rushing yards and 1 touchdown, while Kenneth Gainwell had 140 yards. Suddenly, Tampa Bay is on a two-game win streak, but their next opponent, the Chicago Bears, will be a challenge. Carolina Panthers : The other team that played this week was the Carolina Panthers, and after firing their defensive coordinator, they didn’t win. The Panthers are losing their lead in first place after going on a losing streak, but it wasn’t a horrible loss. Bryce Young played decently; the run game had a fine game, and the run defense did really well. The pass defense, which has been the issue this season, was what got exposed, but they did get an interception. Carolina needs to break the loss streak before it’s too late, but their next game is against the Broncos. Atlanta Falcons : On the other side of that horrible game, the Falcons barely showed up. They attempted to pass, and it ended up with Michael Penix throwing 4, yes, 4, interceptions and only completing 8-24 passes. Then, when running the ball, they were seeing success but didn’t go to Bijan Robinson enough. The defense did their job, but the offense didn’t. Maybe it will be better against the Cincinnati Bengals, but also, that team is 5-2. New Orleans Saints : The Saints were on their bye week. It’ll be fun to see what changes the Saints make for their next game against the Cleveland Browns, because momentum must switch.

title: NY Giants trade candidate: RB Derrick Henry
summary: Should the New York Giants, who are clearly big-game hunting in the running back market with the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, try to bring Derrick Henry to New York? Head coach John Harbaugh has said he would love for the Giants to have a “Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley situation” with the Giants. […]
full_text: Derrick Henry | Getty Images Should the New York Giants, who are clearly big-game hunting in the running back market with the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, try to bring Derrick Henry to New York? Head coach John Harbaugh has said he would love for the Giants to have a “Derrick Henry or Saquon Barkley situation” with the Giants. Clearly, Harbaugh does not believe Cam Skattebo gives him that. The Baltimore Ravens’ season is falling apart. Baltimore is 4-4, last in the NFC North, and has lost its top two quarterbacks, Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntly (turf toe) for the season. The Ravens are going nowhere fast. Mike Florio said on PFT Live that Henry should be begging for a trade to the Giants. “If you’re Derrick Henry, are you showing up today and are you saying ‘Please trade me to the Giants’, or another contender … The season is going down the s——— for the Ravens right now. If I’m Henry and I’m looking at the calendar and I’m looking at the schedule and I’m looking at the situation and I’m thinking I’m not getting any younger and I’d kinda like to have a playoff run. “If I’m the Giants and I’m looking at Jonathan Taylor if I’m John Harbaugh I’m calling my former GM Eric DeCosta today and I’m saying ‘is there any way that Derrick Henry could be available’.” Why it would work Henry, 6-foot-3, 252 pounds, has been one of the pre-eminent running backs in football for a decade. He was the lynchpin of Harbaugh’s rushing attacks with the Ravens the past two seasons, and is the model power/bellcow/explosive running back for a Harbaugh offense. Henry is 32 with more than 3,000 touches in his career. That is a lot of mileage for a running back, and Henry is clearly past what is usually considered the expiration date for when backs are usually at their best. He gained more than 3,500 yards averaged more than 5 yards per carry the last two seasons with Harbaugh. Henry is averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry this year. Is that about Henry? Jackson barely playing? A new offense with a team that has now lost three straight games? Henry is signed through 2027, but has no guaranteed money next season.. He has three void years in his contract, but the Ravens would be responsible for those as dead money. As a rental, the Giants might not have to surrender as much draft capital for Henry as they would for Taylor. Harbaugh has clearly shown a willingness to pick up the phone and try to broker deals. His relationships with DeCosta and Baltimore owner Steve Bisciotti might help get this one done. Why it wouldn’t work There are only two reasons I can think of. Maybe Henry really is finally slowing down. It would be up to Harbaugh and the Giants’ pro personnel department to make that decision. The other would be that the Giants might choose not to go the rental route. [Article updated to reflect that Henry is under contract through the 2027 season].
author: Ed Valentine

title: NY Giants trade deadline 2026: Missing picks complicating efforts to make deal
summary: The New York Giants are clearly pushing to make a big move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, which is now just six days away. The Giants’ efforts, though, are reportedly being hampered by their lack of draft capital. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Giants’ lack of fourth- and fifth-round […]
full_text: Jonathan Taylor | Getty Images The New York Giants are clearly pushing to make a big move prior to the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, which is now just six days away. The Giants’ efforts, though, are reportedly being hampered by their lack of draft capital. NFL insider Jordan Schultz is reporting that the Giants’ lack of fourth- and fifth-round selections in the 2027 NFL Draft is making it more difficult to put together viable packages for teams with players they may be willing to sell. Per Schultz, the Giants are countering that difficulty by “pushing for bigger names who would require higher picks—and seem open to doing that.” The Giants sent their fourth-round pick to the Cleveland Browns to move up and select wide receiver Malachi Fields in this year’s draft. They used their fifth-round pick to acquire quarterback J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart suffered his season-ending injury. The Giants are projected to receive a fourth-round compensatory pick in 2027. Since compensatory picks are not awarded until shortly before the draft, the Giants don’t yet possess that pick and cannot trade it. GM Joe Schoen addressed those moves during his bye week press conference. “Obviously you want to have as many picks as you can,” Schoen said. “But, again, we’re glad we have Malachi Fields. We’re glad we have J.J. So, the utilization of those draft picks that we gave up to get those two players, we’re happy we have them.” Head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that the Giants “always” want to improve the roster. He acknowledged the difficulty, though, of getting deals done. “Easier said than done,” Harbaugh said. “And it’s hard to find players that can make you better, because we have good players. Very good players. So, it’s got to be something that is a need, that fits your financial profile, that fits your price tag. “It’s not like we have a bunch of draft picks, either. We’re not loaded with 12 or 13 draft picks where we’ve got draft capital to burn. We don’t. So, we have to be smart shoppers that way.” Using 2028 picks is a possibility, with Harbaugh saying “it’s easier to put on the credit card.” The difficulty, of course, is that right now those have less value to teams who are selling.

title: 3 NY Giants-Eagles storylines for Week 9: Can New York handle prosperity?
summary: The New York Giants head to Lincoln Financial Field, a place that has been a house of horrors for the Giants more than a decade, to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The script has been flipped in 2026, with the Giants leading the division, while the reeling Eagles enter the game in last place […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images The New York Giants head to Lincoln Financial Field, a place that has been a house of horrors for the Giants more than a decade, to face the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. The script has been flipped in 2026, with the Giants leading the division, while the reeling Eagles enter the game in last place in the NFC East with a six-game losing streak. Let’s look at some of this week’s storylines. Who’s the bully now? The Giants have not beaten the Eages at Lincoln Financial Field since a 15-7 victory on Nov. 27, 2013. The Eagles have won the NFC East title three of the last four seasons, appearing in two Super Bowls and winning one. The Giants went 11-38 from 2023-2025. Yet, at the midway point of this season we are living in an alternate reality. The Giants are leading the division at 4-2-1 and trying to make moves to improve their chances of reaching the playoffs. They are the betting favorite. The Eagles are trying to figure out what truck ran them over and whether or not Humpty Dumpty can be put back together again. It is an amazing turn of events. Question is, can and will the Giants handle their business? Good teams win games like this one. Who’s toting the rock? Tyrone Tracy is on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. Cam Skattebo did not practice on Monday due to his own hamstring injury, and head coach John Harbaugh said Skattebo will be “day to day up to the game.” As of this writing, the Giants have not completed a trade for Jonathan Taylor, Derrick Henry, Tony Pollard, Breece Hall , or any other running back. Najee Harris is somewhere looking for a new job. Devin Singletary , who has 18 carries this season, might be the last man standing from the Giants’ original backfield on Sunday. Gregory Desrosiers will be playing in his first NFL game after being signed off the Los Angeles Chargers practice squad. Practice squad back Phil Mafah has five NFL carries. Eric Gray , released in cuts to the 53-man roster, was just re-signed to the practice squad. He has six fumbles in 81 career touches, hardly a confidence-inspring statistic. Can J.J. keep rolling? J.J. McCarthy has played five excellent quarters of football since replacing Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter of a Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints. He has fans and media members alike conjuring McCarthy vs. Jaxson Dart scenarios regarding who will quarterback the Giants next season. There is a long way to go, though, and McCarthy has a lot to prove before putting the Giants into a situation where they would actually have to make such a decision. Can McCarthy continue to impress? Can he continue to look like a viable NFL starting quarterback? Can he continue to make the Minnesota Vikings silly for dumping him earlier this season in return for the bargain price of a fifth-round pick? That is to be determined. McCarthy is actually 7-4 as a starting quarterback with five consecutive victories. The common denominator in all of those games? Just like his national championship-winning career at Michigan, McCarthy was never asked to do too much in any of them. The Week 7 victory over Houston, when McCarthy went 20 of 28 passing was the most passes he has thrown in any winning effort as an NFL quarterback. The 252 yards passing was also a career-high. Only twice in his career has McCarthy been asked to throw 30 or more passes. In those two games, both losses, he has gone 36 of 74 (48.6% completions) with 2 touchdown passes and 4 interceptions. NFL teams will figure out how the Giants are using McCarthy, and how they are orienting their passing attack. Looking at McCarthy’s pass charts at NextGen Stats, it is clear he does not like to throw the ball in the middle of the field. Twenty-seven of his 28 passes against the Houston Texans were outside the hash marks, and most were outside the numbers. The charts from all 11 of his NFL starts tell the same story. What happens when teams start squeezing the Giants’ passing attack into the middle of the field, where McCarthy doesn’t want to be? What happens when they jam the box and force McCarthy to win games by throwing 35 or more times? McCarthy’s ability to navigate those things will tell us how much he has truly grown as an NFL quarterback.
author: Ed Valentine

summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants get set to face the last place Philadelphia Eagles. full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants get set to face the last place Philadelphia Eagles. John Harbaugh pushing all the right buttons for Giants | ESPN.com Accountability is vital in Harbaugh’s program. This is crucial because it was considered a shortcoming of former coach Brian Daboll and how he led the team. These new Giants are at a point where it’s acceptable and common during team meetings for Harbaugh or his assistants to call out individuals for mistakes during practice or games. “I would say some of [my coaches] have handled it like Harbaugh, some of them haven’t. It really just depends on your coaching style and how you want to handle it,” veteran offensive lineman Aaron Stinnie said. “But I think guys are taking really good to it and like it. I think it helps. It helps keep everyone accountable and stay on the same page. There’s definitely a way to do it and he does a good job of having it in a constructive manner. Just being upfront and honest. Everything is transparency.” Giants looking to big swing From @BigDayESPN : Could the #Giants swing big at the trade deadline? pic.twitter.com/6AoOFWiaFM — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 3, 2026 Why a Jonathan Taylor trade to NY Giants would make sense right now | The Record With John Harbaugh as the face of the franchise, the shot caller of all football decisions, the New York Giants will never punt opportunities that present themselves. And this, where they are at the moment, certainly constitutes an opportunity that few if any Giants saw coming. Blockbuster incoming? All signs point to Giants making splash ahead of NFL trade deadline | The Athletic The first-place Giants won’t be sellers, so any trade would likely involve a player who has fallen out of favor. Center John Michael Schmitz lost his starting job to Bryan Hudson in Week 4. Schmitz provides depth at an important position, but a center-needy team could offer a Day 3 pick for the 2023 second-round pick in the final year of his contract. Safety Tyler Nubin is another recent second-round pick who appears to be on the verge of losing his starting job. Nubin has been a disappointment in New York, but he could be a buy-low option for a team that liked him in the 2024 draft. Defensive tackle Darius Alexander is yet another recent Day 2 pick who could be available as his role has been diminished. The 2025 third-round pick has essentially become unplayable against the run, and he could be made even more expendable if the Giants trade for a defensive tackle. We’re about to find out just how different these Giants are with chance to end ugly Eagles history | New York Post What comes next is not the most severe football challenge but it is an emotional and psychological hurdle, considering what the rival Eagles have inflicted upon the Giants and their fans for more than a decade. “Philly is a very raucous atmosphere to play in, the fans are super similar to our fans up here,’’ said guard Jon Runyan Jr. “The only difference is they’ve had something to cheer about the last couple of years recently. I’m hoping the tables turn a little bit. I feel like they have. It’s up to us to go down there and take care of business. I think we have what we need. We split with them last year so I think we’re building in the right direction.’’ Banks: Kayvon’s value beyond stats #5 is beyond the stat sheet for his team. New @BleavNetwork pod👇🏾 https://t.co/GygObWhrHc pic.twitter.com/7c7Uq2dudq — Carl Banks (@CarlBanksGIII) November 3, 2026 John Harbaugh rejects inheriting Giants’ road losing streak vs. Eagles | USAToday.com When asked about the Giants’ 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia dating to 2013, Harbaugh dismissed any notion that the current team inherits that history. He used an analogy about rejecting an unwanted burden. “I’m trying to think of the analogy because inherit is an interesting word,” Harbaugh said. “You’re sitting there, you’re sitting at one of those, I’ve only seen them on movies where they all go into the lawyer’s office and they read the will, right? What would that be akin to, a 13-game losing streak that you inherit? Yeah, you can say like, no thanks, that’s what I would probably say is like. I’d say like, I’m not up for that, so I’m going to say no thanks to that. Yeah, I didn’t know that, and I probably didn’t need to know that. Yeah, we don’t care, we don’t care about that.” 2026 midseason rookie grades | CBSSports.com 5. Arvell Reese, LB, Giants: A+. Remember all those concerns about Reese’s pro day workout? Seven months later and he’s one of the easiest evaluations in the class because he’s doing exactly what made him such an exciting prospect at Ohio State. Instincts, range, and insane athleticism, while learning on the job, have all made him an immediate difference-maker, and Giants coaches have praised how quickly he’s hit the ground running. 10. Francis Mauigoa, OG, Giants: C+. The move from college tackle to NFL guard hasn’t been seamless, but Mauigoa has steadily gotten better. His athleticism and ability to move defenders in the running game stood out at Miami, although he occasionally struggled with balance and hand placement. Those issues have followed him inside, but his improved pass protection, especially vs. Houston in Week 7, was encouraging. title: NY Giants give veteran cornerback 3-year contract extension
summary: Veteran cornerback Greg Newsome II has signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension ($32 million guaranteed), according to a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz. Newsome, a 2021 first-round pick by the Cleveland Browns, signed a one-year, $7 million contract with the Giants during the offseason. A three-year extension would run through 2029, with guaranteed […]
full_text: Greg Newsome | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Veteran cornerback Greg Newsome II has signed a three-year, $46 million contract extension ($32 million guaranteed), according to a report from NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Newsome, a 2021 first-round pick by the Cleveland Browns, signed a one-year, $7 million contract with the Giants during the offseason. A three-year extension would run through 2029, with guaranteed money likely over the first two seasons. Newsome had three good seasons with Cleveland to start his career. His play declined in 2024, though, and when that continued into 2025 the Browns dealt him to the Jacksonville Jaguars midseason. The 26-year-old was hoping for a resurgence in a defense suited to his skillset when he joined the Giants. “I feel like this is an opportunity for me to be here long-term,” Newsome said shortly after signing with the Giants. “There [were] other places that could have had a little bit longer-term deal, but I wanted to be here, and I wanted to showcase myself in front of the New York fan base and my coaches and players. I’m excited to start fresh here now and hopefully we get something done where I can retire a Giant, because that’s what I want to do.] “With my game, my strong suit I think is playing press man coverage,” Newsome said. “That was something that we did in Cleveland all the time was playing man-to-man, getting in people’s face and challenging guys. So that’s where I feel like my strong suit is. Improvement, I feel like all of my game can improve. If you’re not trying to improve on everything, then you’re not trying to be a great player. I think just improving on all – press, everything, I feel like there’s always something that I can get better at.” Newsome has, indeed, had a resurgent season. He earned a starting job, and his 62.0 passer rating against is the best of his career. So, too, is his reception percentage allowed of 57.7. Newsome is ranked 18th of 106 qualifying cornerbacks by Pro Football and Sports Network with an Impact Score of 82.6. That would be a career-best if it holds for the entire season. Now that a deal with Newsome is done, might the Giants also try to get an extension completed with Deonte Banks?

title: NY Giants trade candidate: Jets RB Breece Hall
summary: The New York Giants are widely thought to be in hot pursuit of Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, hoping to get a deal done before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Perhaps that deal would also bring the Giants veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart. What, though, if that doesn’t materialize? Could the Giants turn […]
full_text: Breece Hall | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The New York Giants are widely thought to be in hot pursuit of Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor, hoping to get a deal done before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Perhaps that deal would also bring the Giants veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart. What, though, if that doesn’t materialize? Could the Giants turn to the crosstown New York Jets for the big-time running back Giants head coach John Harbaugh has clearly sought since taking the job? The Jets say they are not interested in trading Breece Hall . “We’re in the business of keeping good players and he’s one of our better players. So, Breece will still be here,” said Jets head coach Aaron Glenn. Still, plans change. The Tennessee Titans were adamant they were not trading star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons — until the Chicago Bears made them an offer they could not refuse. Connor Hughes, who covers both the Jets and Giants for SNY TV, told me the Jets would have to be “blown away” by an offer to trade the 25-year-old Hall, a 2022 second-round pick. Hughes told me that the inclusion of a second-round pick in any trade package would likely cause the Jets “have a discussion about” moving Hall. Why it would work Hall doesn’t have the resume of Taylor, Saquon Barkley, or Derrick Henry. He has just one 1,000-yard season in four full years. Perhaps, though, that can be explained at least in part by the Jets going 24-52 during Hall’s tenure. You can’t run the ball when you are always chasing. The good part of that from an acquiring team’s perspective is that Hall has just 1,004 touches in the NFL and should have a lot of mileage remaining. The Athletic lists Hall as its No. 7 potential trade candidate , and the best potentially available back after Taylor. Harbaugh said this week that the Giants need to keep both the short- and long-term in mind with limited draft capital to deal from. At 25 and signed through 2028, Hall would do that. Why it wouldn’t work If it would take a first-round pick to acquire Hall, that is probably a bridge too far for the Giants. The other factor is health. Hall is expected back this week, but has missed five weeks with a right quad injury. The Giants would need to be sure Hall is ready to help them right away.

title: NY Giants are betting favorite to win NFC East, and have John Harbaugh to thank
summary: The New York Giants are now the betting favorite to win the NFC East, per FanDuel Sportsbook. The 4-2-1 division-leading Giants are -134 to win their first division title since 2011. The Dallas Cowboys are +220, the Washington Commanders +400, and the Philadelphia Eagles +1600. The struggles of the division’s other three underachieving teams have […]
full_text: The New York Giants are now the betting favorite to win the NFC East, per FanDuel Sportsbook . The 4-2-1 division-leading Giants are -134 to win their first division title since 2011. The Dallas Cowboys are +220, the Washington Commanders +400, and the Philadelphia Eagles +1600. The struggles of the division’s other three underachieving teams have opened the door for the Giants. Head coach John Harbaugh, though, deserves most of the credit. Harbaugh, the $100 million coach the Giants successfully courted after the Baltimore Ravens fired him following 18 seasons, made his team believe it could do what it has done so far. Harbaugh, 63, gave a huge hint of what was to come at his introductory press conference in January. Asked if he considered taking a year off from coaching after the Ravens let him go, Harbaugh scoffed at the idea. “I figured I didn’t have enough time to take time off,” Harbaugh said. “There’s no time for that, so just couldn’t wait to get back to work. That was never a question.” There is something else Harbaugh doesn’t have time for. Rebuilding, or accepting that circumstances — like major injuries at crucial positions — will derail hopes of a good season. “We have an opportunity to go win, and I like these players, man,” Harbaugh said at that introductory press conference. “I know they want to be successful and they want to go to work, so absolutely we can do that, and that’s our plan to do that. The plan is to win every game. I mean, one game at a time. You go into every game planning to win that game. That’s our expectation.” Harbaugh has driven the Giants to have the best, most productive day possible every day. Harbaugh’s Giants put in as many hours and practice as hard as the rules will allow. “You do the best you can with it every single day. Well, that means a lot when you really think about what that means,” Harbaugh said. “Are we really doing our best? Are we really putting everything we have into it for this day? Are we really attacking the day with an enthusiasm unknown to mankind? Another level? Is that possible? Is that something that we can accomplish? Can we have the best meeting and the best practice in the history of the National Football League? Can we? When you do that day by day, you build something, you take it onto the field, and you let the chips fly, and you go play some ball.” So far, a lot of the chips have fallen in the Giants’ favor. In 18 seasons in Baltimore, Harbaugh’s teams made the playoffs 12 times, had just three losing seasons, and won a Super Bowl. He did not have to convince anyone he knew what he was doing. “It started from day one in the spring. Coach (John Harbaugh) came in here and just the details, the messaging, the leadership. His record speaks for itself as a head coach. The guy has won a lot of games,” GM Joe Schoen said during the bye week. “The players were eager to buy in. We have a good, young nucleus of players here that just want to win. Just want to win, whatever it takes. Coach Harbaugh and his staff have done a very good job of laying out the plan. This is what it looks like. This is how you practice. This is how you approach OTA’s. This is how you approach the offseason program. This is how you train in training camp. This is how you prepare in-season, week to week.” If Harbaugh were building instead of trying to win as often as possible, he probably wouldn’t have brought so many ex-Ravens with him. Giving 33-year-old Odell Beckham a chance, even though it didn’t work out, was about trying to field the best team Harbaugh could right now. Trading for J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart’s Week 2 season-ending injury was a clear sign that Harbaugh wasn’t tossing in the towel on the season, despite whatever long-term quarterback drama that move eventually brings with it. Going after Jeffery Simmons and Jonathan Taylor on the trade market is about capitalizing on the opportunity the Giants have, not building for a better tomorrow. Who can challenge the Giants? None of the Giants’ NFC East challengers have had the seasons they imagined. I asked the lead writers from Blogging the Boys (Cowboys), Bleeding Green Nation (Eagles), and Hogs Haven (Commanders) for thoughts on whether they felt their teams could challenge for the crown, and who would eventually win the division. At 3-5, Dallas is in second place. The Cowboys already have a loss to the Giants. They have losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Arizona Cardinals. They haven’t fixed their defensive issues, with young defensive coordinator Christian Parker looking like he might not be ready for the job. Owner Jerry Jones is being asked about head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s future. Despite that, R.J. Ochoa of Blogging the Boys is still a believer that the Cowboys will pull themselves together and win the division. “The Dallas Cowboys will in the most basic, bare bones, literal way possible. “I say this because of the non-Giants teams in the division; the Cowboys might be the least fallible. On paper, the Cowboys have pieces that comprise contending/challenging teams, but they have not been anything close to their on-paper version so far this season. “They deserve no benefit of the doubt right now. Everyone keeps believing they will put together a little run to make “challenging” a thing, but they are losing to hapless teams like the Buccaneers and Cardinals. “Congratulations to the Giants on a successful start to the John Harbaugh era. The Eagles, entering Sunday’s game with the Giants, have lost a stunning six games in a row. They have lost an immense amount of talent, including quarterback Jalen Hurts to injury. They have traded away players like A.J. Brown and Cam Jurgens, and watched right tackle Lane Johnson retire during the season. Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation is taking the Cowboys to emerge as champs. “The Eagles will not. “The Eagles are arguably the worst team in the NFL. It’s hard to see how things are going to get better for them this season. “The Giants certainly have a good energy going for them as they currently sit atop the division. But quarterback uncertainty remains. The Cowboys could eventually wake up; they have the NFL’s sixth-easiest remaining schedule. I’ll take Dallas to very narrowly edge the Giants.” The 2-4-1 Commanders lost quarterback Jayden Daniels for two games, and have been beset by clock management issues. It is hard to count them out, though. Scott Bair of Hogs Haven isn’t quite sure what to expect from the Commanders. “The Commanders have the most talented quarterback in the division. Notice the word choice there. I said most talented. I did not say best. Not while he’s learning a new scheme and seemingly a bit hesitant to let it rip. The rest of the team is not strong enough to contend with the Giants unless he’s Superman, and Daniels isn’t currently wearing the cape. “So, to answer your question, I can’t quite answer it yet. “That Thursday night game against the Giants in Week 10 will tell us everything. If Daniels becomes JD5 and flashes the logo on his chest on that night, he’ll answer the question for you. “If he’s hot, Washington goes on a heater and Big Blue is in trouble. Their defensive players have nearly (but not quite) figured this new blitz-heavy scheme out. If he remains timid or slightly out of sync, then the Giants cruise. “Week 10, baby. Get your popcorn ready.” As the Giants return from their bye, they have games against the Eagles and Commanders in five days. Harbaugh knows what they mean. “The two most important games of the season will be coming up after we come back from the bye, which will set the direction for the rest of the season really,” Harbaugh said after the Week 7 victory over the Houston Texans. Can the Giants pull this off? Maybe, maybe not. Watching it unfold, though, will certainly be better than already being knee-deep in draft talk.

title: Cam Skattebo injury: NY Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles
summary: Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team’s Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the […]
full_text: Cam Skattebo | Getty Images Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team’s Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo’s injury in more detail. “It’s going to be probably day to day up to the game,” Harbaugh said. ”We’re going to just have to see where we’re at. I’ll probably have more information toward the end of the week. We’ll see on both those guys where we’re at.“ Skattebo has had an up-and-down season for the Giants. He scored a touchdown in the team’s Week 1 win against the Dallas Cowboys, but struggled to find the end zone in the next four weeks. He also recorded four fumbles in the team’s first five games. His struggles led to him being benched in the team’s Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road. Skattebo likely will have a big role when the team plays the Philadelphia Eagles this week if he is able to go. Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation.
