title: The Brock Purdy-Mike Evans connection: How good has it been so far?
summary: The San Francisco 49ers moved into the top seed in the NFC during their bye week after the Minnesota Vikings lost. Moving up one spot without playing a game is impressive, but it’s not as impressive as the Brock Purdy-Mike Evans pairing in 2026. Evans left the game against Washington after a huge first half […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers moved into the top seed in the NFC during their bye week after the Minnesota Vikings lost. Moving up one spot without playing a game is impressive, but it’s not as impressive as the Brock Purdy-Mike Evans pairing in 2026. Evans left the game against Washington after a huge first half while dealing with Achilles tendonitis and missed the game in Atlanta, which was the team’s first loss. From the very beginning, the duo looked like they had played together for years. The trust and ball placement from Purdy were on full display, and a motivated Evans is out to prove he is still operating at a high level. Just how good has the pair been? As far as QB/WR duos, the two 49ers rank fourth in the league with a passer rating of 148.5. The two rank fourth in EPA/play, also at +1.06. Purdy to Evans ranks fifth in yards/target at 13.2. Of Evans 27 receptions, 25 have gone for a first down or touchdown. According to Pro Football Focus , Purdy has a big-time throw rate of 18,4% when targeting Evans, and that is the second-highest mark in the NFL. Purdy hasn’t been intercepted on any attempt to Evans. Early Down Rate Early downs: 20 targets, 53% target share, 150.0 passer rating, 14.7 yards/target, and +1.09 EPA Later downs: 18 targets, 47% target share, 142.4 passer rating, 11.4 yards/target, and +1.03 EPA Pressure Under pressure: 12 targets, 32% target share, 102.1 passer rating, 10.7 yards/target, and +0.64 EPA Clean pocket: 26 targets, 68% target share, 154.6 passer rating, 14.3 yards/target, and +1.25 EPA Blitz VS blitz: 8 targets, 21% target share, 158.3 passer rating, 19.1 yards/target, and +1.93 EPA No blitz: 30 targets, 79% target share, 128.1 passer rating, 11.6 yards/target, and +0.83 EPA Play Action Play Action: 5 targets, 13% target share, 118.8 passer rating, 15.2 yards/target, and +1.18 EPA No play action: 33 targets, 87% target share, 151.8 passer rating, 12.8 yards/target, and +1.04 EPA These numbers confirm what your eyes are telling you. Evans is the biggest piece of the 49ers’ offense. Suffice it to say, the 49ers need Evans the rest of the way and down the stretch to compete for a Lombardi. The pairing has been perfect and a blast to watch. Let’s make sure that continues.
author: Jason Aponte

title: DeForest Buckner gets his old number back
summary: Not that it was ever a mystery, DeForest Buckner’s return to the San Francisco 49ers means he’s getting his old No. 99 back. That number has been worn by second-year defensive tackle CJ West. Buckner said he got to know West last week and the two were talking, where West told Buckner, “Hey, bro, 99 […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not that it was ever a mystery, DeForest Buckner’s return to the San Francisco 49ers means he’s getting his old No. 99 back. That number has been worn by second-year defensive tackle CJ West. Buckner said he got to know West last week and the two were talking, where West told Buckner, “Hey, bro, 99 is yours.” West will wear No. 90. Buckner didn’t need to ask for the number. He said West offered it to him. Buckner vowed to “take care” of West, even though CJ asked for nothing in return. Buckner denied telling the Colts he only wanted to be traded to the 49ers. He also wouldn’t say whether he’s discussed or focused on a potential extension with the 49ers after this season. His focus is on the remainder of the season. “Fred and I were just talking in the cafe this morning. You really wanna be a team on the rise. This is a part of the season where, you know, some teams start falling off. The really select group continues to rise and get better every week. That’s what I’m doing. That’s what I’m trying to do.” During Buckner’s press conference on Monday, he said some of his new teammates told him Kris Kocurek plays a lot of 2019 film as teaching tape. The nostalgia is great, but the 49ers brought in Buckner to do a job and do it at a high level. He said he plans to do everything he can to help elevate the defensive line room. When asked about the immediate impact he could make, Buckner leaned into his experience, but also wants to help the young players in the room: “There’s a lot of young guys in the room. I’m an open book. If they want to pick my brain and ask me questions, I’m always an open book to all of them. It doesn’t take just one or two guys to make a room or make a team. It’s the entire room. I’ve always believed that the d-line is the engine of the team. And I wanna pour into those young guys everything that I know, so I can help their game and get even better.” How the snaps look with Buckner in the fold is one of the more intriguing parts about the defense moving forward. Buckner still has the stamina to play 70-75% of the time. That means whoever is next to him will be rotated quite a bit to keep them fresh.
author: Kyle Posey

title: The 49ers are reportedly ‘still looking for a receiver and a pass rusher’
summary: NFL insider Jordan Schultz told The Pivot podcast what to expect ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Unprompted, he brought up the San Francisco 49ers: Last week, I talked about San Francisco and Chicago. Those were two teams that I thought would be really active. Now, the Bears landed [Jeffery] Simmons in a blockbuster. San […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | Kirby Lee-Imagn Images NFL insider Jordan Schultz told The Pivot podcast what to expect ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Unprompted, he brought up the San Francisco 49ers: Last week, I talked about San Francisco and Chicago. Those were two teams that I thought would be really active. Now, the Bears landed [Jeffery] Simmons in a blockbuster. San Francisco got [DeForest] Buckner. So we were in on that. But Ryan, I don’t think either team is done. I think the 49ers are still looking for a receiver and a pass rusher. I wouldn’t rule out another move for either team. There’s a lot of Khalil Mack buzz for both clubs. The Jets have made it clear they’re not looking to trade their stars, including Garrett Wilson. But there has been some curiousity around Breece Hall, so we’ll see what happens there. Earlier in the segment, Schultz said these were the trade targets to watch: Brian Thomas Jr. – Jaguars Jauan Jennings – Vikings Calvin Ridley – Titans Jerry Jeudy – Browns Kayshon Boutte – Texans Hollywood Brown – Eagles Schultz followed that up by saying, “But the biggest name around the league that people are really starting to get curious about is George Pickens in Dallas. He’s playing on the franchise tag. He has not been utilized the same way as last year. ” The market for a pass rusher may not involve as many names as wide receiver. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh recently said, “I want Khalil Mack here. Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team.” The Jets have Will McDonald IV, who had a sack in Week 8, but can go long stretches without making an impact. Arizona has a pass rusher in Josh Sweat who I believe teams will overpay for, if he’s moved at all. It’s hard to imagine the Cardinals going out of their way to make the 49ers better.

title: NFC West Recap: Seahawks, Rams go opposite ways to .500
summary: The San Francisco 49ers didn’t play in Week 8 and still sit at 6-1 atop the NFC West. While they are on bye, the best thing could have happened: The Seahawks got embarrassed at home, dropping a game to the Chicago Bears and putting them 2.5 games back in the division race. The 49ers may […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JANUARY 03: Head coach Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers interacts with head coach Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks after an NFL game on January 3, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers didn’t play in Week 8 and still sit at 6-1 atop the NFC West. While they are on bye, the best thing could have happened: The Seahawks got embarrassed at home, dropping a game to the Chicago Bears and putting them 2.5 games back in the division race. The 49ers may have been on bye, but they weren’t quiet. They brought back defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick, six years after trading him away. He joins a beat-up defensive line that pressured Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. on just three of 34 dropbacks in the Week 7 loss. Help is on the way! Seattle Seahawks (4-4) So much for the Kansas City Chiefs momentum. The defending Super Bowl champions got pushed around on their own field on Monday Night Football, losing 34-17 to the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field. Many may have seen a Bears victory. I don’t think anyone expected the Bears to blow this thing wide open in the fourth quarter, up by three points, and have the Seahawks do Seahawks things to bring them back. After a backbreaking Colston Loveland fumble, the Seahawks not only managed to score a touchdown, but also got a two-point conversion to be down by three points. You know how these games go. Chicago was a bit shaky covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba—something I see lots of defenses do, and I just don’t get it. Chicago’s offense was humming sporadically, but it seemed like the Seahawks were waking up to win this one. Then this happened: When you call a screen you hope it’s blocked up as well as this was. Big-time play by Chicago. pic.twitter.com/n19LGEi43s — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) November 3, 2026 That was enough to open the floodgates. Final score: 34-17 Bears. Seattle got guard Quenton Nelson in a trade from the Indianapolis Colts, as well as running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returning from injury. Despite this, the running game still went nowhere. After Sam Darnold threw an interception late that he didn’t even seem to realize was a pick, you have to wonder if there’s a quarterback problem in Seattle. Sure, Seattle is now 2.5 games back, and that’s great for 49ers fans. The bigger question is the Bears. Did they need to be that scary in embarrassing Seattle? Los Angeles Rams (4-4) With a 24-9 win over the Chargers, the Rams are 4-4. That’s right, t hey have Ram’d it to .500 . The Los Angeles Rams beat the winless Los Angeles Chargers 24-9 at SoFi Stadium in the battle for L.A. nobody asked for. It wasn’t pretty. The Rams didn’t pick up a first down on their first five drives, and they haven’t scored a touchdown on an opening drive all season. They led a 0-7 team just 10-9 at halftime. But this is the Chargers. While the Rams haven’t scored a touchdown on an opening drive all season, the Chargers haven’t won a game all season. That’s right, defense carries this one. Rams safety Quentin Lake and cornerback Trent McDuffie each picked off Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, and the field goals were the only type of points the Chargers could muster. Running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum both combined for 129 yards rushing while getting a touchdown each. Quarterback Matthew Stafford finished 17-of-25 for 157 yards passing and an interception. Not exactly the encore to an MVP season. As I said, this was mostly a defensive game and the Rams’ running backs. So the Rams own Levi’s South SoFi Stadium and are also back to .500. Credit where credit is due. Arizona Cardinals (3-5) We don’t even need to recap this game; rather, we will just jump to 1:35 in the third quarter. Because that’s when Jacoby Brissett got benched for Gardner Minshew. And that means Minshew Magic. Also known as the QB, a bad defense like the Cowboys didn’t prepare for. You may need some audio to read the rest of this—call it setting the mood. Don’t worry, I’m here to help. Open this song in another tab and then continue reading. So, 1:35 in the third quarter. Starting there, Arizona scored four touchdowns in regulation and would have won outright if kicker Chad Ryland hadn’t missed an extra point. Instead, it went to overtime, where a field goal sealed a 33-30 win over the Dallas Cowboys. It’s fair to note that overtime came with just over a minute left in the game. Minshew took the Cardinals down the field and scored. Had the Cardinals made the extra point, there would have been no overtime. Between Brissett and Minshew, the split tells the story. Brissett went 10-of-23 for 119 yards passing and an interception in nearly three quarters. Minshew went 17-of-23 for 188 yards passing, and three touchdowns in less than two, and three of his incompletions were spikes to stop the clock. He even got Cardinals legend Larry Fitzgerald’s attention with throws like this: You changed my life @GardnerMinshew5 this throw is ABSURD https://t.co/beQW4JMc81 pic.twitter.com/VK6s0lhEv1 — LegacyFitz (@LegacyFitz11) November 2, 2026 Beyond Minshew saving the day, another fun stat brought up during the broadcast is the Cardinals’ record in AT&T Stadium: they are undefeated. Nothing much has changed. Hey, the Cardinals might be an NFC West rival, but I’m sure most of the people reading this would rather the Cowboys lose than the Cardinals win. And that was an epic loss for the Cowboys—one for the ages. Onto Week 9 The 49ers come off the bye to host the Las Vegas Raiders. Las Vegas went into Week 8 at 3-4 on a four-game skid, then visited the New York Jets. And they could have lost to the New York Jets. They wound up beating the New York Jets 38-33. Kirk Cousins hasn’t been traded yet, so that game should be a headache for the 49ers, as Cousins seems to have career days against them. Seattle hosts Arizona at Lumen Field in the week’s only division game. The Seahawks won the first meeting and can’t afford another loss. The Cardinals are running high on Minshew, who has been named the starting quarterback. Hopefully they can forget they are the Cardinals for one more game. The Rams head east to face the 2-4-1 Washington Commanders, who hosted the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night. The Eagles have worse injury issues than the 49ers, it seems like, and got smacked on Sunday Night Football. It’s the NFC East, but the Commanders can be sneaky on offense. The 49ers are starting to pull away in a competitive division, but it isn’t over yet. Commanders, make us proud. 1st: San Francisco 49ers ; Next: vs. Las Vegas Raiders 2nd: Seattle Seahawks ; Next: vs. Arizona Cardinals 3rd: Los Angeles Rams ; Next: at Washington Commanders 4th: Arizona Cardinals ; Next: at Seattle Seahawks

title: 3 players the Titans should try trading before the deadline
summary: The NFL trade deadline is officially less than one week away (Nov. 10). The Tennessee Titans are obviously sellers at the deadline following their decision to trade star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for two first-round picks and an additional fourth-round selection. The Simmons trade poses a question: Who else […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Jermaine Johnson II #11 of the Tennessee Titans looks on during the second half of the Week 3 preseason game against the Chicago Bears at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The NFL trade deadline is officially less than one week away (Nov. 10). The Tennessee Titans are obviously sellers at the deadline following their decision to trade star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for two first-round picks and an additional fourth-round selection. The Simmons trade poses a question: Who else will GM Mike Borgonzi look to trade before the deadline? We’ve identified three players Borgonzi should try moving for more draft capital. DE Jermaine Johnson II Jermaine Johnson has been fairly inconsistent as a pass rusher. The Titans acquired his fifth-year rookie contract option when they traded T’Vondre Sweat to the New York Jets for him. That means Johnson is on an expiring contract. He’s a good NFL player who also sets hard edges as a run defender, but getting a draft pick back for an expiring contract would be a worthwhile move. His familiarity with Robert Saleh’s defense could keep him in Tennessee, but trading him would free up more snaps for Femi Oladejo and Keldric Faulk. LB Cody Barton Veteran linebacker Cody Barton has begun losing snaps to Cedric Gray in recent weeks. Most Titans fans are surprised it took this long. Gray and Anthony Hill Jr. are the future tandem for Coach Saleh’s defense. Barton is signed through 2027, which could make trading him a little complicated. He’s not on an expiring contract, but any postseason contending team searching for experienced linebacker help should have interest. RB Tyjae Spears Could the Titans receive anything in return for Tyjae Spears? It’s a question Mike Borgonzi should be asking. Tony Pollard has been exceptional in recent weeks and Spears is also on an expiring contract. He’s an athletic dual-threat back who is especially productive on passing downs. Perhaps there’s an offense in the market for another third-down playmaker.

full_text: The Daily Slop – 4 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Bullock’s Film Room Commanders Film Review: Pass Rush vs Eagles Coming off the bye, they were hoping to turn things around and against the Eagles they certainly did. They delivered five sacks and multiple other pressures. According to NextGenStats, the Commanders had a season-high pressure rate at 46.5%. When they blitzed, they had a pressure rate of 83.3%, the second highest pressure rate on blitzes by any team in the NFL this season. So how did the Commanders do it? During the bye week, I wrote about some schemes that worked which they could use more frequently, and we definitely saw them come up against the Eagles on Sunday night. Things like read blitzes, disguised overloads and B gap stabs were all effective against the Eagles. The Commanders pass rush was under the microscope over the bye week, but against the Eagles they generated 5 sacks and a ton of pressure. Is this sustainable success? I took a closer look: https://t.co/7k6fTzlSnl pic.twitter.com/5QKuOo7s0u — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 4, 2026 This rush is Chaisson at his absolute best. He’s so quick off the snap and his speed is a real threat to any tackle when he gets it right. Mailata is one of the best left tackles in football and very few rushers beat him for speed, but Chaisson does exactly that here. Chaisson times the snap perfectly and by his second step, he’s already hip level with Mailata. He gets Mailata panicked and forces the tackle to completely turn around to try and stay with him. Mailata gets his outside hand on Chaisson’s shoulder, but Chaisson shows nice bend and dip as he gets under Mailata and turns the corner. Mailata makes one last effort to save the block by shoving Chaisson, trying to push him beyond the depth of the quarterback, but the quarterback fails to feel the pressure and step up in the pocket. That allows Chaisson to use that shove as momentum to close even quicker. Chaisson lands a big hit on the quarterback, who just about manages to get a throw away before Chaisson brings him down. That throw looked like it might have been intercepted by Nick Cross, but Shy Tuttle got his hand up at the line of scrimmage to knock it down. Towards the end of the game, Odafe Oweh got in on the action too. Oweh spent most of the game working against Mailata, the Eagles best lineman, so he wasn’t as effective overall as the other rushers. But by getting to work against the same man constantly, he was able to figure out ways to beat him. By the end of the game, Oweh got the better of him. Overall, the Commanders will of course be happy with the uptick from their pass rush unit in this game. They generated much more consistent pressure and of course finished those plays, putting up five sacks. However, this felt to me much more like the Eagles offensive line being bad than the Commanders pass rush being exceptionally good. Don’t get me wrong, you can only play against whoever the opponent puts out there each week, so I’m not trying to discredit this performance. But I do wonder how sustainable it is. The Commanders blitzed at a significantly lower rate than they have done all season. Much of these pressures and sacks came on four-man rushes. We’ve seen through the first six games of the season that this pass rush isn’t good enough to consistently win with four, and that Daronte Jones has had to blitz a lot and dial up various pressure packages in order to generate consistent pressure. This game doesn’t line up with that theme so far this season, which speaks to an issue with the Eagles offensive line rather than some big adjustment the Commanders made over the bye week. Individually, everyone played well up front. Chaisson had perhaps his best game in a Commanders uniform. Omenihu was a menace to whoever had to try and block him on the inside. Armstrong got the better of Bell frequently. Oweh had a solid game against one of the best tackles in the league. While Oweh and Chaisson had some very good reps against Mailata, they’ve had some very good reps individually in lots of games this season and the overall rush unit hasn’t looked this good. So I’m reluctant to say that this group has turned the corner. I definitely believe in their talent and I like the unit overall, but I’m eager to see if they can stack up performances like that against a Rams team with a much stronger offensive line. Commanders.com Final thoughts | Updates on McNichols, pass-rush is more in sync — Both Trey Amos and Nick Cross, who missed extended portions of the season with various injuries, are getting more comfortable by the week. Quinn thought Cross operated well as the nickel defensive back, while Amos had a pair of key pass breakups. It also feels like their presence has helped stabilize the secondary, which needed reinforcements. “I really felt his communication in this game, the urgency of what we’re looking for from that,” Quinn said of Cross. “So, I thought that was a good step forward as well.” — One of the biggest storylines from Sunday’s game was how quarterback Jayden Daniels brought the offense together after going down 10-0 to rally the unit. It apparently worked, because the Commanders went on to score 27 unanswered points after that. Quinn said he loved the Daniels took charge. “There comes a point when it’s enough is enough and this is not a game plan specific one that can be all the way tricked out that’s hard to do. And so, for he and for his teammates to look one another in the eye and say, ‘Okay, let’s get this part of our football in order and do this now.’ It’s usually more effective that way. So the fact that it didn’t have to be me as the one doing that, I thought was good. Obviously, frustration and all that builds in, so I like it when that happens.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN 2026 NFL trade deadline: Players to watch, buzz and goals for all 32 teams Washington Commanders (2-4-1) Chance to make playoffs: 11.6% Projected first-round draft slot: No. 9 What is the deadline goal? Get better. It’s an obvious goal for any team, but it’s also how Washington views the situation and why the Commanders wouldn’t consider themselves too active in looking to acquire or trade players based on their record. Even if, say, they lost to the Rams on Sunday and started to trade veterans on one-year deals for draft picks, they could still look to add talent, too — not for this season alone but for the long hall. A player such as Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. would make sense. He has a high ceiling at a position they will need help at in 2027. Washington could also use more help at running back and offensive line. The Commanders have seven draft picks in 2027, the first time since 2024 that they have all of their selections. — John Keim Who could be on the move? Offensive tackle Andrew Wylie. Wylie is an swing-tackle type on an inexpensive contract who could be of interest in a market in which every team is looking for offensive line help and there’s rarely any available. — Graziano Who should they target? Chargers RB Kimani Vidal. One spot at which Washington could use an upgrade is running back. Commanders running backs have amassed minus-69 rush yards over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. title: NFL trade deadline: A deep dive into potential Commanders targets
summary: Once again, Washington finds itself at a familiar crossroads as the NFL trade deadline approaches, trapped in the classic dilemma of whether to buy or sell. However, the internal and external landscape has shifted dramatically. The team’s presumed primary trade target, left guard Quenton Nelson was shipped off to Seattle, while their most valuable trade […]
full_text: Once again, Washington finds itself at a familiar crossroads as the NFL trade deadline approaches, trapped in the classic dilemma of whether to buy or sell. However, the internal and external landscape has shifted dramatically. The team’s presumed primary trade target, left guard Quenton Nelson was shipped off to Seattle , while their most valuable trade asset , Daron Payne, was lost for the season after suffering a Jones fracture in his foot. While most front offices in this precarious position would choose to stand pat and do nothing, Washington’s circumstances are uniquely complicated. The NFC East remains wide open. Philadelphia is officially tanking, Dallas is imploding and the Giants are an incredibly flawed unit. Because no one else seems to want the division, a playoff berth remains a long, but realistic shot. On the flip side, Washington has glaring roster holes, and the coaching staff hasn’t inspired enough confidence to make a true postseason push feel believable. Ultimately, Sunday’s matchup against the Rams will likely act as the pendulum that swings the front office in one direction or the other. In the meantime, a comprehensive blueprint outlines the names to consider selling — and the pieces to look at bringing in. Selling EDGE Dorrance Armstrong Dorance Armstrong finally got himself on the sack scoreboard against Philly, but he increasingly looks like the odd man out in this rotation. He is still working his way back into form after an ACL tear derailed a highly impressive start to his campaign last year. While his current market value might not trigger a bidding war, his status on an expiring contract makes him a prime candidate to move. Getting any draft capital in return is better than letting him walk for nothing. Potential Buyers: Dallas Cowboys, Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Cincinnati Bengals EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson I’m really against trading K’Lavon Chaisson, as he has arguably been the team’s most effective pure pass rusher and fits Daronte Jones’ defensive scheme to a tee. However, he is also on an one-year deal , which automatically makes him Washington’s most valuable healthy trade asset. Contending teams are always desperate for EDGE help down the stretch, meaning Chaisson would command a robust market and bring back the highest return if the front office decides to pivot toward the future. Potential Buyers: San Francisco 49ers, Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Cincinnati Bengals. OL Andrew Wylie While casual observers might scoff at Wylie’s trade value; experienced, plug-and-play veteran offensive linemen are incredibly difficult to find midseason. Wylie has built a steady reputation across the league as a stable, high-floor, yet unspectacular right tackle who can also play inside. For a contender dealing with a sudden injury along the front five, Wylie represents an affordable insurance policy who won’t derail an offense. Potential Buyers: Teams requiring immediate, veteran tackle depth or frontline protection stability. QB Marcus Mariota Put the pitchforks down for just a second and hear this out. Everyone knows how vital a high-level backup quarterback is in today’s NFL, especially with Jayden Daniels playing a physical brand of football where a single bad hit puts the season in Mariota’s hands. However, multiple teams are desperate for immediate quarterback stability and are willing to overpay. If Mariota genuinely wants another shot to start, Washington could leverage that desire into significant draft capital. While a trade remains highly unlikely given his value as a locker room mentor and insurance policy, every player has a price tag if the right offer rolls in. Potential Buyers: Baltimore Ravens, Minnesota Vikings DBs Mikey Sainristil & Quan Martin These two young defensive backs belong in the same conversation because they present nearly identical dilemmas. If a buyer emerges for either player, it will be a team looking to gamble on their raw traits, hoping a change of scenery can salvage their development and unlock their potential in a different system. At this stage, if a front office offers even an ounce of real draft value for either defender, management should take the deal immediately and run. Potential Buyers: Buffalo Bills, Pittsburgh Steelers, Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions . Buyers Running Backs Jonathan Taylor The potential pairing of Jayden Daniels and Jonathan Taylor in the same backfield is nothing short of electrifying. One could easily argue that Taylor represents the most talented, game-changing trade piece currently available on the market. However, that elite pedigree comes with a massive price tag, which might ultimately cause Washington’s front office to hesitate. At 27 years old, Taylor carries a heavy career workload on his body. Trading premium assets for a running back with significant mileage always raises red flags. Yet, if he can maintain his current high level of production, he would instantly become the most dominant skill-position player Daniels has ever shared a huddle with in Washington, completely redefining the team’s offensive identity. Value: Low Day 1 or High Day 2 (plus) pick Tony Pollard It seems someone tipped Pollard off about the deadline rumors because he has put on an absolute clinic over the past two weeks. Pollard remains a highly underappreciated player who provides efficiency both as an interior rusher, and a reliable outlet in the passing game. While he may not be a game changer who completely tilts defensive game plans, he is the exact type of high-floor contributor who helps you win tight football games down the stretch. Hitting the age 30 threshold means his price tag is suppressed, but that exact same age factor might sway front offices away from making a move entirely. Projected Value: Mid-to-low Day 3 pick Breece Hall Despite recently signing an extension with the Jets , history shows that long-term contracts don’t make a player untradeable, look no further than how New York handled Sauce Gardner last year. While Hall is currently sidelined with an injury, his upside remains undeniable. When fully healthy, he is an elite, dynamic weapon out of the backfield, the exact type of premier playmaker that a young quarterback like Jayden Daniels has yet to work with in the NFL. Bringing in an explosive dual-threat like Hall would completely transform the offense’s ceiling. Value: High-to-Mid Day 2 Pick Keaton Mitchell/Omarion Hampton/Kimani Vidal Sitting at a disappointing 0-7, the Chargers are in complete disarray, and their lackluster running game has left a lot to be desired. Ironically, the backfield remains arguably the deepest room on the roster, making it prime real estate for draft capital. Los Angeles needs to accumulate as many assets as possible to jumpstart this rebuild and identify core players who can actually help turn the franchise around. • Omarion Hampton: As the prize of the group, Hampton possesses the true three-down skillset that will likely command a premium. • Projected Value: Day 2 Pick • Keaton Mitchell & Kimani Vidal: Both serve as highly intriguing change-of-pace options who could immediately boost a contender’s depth chart for a much lower entry cost. • Projected Value: High-to-Mid Day 3 Pick Receiver Josh Downs I wasn’t going to write anything about Downs until I saw some reports about him being tied to the team. Downs has been a solid and reliable WR for the Colts given his size he would be a slot WR wherever he goes and at 25, you’re getting a really sound player . I do worry about his next contract. Indy first-hand saw how outrageous the free agent market for WRs can get with the Alec Pierce deal. Investing a ton of money into him while sending out draft capital will the be real question for teams here. Value: High-to-Mid Day 3 Pick Brian Thomas Jr. To be entirely frank, a Brian Thomas Jr. departure from Jacksonville still feels highly improbable. Though a strong argument can be made that the…

full_text: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 31: Defensive back Zach Lutmer #6 of the Iowa Hawkeyes forces a fumble in the second half against wide receiver Tyrell Henry #0 of the Wisconsin Badgers at Kinnick Stadium on October 31, 2026 in Madison, WI. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 9 in college football wasn’t easy for a few of the top teams in the AP Top 25. No. 1 Miami squeaked out a win by relying on their star offensive players Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney. The same could not be said for No. 2 Ohio State. Missing starting quarterback Julian Sayin, the Buckeyes struggled to score in their loss to USC. No. 4 Indiana needed overtime and great plays by wide receiver Charlie Becker to take down Minnesota. Teams like No. 3 Georgia and No. 5 Notre Dame, however, coasted to victory. The first College Football Playoff rankings of the season have been released ahead of a great slate of games in Week 10. The feature matchup of the week will be No. 1 Miami traveling to South Bend, Ind., to face No. 4 Notre Dame. The Holy War will take place in Salt Lake City between No. 3 Utah and No. 7 BYU. Arch Manning and No. 10 Texas will try to continue their strong play against No. 19 Missouri. No. 8 Kentucky visits No. 16 Tennessee while No. 9 Alabama will go on the road to Baton Rouge to face No. 15 LSU. No. 2 Georgia will face one of their stiffest challenges in No. 12 Ole Miss. Here are a few players who had a good week and might be able to help out the Commanders. Let me know what you think about these prospects and feel free to post players that stood out to you: Kevin Jennings | QB | RS Senior | SMU SMU’s Kevin Jennings did all he could to try to get a win for the Mustangs, but they came up a little short versus Syracuse. Let’s get the biggest knock on Jennings out of the way: he’s an incredibly small quarterback at 6’, 195 pounds. Given that he’s a redshirt senior, he probably can’t get much bigger. If you are comfortable with his size, Jennings has a lot of tools at the position. He has a quick release and is an accurate passer. There is good velocity on his passes that helps him fit throws into tight windows and beat coverage. With that said, he doesn’t have a rocket arm, but it is good enough for the pros. He’s also shown the ability to put touch on his passes to get over defenders. Jennings will manipulate coverage with his eyes and pump fakes to help his receivers get open. While he’s not a dazzling runner, Jennings is decisive when he tucks the ball to run. An area where Jennings can improve is getting rid of the ball to avoid sacks. He can hold the ball a beat too long and take sacks unnecessarily. Jennings threw for 352 yards and two touchdowns, going 29 of 36, in a loss. Cole Tabb | RB | Junior | Cincinnati After a thrilling upset of Texas Tech, Cincinnati came back down to earth with a loss to Utah. Cole Tabb , however, is still playing out of this world. A smaller back that’s only 5’8”, 200 pounds, Tabb excels in a zone blocking scheme because of his vision and burst. He can feel the holes developing, find them, and burst through. Once in the open field, Tabb has very good long speed. He’s not the most powerful or elusive runner, but his low center of gravity allows him to break his fair share of tackles. Tabb will also contribute in the passing game, making him a viable third-down back. In the loss to Utah, Tabb had 131 yards on 14 carries and a touchdown. Cincinnati RB Cole Tabb (5-8, 200) has been as productive as any, to the point that he should declare Had THE massive breakout from a 4.1 YPC Stanford career to 9.6 (1st in FBS). Not getting bigger. Hit the road pic.twitter.com/ayXFLRPIzz — Clint Goss (@NFLDraftDome) November 1, 2026 Top 10 Fastest Max Speed | Week 8 1 | 21.1 MPH Cole Tabb @ColeTabb RB Cincinnati #ReelSpeed pic.twitter.com/0QtfJiiUFr — Reel Analytics (@RAanalytics) October 26, 2026 Carlos Hernandez | WR | Senior | Wake Forest Wake Forest is having one of their best seasons in recent memory, with their only loss coming to Miami. Carlos Hernandez has been their best receiver. At 6’, 190 pounds, Hernandez is quick at the top of his routes. That creates the separation he needs to get open. His hands are reliable, even making some tough contested catches despite not being the biggest receiver. He looks to have good speed after the catch. I’d also like to see him beat press man coverage; otherwise, he might be limited to the slot in the NFL. Hernandez made eight catches for 136 yards and a touchdown in the Demon Deacons win over UVA. Jelani Thurman | TE | RS Junior | UNC UNC gave Miami a scare in Chapel Hill, NC, but the Hurricanes survived. Jelani Thurman was a big reason why the Tar Heels had a chance in the game. A transfer from Ohio State, the 6’6”, 245 pounder is an athletic pass catcher. UNC likes to use his speed to out run defenders on crossing routes or to beat defenders down the seam. Improving the diversity of his routes would make him an even more dangerous receiving threat. He’s a competitive blocker who is effective, but needs to work on getting lower to improve his leverage. Thurman had five receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns against Miami. Thurman is tied for second in the nation for receiving touchdowns for tight ends with six. Anthonie Knapp | OG | Junior | Notre Dame Notre Dame is one of the most talented teams in the country thanks to talented players like Anthonie Knapp. Only a true junior, Knapp has started at tackle and guard since his freshman year. He’s an incredibly strong player at 6’5”, 305 pounds. Knapp plays with a wide base and stays balanced in pass protection. Notre Dame uses both gap and zone scheme runs. Knapp excels at both because of his athleticism. He’s an effective puller and lead blocker on gap runs, and he gets to necessary spots to cut off defenders on zone runs. With power and leverage, he can move defenders as a run blocker and plays through the whistle. Notre Dame LG Anthonie Knapp (#54) put some really clean film out against UNC during week 5. One of my favorite OL in this class due to his consistency, technique, and athleticism. pic.twitter.com/oCWjWwJGOx — Jay (@DraftwithJay) October 13, 2026 Sebastian Cheeks | EDGE | Senior | Wisconsin Wisconsin took it on the chin and got shut out by Iowa. Nonetheless, Sebastian Cheeks still had a good day rushing the passer. Cheeks started his career at UNC and has had modest production in previous years. At 6’3”, 243 pounds, Cheeks might be a little undersized to be an edge rusher in a 3-4 defense. He uses his speed and quickness to his advantage. Cheeks converts speed to power effectively, bull rushing blockers into the pocket. If the blocker anchors, his hand usage is good enough to disengage and get to the quarterback. His speed and quickness make him effective running stunts and looping inside on rushes. He is strong enough to hold the edge in the run game but needs to make sure he doesn’t give up contain being too eager to make a play. Cheeks had five tackles and a sack against Iowa. On the defensive side of the ball, Nicholas Rodriguez continued his prolific ways against the Razorbacks. Rodriguez has had double-digit tackles in every game this season except the opener. He’s small at 6’, 225 pounds, but Rodriguez is technically sound as a tackler and he rarely misses. His quickness allows him to sift through the…

title: Will Commanders be on-field winners over the next 5 games? – survey
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Commanders fans and fans across the country. Sign up here to participate in the weekly emailed surveys: Now that the season is well underway, we’re continuing to ask the standard confidence question each week; that is, “Are you confident the Commanders are headed in the right direction?” We’ve been asking that question weekly from September to December for many years. With the Commanders fresh off of a 17-point prime-time victory over the Eagles, and with the overall record standing a 2-4-1 after 7 games, there is a bit of a “2020 season” feel to the current situation, with a weak NFC East and upcoming winnable games. Washington’s next 7 opponents have a combined record of 22-30-1 (.415 win percentage), and only 2 of them — the Giants and Bengals — have winning records. Typically, any team with just one win as the season approaches the halfway mark would be thinking more about the April draft than about January playoffs. But with the Eagles on a 6-game skid, the Cowboys looking as vulnerable as the Commanders themselves, and the Giants struggling to hold onto the division lead with JJ McCarthy behind center, it’s not unrealistic for the Commanders to see themselves as being in contention for the NFC East title and spot in the playoffs. But any sunshine & unicorn dreams of what might be can probably only come to pass if the Commanders can win 7 (or more) of their remaining 10 games. In today’s second question, we ask you how many games the burgundy & gold will win the next 5 weeks. Comments & Results Of course, we invite you to answer the survey questions below, but also feel free to expand on your answers and provide nuance in the comments section. title: NFL Power Rankings Week 9: Commanders’ win over Eagles worth less this year
summary: The Washington Commanders are 2-4-1 and a win over the lowly Eagles moved the needle a little on this odd season…in both ways. Most Power Rankers moved Washington up after Jayden Daniels’ first win in over a year, but the stink of a tank that’s surrounding the Eagles actually lowered the Commanders rankings in the […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 01: Jayden Daniels #5 of the Washington Commanders throws a pass against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Northwest Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are 2-4-1 and a win over the lowly Eagles moved the needle a little on this odd season…in both ways. Most Power Rankers moved Washington up after Jayden Daniels’ first win in over a year, but the stink of a tank that’s surrounding the Eagles actually lowered the Commanders rankings in the NFL.com rankings. Every other ranking stayed the same or improved. The NFC East is still the worst division in the NFL with the New York Giants in the lead in Week 9. This week’s results put the Washington Commanders within two games of the division lead with a rematch against the Giants set for Thursday Night Football next week. The win over the Eagles kept Washington alive in the division, with Philly getting kicked to the basement of the division. The Power Rankers are higher on the Washington Commanders after getting their second win of the season, but there’s only so much you can rise after a 17-point win over a team that’s given up on the season. The Rams are coming to town on Sunday, and this is a “filter game”. The Rams need a win to contend in the NFC West, and the Commanders need a win to maintain any hope for this season before next week’s trade deadline. High: 1 7 Low: 27 Average: 24.1 #17 Walter Football It’s hard to believe that Jayden Daniels just won his first game of the year. I know he was out for a while, but it still feels like he probably should have won a game by now. However, that apparently hadn’t happened. The win over Philadelphia was Washington’s first victory since Week 3 against Seattle, which feels like a million years ago. Last week: 19 #19 Real GM Last week: 21 #21 USA Today (Davis) Despite their multitudinous mistakes this season, no team has turned the ball over fewer times (3) − which is exactly why the Commanders (still) have a legit shot to win the NFC East. Last week: 21 #22 Sports Illustrated (Orr) At this point in the race, Washington is my favorite to wind up winning the NFC East. Last night, the breadcrumbs shown between Jayden Daniels and Antonio Williams leads me to believe there’s just enough of a spark left in this offense to generate a run. Last week: 27 #23 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) Biggest need: Receiver help Like everyone else in the NFC South and NFC East, other than the Eagles, the Commanders should feel like they have a shot to be division champions. The Commanders are flawed, without question, but sit just two games behind the Giants in the division. It’s not like New York is a lock to run away with it. The biggest problem for the Commanders is the loss of receiver Terry McLaurin for the season. It leaves them thin at receiver, and the good news is there are a lot of veterans available at the deadline at various price points. The Commanders should be interested. They also should be interested in improving a secondary that ranks 27th in passing yards allowed. Last week: 24 Full Press Coverage (Glendon) Washington ended its long winless stretch by overcoming an early 10-0 deficit and beating Philadelphia 27-10. Jayden Daniels managed the offense, and the defensive front sacked Tanner McKee five times. One win does not solve the season, but beating a division rival gives the Commanders something to build around. Last week: 27 New York Post (Dunleavy) Last week: 30 Team Rankings Last week: 26 #24 Sporting News (Iyer) The Commanders are going through a cruel twist with Jayden Daniels healthy but key pieces such as Terry McLaurin, Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Laremy Tunsil all on the shelf. The good news is Dan Quinn’s defense is playing well to give him a short reprieve. Last week: 29 NFL Spin Zone (Scataglia) You get the sense that the Washington Commanders could end up making a huge coaching move if they don’t beat the Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Ever since that breakout season in 2024, things have fallen off the rails for Washington, as they have won just six regular season games since the start of the 2025 season, and QB Jayden Daniels has struggled to stay healthy. With that said, Washington getting within one game of the Super Bowl two years ago could mean that more success is on the horizon if the necessary change is made. A non-playoff team trending toward making major changes, Washington should be able to beat Philly on SNF this week. Update: Washington beat Philadelphia on Sunday Night Football in a game they should have won, so I am not sure this really changes things big-picture wise. The Commanders are still an overall bad football team with way more questions than answers. Last week: 29 Fansided (La Canfora) They showed some fight and gumption amid more upheaval on their defense and bringing in new coaches. And it actually worked. Yeah, it was against an Eagles backup, but there was cohesion and connection sorely lacking all season on that side of the ball. Jayden Daniels is not nearly as aggressive as we have seen in the past, however. Last week: 30 FTN Fantasy (Kelley) Sunday’s 81 yards were Treylon Burks ’ most since the sixth game of his career back in 2022. He’s already set a career high in touchdowns (2), and he has his most yards in a season since that rookie campaign. Last week: 25 Pro Football Talk Backward Hat Energy. Last week: 30 Kalshi Last week: 26 Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . #25 ESPN Best in-season trade acquisition ever: WR Calvin Muhammad in 1984 This really is based on one season, as Muhammad played only two years for Washington. The franchise needed help after Art Monk was injured and traded a fourth-round pick to Oakland for the speedy Muhammad. In his 10 games with Washington in 1984, Muhammad caught 42 passes for 729 yards and four touchdowns. He was a key reason why, even without Monk, Washington’s offense remained among the best in the NFL, ranking third in points and ninth in yards. A year later, with a healthy receiving group, Muhammad caught only nine passes and was released before the 1986 season. — John Keim Last week: 29 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) Reality check: Jayden Daniels is getting beat up The Commanders quarterback took a big hit from Nolan Smith on Sunday night that just added to what already has been a black-and-blue season. Daniels has only rushed for 33 yards (all on scrambles) in the last two weeks. If he’s not dynamic on the ground, he’s not the player Washington thought he was as a rookie, but that style of play is taking a toll. Last week: 27 Fox Sports (Vacchiano) Super Bowl odds: +12000 (22nd) The Commanders scored 27 unanswered points to beat a division rival on Sunday night, and ordinarily that would be cause for celebration. But the team they beat is the ghost of the Philadelphia Eagles, and it’s not like the Commanders needed much of an effort to do it. It certainly was a much-needed win for Dan Quinn , who miraculously managed to survive the bye week. He’ll need a lot more of those and a lot more from star QB Jayden Daniels , however, to keep his job after the season. And there are too many injuries and holes in the Commanders’ lineup to expect that. Stat To Know : Washington’s win over Philadelphia on Sunday was Jayden Daniels’ first win as the Commanders’ starter since Oct. 5, 2025. title: CB Trey Amos & WR Antonio Williams: part of Commanders core young talent
summary: The Daily Slop – 3 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Riggo’s Rag Trey […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 1: Trey Amos #23 of the Washington Commanders celebrates after a play during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Northwest Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 3 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Riggo’s Rag Trey Amos gives Commanders a glimpse of something bigger than one win The 2025 second-round pick out of Ole Miss had himself a ballgame, shutting down everything in his path . Amos also should have had his first career interception, but it was called back for a very dubious unnecessary roughness penalty on edge rusher K’Lavon Chaisson. It’s exactly what Washington needed from a player many believe can be a franchise cornerstone. With Amos, it’s all been about availability. His rookie season was cut short due to a fractured fibula, and an ankle injury sustained in his second practice of training camp delayed the defensive back’s 2026 debut until Week 6 at the San Francisco 49ers. But whenever Amos has played, he’s produced. He had six pass deflections as a rookie and two more on Sunday night, while allowing only one reception for seven yards. When he’s been healthy, Amos has shown the potential to be a star. He has the instincts and measurables of a Pro Bowl-level lockdown corner who can provide stability at the position for years. And even though he was out for almost a year, Amos has gotten back into his groove much quicker than anticipated. It’s hard to overstate the difference Amos has made for Washington since his return. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room Note : Unless something changes, this article appears to be unlocked and available to be read from beginning to end Commanders Film Review: Antonio Williams vs Eagles [ Note : The play described in the excerpt below is embedded in the tweet posted in the body of the article ] Commanders head coach Dan Quinn singled out rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams as someone that he thought could step up and play a bigger role after star receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending injury a few weeks ago. Against the Eagles, Williams certainly didn’t disappoint. He caught five passes for 54 yards and could have had plenty more too. The Eagles have a strong secondary but every corner that faced him struggled to stick close. There were a number of key traits that stood out from Williams in this game and I’ll try and cover them all in this post. First, let’s start with the most important thing, his hands. Williams displayed good hands throughout the game, making some tough adjustments to pull in passes that weren’t perfectly accurate. He often did it in a way that made you quickly forget the ball wasn’t perfect too, which I’m sure his quarterback appreciates. This play is a great example of the combination of all of the traits we’ve seen from Williams in this post so far. He shows good speed, good route running, and great hands. Williams begins this play as the outside receiver to the right of the formation, but he’s aligned tight to the formation. Initially, he has cornerback Quinyon Mitchell lined up opposite him, but that soon changes. The Commanders motion tight end Chig Okonkwo outside of Williams, making Williams the slot receiver. The Eagles react by bumping Mitchell outside over Okonkwo, while the safety rotates down from deep to cover Williams. Commanders rookie WR Antonio Williams had a strong outing against the Eagles on Sunday. I broke down his performance: https://t.co/AHm0t9m2Gz pic.twitter.com/oZj7XEuvOm — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 3, 2026 That’s a strong matchup for the Commanders and one Williams takes full advantage of. Williams runs a double move against the safety. He initially angles his route outside and gets all the way to the edge of the numbers as he fully sells his fake break outside. This commitment to the fake forces the safety to bite on it, which enables Williams to burst past him. Williams opens up a gap of five yards on the safety very quickly and Daniels pulls the trigger. His throw is a little lofty and Williams has to slow down as he tracks the ball in the air. But he makes a nice adjustment to work back to the ball, jumping up to grab the ball before the safety could get there. He bobbles the pass slightly but manages to secure the ball as the safety lands a big hit, completing the 30-yard gain. It was an impressive outing from the rookie receiver and one that means he now leads the Commanders receivers with 259 receiving yards from 23 catches so far this season. If he continues to play this well, those numbers should only grow. He’s definitely worthy of a bigger role and more targets within the offense, especially without McLaurin. He’s doing a great job on the outside as the Z receiver but he’s also very capable of playing the same role as Diggs in the slot. I wonder if we’ll see him shift inside a little more often in key situations as the season progresses, trusting him to make some of those critical plays in big spots that Diggs is making. Diggs has been a great signing so far, but Williams is the future, so I wonder if we’ll see a passing of the torch at some point. For now though, with Burks playing McLaurin’s X receiver role, Williams can claim the Z receiver role as his own and he should only become an increasingly larger part of the offense going forward. Antonio Williams Week 8 vs. Eagles: 50 SNAPS (83%) | 7 TGT | 5 REC | 54 YDS | 30 LNG Played more snaps than any other #Commanders pass catcher, ahead of Treylon Burks (40) and Stefon Diggs (39). Turned that into team highs in targets and catches, with his 5 grabs a career best.… pic.twitter.com/qNUV9S4P44 — Johnathan (@DCuratedSports) November 2, 2026 More from Sports Illustrated: Snap Judgment: Williams ( 50 snaps – 83% ) led the receivers in playing time, ahead of Burks (40 snaps – 67%) and Diggs (39 snaps – 65%). I’d keep him at the front of this rotation. Williams caught three passes for 20 yards on Washington’s 89-yard touchdown drive. His five-yard catch on third-and-4 kept the possession alive, and a 10-yard reception on second-and-10 moved the chains again. In the fourth quarter, his 30-yard catch was the biggest gain on the drive that pushed Washington’s lead to 19-10. Sports Illustrated Five Sacks Without Three DTs Washington’s defensive front supplied the answer it needed most. Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw and Jer’Zhan Newton were all unavailable, but the Commanders sacked Tanner McKee five times and held Saquon Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries. Charles Omenihu returned with a sack, three quarterback hits and a fumble recovery. Quinn said Monday the rush looked more coordinated and connected after the staff made it a focus during the bye. With Payne’s foot injury reportedly ending his season, Washington will need that work to hold up beyond one game. title: NFL Week 9 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips and trade deadline news
summary: What now for the Ravens without Lamar Jackson? What are people around the NFL saying about Justin Herbert's struggles? And what's the latest on the looming trade deadline?
full_text:
It's Week 9 of the  2026 NFL season , which means two things. First, we're about to hit midseason. Second, the trade deadline is right around the corner. And insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 The Ravens are in a tough spot, dropping to 4-4 and losing not only QB1 Lamar Jackson but also QB2 Tyler Huntley to injuries. What's next for Baltimore? Will the Ravens focus their attention on 2027 or still try to turn things around this season in a tight AFC North? Out west, what's going on with Justin Herbert ? The Chargers obviously have big problems at 0-7, and Herbert hasn't played well. What are we hearing on his struggles?

 And what about trade buzz? What's the latest around the league? Which teams could be active, and which players could be on the move before the Tuesday deadline? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 9.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Next steps for the Ravens 
 Buzz on Herbert's struggles 
 Deadline intel | Fantasy advice 
 More notes and nuggets 

 
 

 What's your sense on where the Ravens go from here? 
 Graziano: Baltimore isn't a throw-in-the-towel type of organization. My sense is that the Ravens will work to solve the problem and will be open to a number of ideas at quarterback with Lamar Jackson  ( thumb ) and Tyler Huntley  (toe) out. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano has been announced as their starter  for  Thursday night  against Jacksonville, but if, for example, the Cardinals are done with Jacoby Brissett , Baltimore would be a team I'd expect to at least look into bringing in Brissett for Week 10 on.

 

 Fowler: In the short term, there are several players with lower-cost contracts if the Ravens choose to pursue them. Brissett was with Ravens quarterbacks coach Isaiah Woolfork last season in Arizona. Bears backup Tyson Bagent has familiarity with Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. And some conversations I had early this week made me think the Colts' Daniel Jones is at least on the radar. Baltimore could essentially sign him without spending a lot because of his struggles. Jones' $5.5 million base salary is tradable, and his 2027 guarantees don't trigger until the offseason. He's roughly 11 months post-Achilles tear , so perhaps his play improves.

 Graziano: My bigger question is a long-term one involving Jackson's future with the franchise . I believed going into this season that the most important big-picture goal the Ravens had was to get to next offseason with Jackson feeling good about signing an extension that keeps him in Baltimore for years to come. Now that it is apparent that the season isn't going the way he or they hoped, my focus is trying to figure out what comes next for the Ravens and Jackson.

 Fowler: Assuming Jackson is done for the season, his $84 million cap hit in 2027 is an albatross for Baltimore, which could give Baltimore justifiable hesitance about giving him a top-of-the-market extension because of durability concerns. Thursday will mark Jackson's fourth missed game this season -- the fourth time in six seasons he has missed four or more games.

 I'm pumping the brakes on the "Lamar played his last down in Baltimore" talk for now. He's under contract in 2027. But the Ravens must at least now consider life without him. They had a chance to extend him last offseason, and it didn't happen -- either because he didn't want to sign or they didn't make him an irresistible offer. Both sides eventually need to figure out what they want out of their immediate future together.

 Graziano: Yeah, if they get to next spring and still can't get a deal done, they are simply going to have to consider trading him. The no-franchise tag clause in his contract gives him incredible leverage and means he has no reason to sign an extension with Baltimore that he doesn't absolutely love. If nothing happens before March 2028, Jackson would be an unrestricted free agent with at least two MVP awards on his résumé. And the no-trade clause means he could decide his team.

 Jackson didn't get the fully guaranteed deal he was looking for the last time he was up for an extension, but he got an awful lot  of money. And the reason he got those clauses in his contract is because he wants to have control over where he finishes his career.

 Fowler: The no-franchise tag and no-trade clauses make for a fascinating dynamic. He entered the season with considerable leverage, which he mostly still has. But the sheen is wearing off slightly. He'll be 30 in January, which isn't a big deal for quarterbacks but is at least a consideration in terms of his rushing ability.

 

 But if Baltimore were to listen, his trade market should look more robust than it did a few years ago when he was on the franchise tag and whispers of collusion persisted . Whether Baltimore entertains a deal is still a big "if." But come March, Jackson will be 12 months from the chance to enter true free agency, so the clock is ticking.

 

 
 What's the buzz around the league on Justin Herbert 's struggles? 
 Fowler: League evaluators typically support Herbert more than the media does, but it has been harder to defend him this season. He looks hesitant and is seeing the field poorly. "He doesn't seem comfortable in the offense," an AFC exec said. "I don't know that it's a great schematic fit for his talents. He's throwing a lot of picks where he simply isn't seeing defenders. I don't know how it gets better."

 Coaches are more inclined to give him grace. "The entire team has been devastated around him," said an NFL defensive coach who recently prepared for him. "The O-line is a mess, the running game is bad, and the skill guys aren't very good. It's nearly impossible to have success with that setup."

 Herbert has proof of concept -- six seasons of quality quarterback play, some of it at quite a high level -- but is in the kind of funk that makes you wonder whether this type of downturn was inevitable, no matter how much Jim Harbaugh tried to motivate him publicly or privately.

 Graziano: I have heard similar things about him being an awkward fit for what Mike McDaniel wants his quarterback to do, specifically diagnosing the defense at the line of scrimmage and adjusting accordingly. Oddly, McDaniel's success in Miami came because of his ability to scheme around Tua Tagovailoa 's deficiencies, but one thing Tagovailoa could do was make the right decisions when he got to the line. If that's not something that comes as easily to Herbert, that might be showing up.

 The question is whether this becomes a completely lost season or if there's some way for Herbert to get to the end of it feeling better about what lies ahead. Considering the Chargers' 0-7 record, the former feels more likely.

 

 Fowler: What's amazing is the Chargers could have used the Week 7 bye to improve their offense. But Harbaugh made zero changes . It's almost as if the Chargers felt that they could roll the ball out and magically turn things around. They probably should have received more heat for not tweaking much of anything.

 McDaniel did tweak Herbert's mechanics in the offseason, having him use a weighted, bright green ball to promote a quicker release. Part of me wonders whether the changes affected his confidence. Or maybe he simply never recovered from that ugly playoff loss to New England last season, when he was sacked six times and Los Angeles scored three points. He has taken 248 sacks in six-plus years. Those hits add up.

 Graziano: No doubt. I've been asking teams if they have a sense of what the Chargers are going to do ahead of the trade deadline, and a couple told me over the weekend that they don't get the sense that Los Angeles is eager to enter teardown mode. At least entering Sunday, I wasn't getting the impression that the Chargers were open to trading players to inquiring…

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline: Players to watch, buzz and goals for all 32 teams
summary: We outlined deadline plans for all 32 teams, including who could be dealt before 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday. Here's what you need to know.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET. We have already had a fair share of trades made this season , but could more be on the horizon? Will the Colts continue to trade players away -- such as  Jonathan Taylor -- and build draft capital for the future? Will the Chiefs finally find a trade for a dependable wide receiver for QB  Patrick Mahomes ? How will the Eagles and Ravens approach things without their QB1s? Let's take a 32-team look at what to expect over the next week.

 First, we checked where each team stands through Week 8 using ESPN's Football Power Index projections. Then, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to name each team's trade deadline goal. Who is staying put, and who is open for business? Next, NFL insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano leaned on their reporting to predict which players on every team could be on the move. Finally, analysts Aaron Schatz and Seth Walder picked one player each team should try to acquire.

 Here's everything you need to know heading into the deadline.

 
 Jump to: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 

 Arizona Cardinals (3-5) 
 Chance to make playoffs: 1.1% 
 Projected first-round draft slot: No. 8

 What is the deadline goal?  Keep building for the future. That seems to be the M.O. of another M.O. -- Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort. He's in Year 4 of a three-year rebuild that hasn't blossomed yet. Moving players who are unhappy or veterans for draft capital is not out of the question after trading Marvin Harrison Jr . to the Texans last month. The Cardinals want to build toward the future, especially for next season when they will likely have to address the quarterback position again.  -- Josh Weinfuss 

 

 Who could be on the move? Edge  Josh Sweat . The Cardinals have received trade interest on Sweat, who would be a natural fit in Dallas. Word is he wants a new deal, which could be a hurdle. Safety Budda Baker and quarterback Jacoby Brissett  are also names to watch. -- Fowler 

 Who should they target? Vikings WR Tai Felton . Felton has only six receptions in a season and a half in the NFL, but the Cardinals could try to find the skills that made him a third-round pick in 2025. They need young receiving talent behind Michael Wilson . -- Schatz 

 
 

 

 Atlanta Falcons (3-5) 
 Chance to make playoffs: 7.9% 
 Projected first-round draft slot: No. 10

 What is the deadline goal? Don't give up valuable future assets. New Falcons general manager Ian Cunningham hated that the team had only five draft picks in 2026. He vowed that the franchise would never have that few again. Cunningham wants to build the Falcons through the draft. So, do not expect him to gamble away picks unless there's a no-brainer offer out there. The Falcons are unlikely to be active with their 3-5 record, because they still believe they can win the NFC South. They just won't give up important draft capital to do it. -- Marc Raimondi 

 Who could be on the move? Safety  Jessie Bates III . To be clear ... I do not believe the Falcons are trying to trade Bates, and I would be surprised if they did. But he's an excellent player in the final year of his contract, and there are teams out there that would like to know whether they can get him. I believe it would take a huge offer. -- Graziano 

 Who should they target? Texans WR Kayshon Boutte . This would be the second time Boutte has been traded this season, after the Patriots dealt him to Houston in August. But that was before the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr . (and before the Texans got out to a 2-5 start). The Falcons are 3-5 but not out of the race in the NFC South, so adding a cheap player who could help is not out of the question, and Boutte is exactly that. -- Walder 

 
 

 

 Baltimore Ravens (4-4) 
 Chance to make playoffs: 7.2% 
 Projected first-round draft slot: No. 11

 What is the deadline goal? Trade for a QB or listen to offers. With injured QB Lamar Jackson (right thumb) out for at least four games and perhaps the season, the Ravens have to decide whether they want to add a quarterback to try to keep the season afloat or trade their own players for capital. Running back Derrick Henry could be a target for a championship contender. But it wouldn't be surprising if the Ravens stand pat. -- Jamison Hensley 

 Who could be on the move?  Wide receiver  Rashod Bateman . Several teams are looking for receiver help, and Bateman would have value, should Baltimore entertain it. He's not a focal point in the offense and would probably welcome the chance to be more of one elsewhere. -- Fowler 

 

 Who should they target? Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett . The injury to Jackson completely changes the Ravens' needs. They're still in the playoff race and need a quarterback with more experience than undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano . Brissett might have lost his job to  Gardner Minshew II  on Sunday, but he still ranks 24th among qualified quarterbacks with a 48.9 QBR. That's not good, but that's not undrafted rookie level, either. -- Schatz 

 
 

 

 Buffalo Bills (6-1) 
 Chance to make playoffs: 99.1% 
 Projected first-round draft slot: No. 31

 What is the deadline goal? Be aggressive with secondary options. With the way the Bills' offense is playing, a league-average defense should be enough to make them serious contenders. Now, the salary cap situation complicates things. With the roster as is, the Bills have a little less than $4 million to spend. But they should be in the market for an extra safety or nickel corner to fortify a weakness and alleviate some of the concerns caused by injuries and early-season mistakes. -- Nick Suss 

 Who could be on the move? Wide receiver  Keon Coleman . Coleman has played well enough to stay in Buffalo's short-term and maybe long-term plans. But I'm not sure this team will trade anyone . So consider this pure speculation that Coleman could be attractive enough to a receiver-needy team to bring back the defensive help Buffalo seeks. -- Graziano 

 Who should they target? Buccaneers edge Yaya Diaby . He would provide a jolt of pass rush to a defense that badly needs it. Buffalo ranks 26th in pass rush win rate, but Diaby's win rate at edge is in the 97th percentile this season, and he has 3.0 sacks. The Bills are in a tight cap situation, but Diaby is a pending free agent. -- Walder 

 
 

 

 Carolina Panthers (3-4) 
 Chance to make playoffs: 23.6% 
 Projected first-round draft slot: No. 13

 What is the deadline goal?  Find cost-effective help, if possible. The Panthers are in an awkward spot after losing two consecutive games and firing defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero last week. But while they are under .500, they're still leading the NFC South entering Week 9. Carolina needs help at cornerback and on the offensive line. Coach Dave Canales said they're open to improving the roster with a trade, but they'll need to use some salary cap gymnastics (they have less than $1 million in cap space) to make that happen. -- Mike Kaye 

 

 Who could be on the move? Tight end  Ja'Tavion Sanders . Sanders has fallen out of favor in Carolina and was a healthy scratch last Thursday night in Green Bay. Sanders doesn't hold significant value, but perhaps a Day 3 pick swap gets this done. -- Fowler 

 Who should they target? Jets S  Andre Cisco . New York can send a veteran free safety to the contending Panthers in exchange for youth at the position. This would also allow sixth-round rookie Zakee Wheatley more time to develop and improve the Panthers' pass defense, which ranks 21st in DVOA against deep passes. -- Schatz 

 
 

 

 Chicago Bears (6-2) 
 Chance to make playoffs: 90.4% 
 Projected first-round draft slot: No pick

 What is the deadline goal?  All-in. The Bears showed they are trying to win a Super Bowl when they sent two first-round picks to the Titans for…

title: Fantasy football D/ST outlook for Weeks 9-12: Fire up Texans, and how 'bout them Cowboys?
summary: Looking for the right D/ST units to stream over the next four weeks? Here's what you need to know.
full_text:
Every four weeks in this space, the D/ST Road Map helps fantasy managers navigate a streaming defense strategy through the upcoming month's games.

 If streaming team defense/special teams is a new concept to you, consider the numbers so far in 2026: The top five D/STs selected on average in the preseason have averaged 6.7 fantasy points. To put that into perspective, D/STs that have faced the five offenses that have surrendered the most points have averaged 9.4.

 With this being the peak of the bye weeks -- "bye-mageddon" (six teams on bye) arrives in Week 11 -- every manager is surely in need of at least a one-week plug-in. To help you navigate these important weeks just ahead of the fantasy playoffs, what follows is my updated D/ST Road Map for Weeks 9-12, spanning the remainder of November.

 Top 10 offenses to exploit 
 

 Here are the 10 offenses that, over the past five weeks, have been the best against which to stream D/STs:

 1. Los Angeles Chargers : added 6.6 fantasy points to a D/ST's score on average 
2. Minnesota Vikings : +4.8 
3. Carolina Panthers : +4.4 
4. Indianapolis Colts : +4.1 
5. Baltimore Ravens : +3.8 
6. Cleveland Browns : +3.5 
7. Seattle Seahawks : +3.1 
8. Philadelphia Eagles : +2.4 
9. Tennessee Titans : +2.2 
10. Arizona Cardinals : +1.9

 It might be puzzling to see the Vikings, tied for the league's best record (6-1) and fifth in point differential (+47), high on the list, but much more of the credit for their hot start should be attributed to their outstanding defense. Offensively speaking, the Vikings are a bottom-10 team in points scored and total yards per game, and they have an above-average sack rate. Avoid their defense with your skill-position players, but have little fear of streaming your defense against Kyler Murray and company.

 The New York Jets (+1.5), tied for the second-most sacks in the league, narrowly missed the cutoff but are another worthy streaming target.

 Top 10 offenses to avoid 
 1. Detroit Lions : subtracted 6.4 points from a D/ST's score on average 
2. Houston Texans : minus-4.0 
3. Buffalo Bills : minus-4.0 
4. Cincinnati Bengals : minus-3.8 
5. Las Vegas Raiders : minus-3.8 
6. New England Patriots : minus-3.4 
7. Kansas City Chiefs : minus-3.3 
8. Jacksonville Jaguars : minus-2.6 
9. Denver Broncos : minus-2.4 
10. Dallas Cowboys : minus-2.0

 The surprising Raiders, the No. 2 offense against which to stream entering the season, enter the list after scoring 30-plus points for the second time in three weeks. All this despite 38-year-old Kirk Cousins doing a fine job as their starting quarterback, and despite their benching their starting running back, Ashton Jeanty , for the start of their Week 8 win. Should the Raiders surrender to the occasional calls for rookie Fernando Mendoza to take over for Cousins, this stance will almost assuredly change, but for now, temper your expectations from D/STs that face the Raiders.

 The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (minus-1.7), once an offense against which to stream while Baker Mayfield was sidelined with a dislocated thumb, narrowly missed the cutoff.

 The D/ST to lock in for November: Texans 
 

 You couldn't ask for a softer schedule than what the Texans face. In Week 9, they visit the reeling, 0-7 Chargers. In Week 10, they've got a road game against the most sack-prone team in the Browns. In Week 11, they return home to host the rebuilding Colts. And in Week 12, they'll get another home game, this time against a Ravens team that lost its top two quarterbacks to injuries Sunday.

 The Texans were heavily drafted in the preseason, but as things stand they're available in more than one-third of ESPN leagues. If they're out there in yours, snatch them up for what's a full November of must-start matchups.

 The other D/ST to lock in for November: Cowboys 
 They're one of the two more widely available, exiting Week 8 still out there in more than 80% of ESPN leagues. The Cowboys do have one middling-to-tough D/ST matchup, a Week 10 home game against the San Francisco 49ers , but other than that should be in your lineups for the other three. Those include a road game against the Colts and home games against the low-scoring Titans and injury-riddled Eagles.

 D/ST week-by-week Road Map 
 Here's a handy guide for streaming the position on a weekly basis, and we'll also have an updated version to help steer you through Weeks 13-17. All D/STs are ranked in my order of preference, regardless of roster rate in ESPN leagues, so that you won't miss out on a higher quality defense if it becomes available in yours.
